locations.name: Golden Krone Hotel, Bistritz
locations.description: Thoroughly old-fashioned inn with a wide archway to an inn-yard; guests' room upstairs; bench outside the door where locals sit.
features: inn-yard with oleander and orange trees in green tubs
locations.atmosphere: quaint but fearful; staff cross themselves
locations.quote: thoroughly old-fashioned, for of course I wanted to see all I could of the ways of the country

locations.name: Bistritz
locations.description: Old frontier town near the Borgo Pass with a stormy history: five great fires fifty years earlier, and a three-week siege in the early seventeenth century that killed 13,000.
locations.quote: it has had a very stormy existence, and it certainly shows marks of it

locations.name: Hotel Royale, Klausenburgh
locations.description: Comfortable hotel where Harker sups on paprika hendl and breakfasts on mamaliga and impletata.
locations.atmosphere: warm but troubled by howling dog
locations.quote: I stopped for the night at the Hotel Royale

locations.name: Mittel Land road
locations.description: Rugged road through green swelling hills, orchards in blossom, steep hills crowned with farmhouses with blank gable ends, pine woods running down like tongues of flame.
locations.atmosphere: idyllic then threatening as dusk falls
locations.quote: a bewildering mass of fruit blossom—apple, plum, pear, cherry

locations.name: Carpathian mountains vista
locations.description: Mighty forested slopes, blue and purple shadowed peaks, jagged crags, snowy summits glowing pink at sunset, waterfalls glimpsed in rifts; the peak called Isten szek, God's seat.
locations.quote: the snowy mountain-top still held the sunset, and seemed to glow out with a delicate cool pink

locations.name: Borgo Pass
locations.description: Cleft in the hills where mountains frown down on both sides; sandy white road; the eastern side opens under rolling thundercloud.
locations.quote: the mountains seemed to come nearer to us on each side and to frown down upon us

locations.name: Wooded side road and stone-pile glade
locations.description: Narrow road turning sharply right, trees arching into a tunnel, frowning rocks, powdery snow; blue flame spots where the driver stacks stones.
locations.quote: Soon we were hemmed in with trees, which in places arched right over the roadway till we passed as through a tunnel

locations.name: Castle Dracula courtyard (arrival)
locations.description: Courtyard of a vast ruined castle with tall black windows and broken jagged battlements against the moonlit sky.
locations.quote: whose broken battlements showed a jagged line against the moonlit sky

locations.name: Castle courtyard
locations.description: Large courtyard with several dark ways leading from it under great round arches.
locations.quote: several dark ways led from it under great round arches

locations.name: Great door
locations.description: Old door studded with large iron nails in a projecting doorway of massive worn carved stone; no bell or knocker; secured with chains, bolts and a key.
locations.quote: a great door, old and studded with large iron nails, and set in a projecting doorway of massive stone

locations.name: Entry passage and winding stair
locations.description: Stone passage, great winding stair and another passage where footsteps ring on stone floor.
locations.quote: up a great winding stair, and along another great passage, on whose stone floor our steps rang heavily

locations.name: Dining room
locations.description: Well-lit room with table set for supper and a mighty hearth with a great log fire; later laid with breakfast with coffee kept hot on the hearth.
locations.quote: a table was spread for supper, and on whose mighty hearth a great fire of logs, freshly replenished, flamed and flared

locations.name: Octagonal room
locations.description: Small octagonal room between the dining room and the bedroom, lit by a single lamp, apparently without any window.
locations.quote: a small octagonal room lit by a single lamp, and seemingly without a window of any sort

locations.name: Harker's bedroom
locations.description: Great bedroom with log fire, centuries-old costly hangings; window opens to the courtyard; no mirror.
locations.quote: the hangings of my bed are of the costliest and most beautiful fabrics

locations.name: Library
locations.description: Room full of English books and periodicals; a central table covered with magazines; lamps lit at dusk; sofa; atlas.
features: London Directory, Red and Blue books, Whitaker's Almanac, Army and Navy Lists, Law List
locations.quote: a vast number of English books, whole shelves full of them

locations.name: Locked door opposite Harker's door
locations.description: A door Harker tries and finds locked.
locations.quote: The door opposite mine I tried, but found it locked.

locations.name: South room at the precipice
locations.description: Room off the stairs facing south, the castle on the very edge of a precipice with a drop of a thousand feet and a sea of green tree-tops with silver rivers in gorges.
features: view of forest and river gorges
locations.quote: A stone falling from the window would fall a thousand feet without touching anything!

locations.name: Carfax (described)
locations.description: Estate at Purfleet with a high old stone wall, rusted oak and iron gates, twenty acres, dark pond fed by springs, large straggling house of all periods including a thick-walled keep with a few high barred windows, next to an old chapel; near a private lunatic asylum.
features: stone keep with barred high windows
locations.quote: The estate is called Carfax, no doubt a corruption of the old Quatre Face

locations.name: Castle stairs and corridors
locations.description: Stone stairs and passages with many locked doors; a stairway leading up to a south-looking window.
locations.quote: I rushed up and down the stairs, trying every door and peering out of every window I could find

locations.name: South-looking stairway window
locations.description: Tall, deep, stone-mullioned window, weather-worn, no casement; below and to the left is the Count's window; the castle wall falls to an abyss.
locations.quote: The window at which I stood was tall and deep, stone-mullioned, and though weatherworn, was still complete

locations.name: Hall at the great door
locations.description: Entry hall; bolts easy to draw, chains unhooked, door locked with no key; small dusty rooms nearby with moth-eaten furniture.
locations.quote: I found I could pull back the bolts easily enough and unhook the great chains; but the door was locked

locations.name: Sagging door at the top of the stairway
locations.description: A heavy door whose fallen hinges leave it resting on the floor; opened by forcing.
locations.quote: the hinges had fallen somewhat, and the heavy door rested on the floor

locations.name: The ladies' rooms (south wing)
locations.description: Suite one storey down and further right; end room windows face west and south over precipices; diamond panes, curtainless windows, dust, moth; comfortable furniture, a little oak table, a great couch.
features: view west to jagged mountains with mountain ash and thorn
locations.quote: the yellow moonlight, flooding in through the diamond panes, enabled one to see even colours

locations.name: Castle rock and precipice
locations.description: Castle built on the corner of a great rock, impregnable on three sides, with large windows placed where sling, bow or culverin cannot reach.
locations.quote: The castle was built on the corner of a great rock, so that on three sides it was quite impregnable

locations.name: Harker's bedroom (sanctuary)
locations.description: Room with wardrobe, portmanteau, window barred and looking onto the courtyard.
locations.quote: it is now a sort of sanctuary

locations.name: South-wing door
locations.description: Door at the top of the stairway, now closed, splintered at the jamb and fastened from inside.
locations.quote: part of the woodwork was splintered

locations.name: Courtyard with Szgany camp
locations.description: Courtyard where gipsies encamp and later great boxes are stacked in a heap in a corner; gateway opposite Harker's window; a high tower.
locations.quote: great, square boxes, with handles of thick rope

locations.name: Window ledge on the south side
locations.description: Narrow ledge of big, roughly cut stones with the mortar washed away between them, running round the building above the abyss.
locations.quote: the narrow ledge of stone which runs around the building on this side

locations.name: The Count's room
locations.description: Barely furnished, dusty, same style as the south rooms, window with sash; heap of gold of many nations; heavy door in a corner leading to a stone passage; key not found.
features: heap of old gold (Roman, British, Austrian, Hungarian, Greek, Turkish)
locations.quote: a great heap of gold in one corner—gold of all kinds, Roman, and British, and Austrian, and Hungarian, and Greek and Turkish money

locations.name: Circular stair and tunnel passage
locations.description: Steep circular stairway lit only by loopholes in heavy masonry, leading to a dark tunnel-like passage with the smell of newly turned earth.
locations.quote: the odour of old earth newly turned

locations.name: Ruined chapel
locations.description: Old chapel used as graveyard; roof broken; steps in two places down to vaults; ground freshly dug; wooden boxes filled with earth.
features: fragments of old coffins and dust
locations.quote: an old, ruined chapel, which had evidently been used as a graveyard

locations.name: Third vault
locations.description: Vault where the Count's earth-box lies with pierced lid beside it.
features: great box on newly dug earth
locations.quote: By the side of the box was its cover, pierced with holes here and there.

locations.name: Hall door and entrance hall
locations.description: Entry with ponderous bolts and chains; door unlocked in the Count's pretence, then locked.
locations.quote: the great bolts clanged and echoed through the hall

locations.name: 17, Chatham Street
locations.description: Lucy Westenra's London town house, where she and her mother receive callers; suitors find Lucy alone in the room.
features: a looking glass (Lucy studies her face in it)
a fireplace (Lucy recalls sitting by the fire undressing with Mina)
locations.quote: 17, Chatham Street

locations.name: Seward's lunatic asylum
locations.description: An immense private lunatic asylum under Dr. Seward's sole care, with wards of patients he visits.
locations.quote: he has an immense lunatic asylum all under his own care

locations.name: Quincey's camp-fire dinner (the Korea)
locations.description: Planned private dinner where Quincey and Seward will drink to Arthur; Seward and Quincey were pals 'at the Korea'.
locations.quote: There will only be one other, our old pal at the Korea, Jack Seward.

locations.name: The Crescent, Whitby
locations.description: Terrace of rooms where the Westenras and Mina lodge.
locations.quote: we drove up to the house at the Crescent in which they have rooms

locations.name: Whitby town and Esk valley
locations.description: Deep green steep valley with the small River Esk, a great viaduct on high piers, and old red-roofed houses piled up like Nuremberg.
locations.quote: The houses of the old town are all red-roofed, and seem piled up one over the other anyhow

locations.name: Whitby Abbey ruin
locations.description: Immense noble ruin above the town, sacked by the Danes, with a legend of a white lady at a window.
locations.quote: there is a legend that a white lady is seen in one of the windows

locations.name: St. Mary's churchyard (East Cliff)
locations.description: Large graveyard of tombstones on a steep cliff above the harbour; erosion has collapsed graves, with stonework hanging over the sandy path far below. Walks with seats run through it.
features: slab-stone seat over the Canon grave near cliff edge
collapsed bank with exposed grave stonework
old house next to the abbey
locations.atmosphere: peaceful by day, ominous in grey weather
locations.quote: part of the stonework of the graves stretches out over the sandy pathway far below

locations.name: The 199 steps (church stairs)
locations.description: Hundreds of steps winding in a delicate gentle curve from town to church, so shallow a horse could walk them (number not stated).
locations.quote: there are hundreds of them—I do not know how many—and they wind up in a delicate curve

locations.name: Whitby harbour
locations.description: Long granite wall with a curved end and lighthouse on the far side, a heavy sea-wall outside; a crooked elbow pier with lighthouse on the near side; narrow opening between the piers, tidal sand flats at low water.
features: reef with bell buoy half a mile out
locations.quote: Between the two piers there is a narrow opening into the harbour, which then suddenly widens.

locations.name: Renfield's cell
locations.description: Asylum room with a window where he puts sugar to attract flies, a pillow, boxes of spiders.
features: sash window that opens an inch
corridor door guarded by an attendant
locations.quote: He was spreading out his sugar, which he had saved, in the window

locations.name: Whitby East Cliff churchyard
locations.description: Cliff-top graveyard commanding sea views; flat thruff-stones project over the lane where the cliff has fallen away; walk along the cliff; seat fixed on a tombstone.
features: flat tombstones overhanging the lane to East Pier
locations.quote: some of the flat tombstones... actually project over where the sustaining cliff has fallen away

locations.name: Tate Hill Pier
locations.description: Small pier in the south-east corner of the harbour under the East Cliff, with an accumulation of sand and gravel; the Demeter drives onto it.
locations.quote: pitched herself on that accumulation of sand and gravel washed by many tides and many storms

locations.name: Whitby harbour piers
locations.description: Two piers with lanterned lighthouses, iron stanchions, narrow mouth, East Pier and West Pier; Drawbridge links West Cliff.
locations.quote: the lanthorns of the lighthouses which rise from the end of either pier

locations.name: The Demeter (schooner)
locations.description: Russian schooner from Varna, crew of five hands plus captain; cargo of silver sand ballast and great wooden boxes of mould.
locations.quote: the schooner is a Russian from Varna, and is called the Demeter

locations.name: Whitby mortuary
locations.description: Place where the dead steersman is taken to await inquest.
locations.quote: placed in the mortuary to await inquest

locations.name: Robin Hood's Bay inn
locations.description: Sweet old-fashioned inn with a bow-window right over the seaweed-covered rocks of the strand.
locations.quote: a sweet little old-fashioned inn, with a bow-window right over the seaweed-covered rocks of the strand

locations.name: Mina and Lucy's bedroom, the Crescent
locations.description: Shared room with two beds, a lockable door, a window with a blind and a sill that opens to the street.
locations.quote: I have taken care that the door is locked and the window securely fastened.

locations.name: Whitby at night (West Cliff to East Cliff route)
locations.description: Empty streets: the Crescent, North Terrace, West Cliff, steep steps to the pier, fish-market, bridge to the East Cliff, endless steps to the abbey, wynds (steep closes).
locations.quote: a bright full moon, with heavy black, driving clouds, which threw the whole scene into a fleeting diorama of light and shade

locations.name: East Cliff churchyard seat
locations.description: Favourite seat fixed on a flat stone slab; view over harbour; St. Mary's church and abbey behind.
locations.quote: there, on our favourite seat, the silver light of the moon struck a half-reclining figure, snowy white.

locations.name: Casino Terrace and Mulgrave Woods
locations.description: Promenade with music (Spohr, Mackenzie); woods reached by cliff path and road with a gate.
locations.quote: we strolled in the Casino Terrace, and heard some good music by Spohr and Mackenzie

locations.name: Carfax
locations.description: Deserted house near Purfleet beside the asylum behind a high wall; includes a partially ruined ancient chapel marked 'A' with an ironbound oak door; main hall holds keys.
locations.quote: the ancient chapel of the mansion

locations.name: Asylum padded room
locations.description: Padded cell where Renfield is chained to the wall in a strait-waistcoat.
locations.quote: he's chained to the wall in the padded room

locations.name: Buda-Pesth Hospital of St. Joseph and Ste. Mary
locations.description: Convent hospital with a sanatorium in the hills where Jonathan recovers.
locations.quote: Hospital of St. Joseph and Ste. Mary, Buda-Pesth

locations.name: Hospital of St. Joseph and Ste. Mary, Buda-Pesth
locations.description: A convent hospital run by sisters, with a Superior and a chaplain of the English mission church. Jonathan lies propped on pillows in a bed by a window.
locations.quote: I am now sitting by his bedside, where I can see his face while he sleeps.

locations.name: Renfield's padded room
locations.description: Padded cell in Seward's asylum; the door edge between ridges of padding bears Renfield's nail-mark tally of caught flies.
locations.quote: making nail-marks on the edge of the door between the ridges of padding

locations.name: Renfield's own room
locations.description: A normal asylum room with a window that opens; sugar spread on the sill attracts flies, kept in a box.
locations.quote: He has the sugar of his tea spread out on the window-sill

locations.name: Grounds of the deserted house and old chapel door
locations.description: Overgrown grounds next to the asylum; the old chapel door is where Renfield presses himself.
locations.quote: pressed against the old chapel door

locations.name: Seward's asylum exterior and gate
locations.description: Cold stone building seen at a gate with a smoky London sunset behind it.
locations.atmosphere: grim contrast of lurid sunset and desolate institution
locations.quote: all the grim sternness of my own cold stone building, with its wealth of breathing misery

locations.name: Hillingham, Lucy's bedroom
locations.description: Lucy's room with a window where scratching/flapping is heard; a clock strikes twelve.
locations.quote: when the clock struck twelve it waked me from a doze

locations.name: Hillingham boudoir
locations.description: Lucy's private sitting room with a stiff window whose cord breaks.
locations.quote: We went into her boudoir

locations.name: Liverpool Street station
locations.description: London railway terminus where Seward meets Van Helsing.
locations.quote: when we met at Liverpool Street

locations.name: Adjoining room at Hillingham
locations.description: Cozy room with a fire and a sofa, next to Lucy's, connected by open doors.
locations.quote: a room next her own, where a cozy fire was burning

locations.name: Hillingham hall and dining-room
locations.description: Entrance hall with hall-door; dining-room holds the brandy decanter and port.
locations.quote: I flew to the dining-room, and returned with the decanter.

locations.name: Hillingham morning room and boudoir
locations.description: Rooms where Mrs. Westenra breakfasts early.
locations.quote: coming out of the morning room

locations.name: Hillingham dining-room
locations.description: Room with a table, a sideboard bearing medicine bottles and a sherry decanter.
locations.quote: looking on the sideboard, I found that the bottle which mother's doctor uses for her

locations.name: Hillingham grounds and shrubbery
locations.description: Garden beneath the window with shrubbery from which a deep fierce howl is heard.
locations.quote: outside in the shrubbery I heard a sort of howl like a dog's

locations.name: Zoological Gardens wolf section
locations.description: Section with cages for wolves, jackals, hyenas; cottage behind the elephant-house; monkey-house.
locations.quote: Thomas Bilder lives in one of the cottages in the enclosure behind the elephant-house

locations.name: Seward's study
locations.description: Superintendent's study with table, books and carpet.
features: safe with the second copy of the manuscript
locations.quote: I was engaged after dinner in my study posting up my books

locations.name: Lucy's room with the broken window
locations.description: Bedroom with blind blowing in, shattered glass, dust-like specks swirling and lights burning blue.
locations.quote: the lights burn blue and dim

locations.name: Hillingham front avenue and porch
locations.description: Drive with gate leading to a house with locked doors and windows.
locations.quote: I went up the avenue alone.

locations.name: Hillingham kitchen and servants' rooms
locations.description: Kitchen with iron-barred window, boiler and fires still alive.
locations.quote: a kitchen window ... the iron bars which guarded the window

locations.name: Hillingham dining-room (shuttered)
locations.description: Dim room with shutters and blinds drawn, a sofa, table with sherry decanter.
locations.quote: dimly lit by rays of light through the shutters

locations.name: Lucy's bedroom (death-chamber)
locations.description: Bed with two women, window broken, sheet blown back by draught.
locations.quote: the edge of which had been blown back by the draught through the broken window

locations.name: Breakfast-room
locations.description: Less cheerless room with blinds up.
locations.quote: the breakfast-room, where the blinds were not drawn down

locations.name: Hillingham drawing-room
locations.description: Room with a big fire and two sofas.
locations.quote: Come to the drawing-room, where there is a big fire, and there are two sofas.

locations.name: Hawkins's house, Exeter
locations.description: Beautiful old house seeing the cathedral close with great elms and cawing rooks.
locations.quote: the great elms of the cathedral close

locations.name: Empty house adjoining the asylum (Carfax)
locations.description: Grounds where the carriers' cart delivers great wooden boxes.
locations.quote: some great wooden boxes

locations.name: Renfield's room
locations.description: Room with a window Renfield breaks through.
locations.quote: he had broken out through the window of his room

locations.name: Westenra house death-chamber (chapelle ardente)
locations.description: Room turned into a small chapel of death with a wilderness of white flowers, tall wax candles, the bed/bier with Lucy under a winding-sheet and lawn cloth; later with Mrs. Westenra's coffin too, and undertaker's display of goods.
locations.atmosphere: mortuary, hushed, beautiful and unsettling; garlic smell over lily and rose
locations.lighting_time: candlelight at night; dim at day
locations.quote: the room was turned into a small chapelle ardente.

locations.name: Westenra house hall
locations.description: Hall where the box of wild garlic from Mr. Van Helsing's order sits unopened.
locations.quote: a handful of wild garlic from the box waiting in the hall

locations.name: Westenra house drawing-room and dining room
locations.description: Rooms used by Arthur, Seward and Van Helsing for farewell, lunch with the solicitor, and dinner with cigars.
locations.quote: We all dined together

locations.name: Exeter church / Hawkins funeral
locations.description: Small, simple, solemn service for Mr. Hawkins.
locations.quote: The service was very simple and very solemn.

locations.name: Piccadilly outside Guiliano's
locations.description: Busy London street with a shop, a victoria carriage, hansom cabs and a girl in a big cart-wheel hat.
locations.quote: sitting in a victoria outside Guiliano’s

locations.name: Railway carriage
locations.description: Carriage in which Van Helsing and Seward return; Seward draws down the blinds.
locations.quote: I had to draw down the blinds

locations.name: Westenra family tomb, Kingstead churchyard
locations.description: A 'so fine marble house' death-house in a lonely churchyard where many of her kin rest; sun rises over Hampstead Hill, wild flowers grow.
locations.quote: a lordly death-house in a lonely churchyard

locations.name: Hampstead Heath, Shooter's Hill side
locations.description: Less-frequented part of the Heath with furze bushes where a child was found.
locations.quote: under a furze bush at the Shooter’s Hill side of Hampstead Heath

locations.name: Harkers' home, Exeter
locations.description: Mina's room, drawing-room with sofa and workbasket, a typewriter.
locations.quote: lock myself up in my room and read it

locations.name: Exeter hotel and railway station
locations.description: The hotel where Van Helsing stayed and the platform with train windows.
locations.quote: waiting for the train to start

locations.name: Seward's asylum study
locations.description: Study with a table and chairs.
locations.quote: almost bounded into the room

locations.name: Westenra tomb, Kingstead churchyard
locations.description: Marble vault with a creaky door; inside time-discoloured stone, dust-encrusted mortar, rusty dank iron, tarnished brass, clouded silver-plating on coffins, dead withered flowers, spiders and beetles. Lucy's coffin is wood with a lead casing.
features: creaky door with falling (not spring) lock
locations.atmosphere: miserable, sordid, decayed; mean-looking in sunshine
locations.lighting_time: candle at night, sunlight by day
locations.quote: the effect was more miserable and sordid than could have been imagined.

locations.name: Kingstead churchyard
locations.description: Low walled churchyard with yew trees, junipers marking the church path, alder clump, railed-off tombs, headstones.
locations.quote: I took up my place behind a yew-tree

locations.name: North Hospital ward
locations.description: Ward where the child recovers.
locations.quote: Dr. Vincent took the bandage from its throat

locations.name: Jack Straw's Castle
locations.description: Hampstead inn crowded with bicyclists.
locations.quote: a little crowd of bicyclists and others who were genially noisy

locations.name: Hampstead Heath edge near the Spaniards
locations.description: Pathway where the child is left for a policeman; the Spaniards where a cab is found.
locations.quote: At the edge of Hampstead Heath we heard a policeman’s heavy tramp

locations.name: Berkeley Hotel
locations.description: Hotel where Van Helsing lodges and meets Arthur and Quincey.
locations.quote: to the Berkeley Hotel at ten of the clock

locations.name: Westenra tomb interior (two visits)
locations.description: Vault with Lucy's coffin and others; wax candles stuck on other coffins; dark lantern; blue-flame oil lamp in corner.
features: other coffins used as candle stands
interstice small enough for a knife-blade
locations.quote: candles, which, when lighted, he stuck, by melting their own ends, on other coffins

locations.name: Kingstead churchyard at night
locations.description: Low wall, avenue of yews, cypress and juniper, scudding clouds, moonlight gleams, dogs howling, distant red sky and muffled roar of the city.
locations.quote: never did tombs look so ghastly white

locations.name: Churchyard at sunset/after funeral
locations.description: Gravediggers' work finished, sexton locks gate.
locations.quote: the sexton under the belief that every one had gone, had locked the gate

locations.name: Tomb exterior with Host seal
locations.description: Door with strips of white putty-and-Host in the crevices.
locations.quote: began to lay them into the crevices between the door and its setting in the tomb.

locations.name: Paddington station platform
locations.description: Arrival platform with crowd that melts away after the train.
locations.quote: The crowd melted away, after the bustling fashion common to arrival platforms

locations.name: Dr. Seward's study
locations.description: Study with a table holding the phonograph, a large drawer of wax cylinders, a cupboard with a case-bottle of brandy, and stacked typewriting.
locations.quote: He stood up and opened a large drawer, in which were arranged in order a number of hollow cylinders of metal covered with dark wax

locations.name: Purfleet asylum (Seward's house)
locations.description: Lunatic asylum with study, library, sitting-room and bedroom for Mrs. Harker, corridors, window overlooking the garden.
locations.quote: she was unable to repress a shudder when we entered.

locations.name: Whitby harbour, station and Billington's office
locations.description: Port with coastguards, Customs, harbour-master and station where boxes were received.
locations.atmosphere: local legend of the strange ship
locations.quote: the strange entry of the ship, which is already taking its place in local tradition

locations.name: Carfax, old chapel and house (as described by carriers)
locations.description: A house untouched for a hundred years, dust thick enough to sleep on, smelling of old Jerusalem; the old chapel is the worst.
locations.quote: I wouldn’t take less nor a quid a moment to stay there arter dark.

locations.name: Asylum corridor and passage
locations.description: Passage leading down to Renfield's room.
locations.quote: we all went down the passage together.

locations.name: Lawn and wood beyond the asylum
locations.description: Garden where Morris stands and fires; wood into which the bat flies.
locations.quote: it flew away into the wood.

locations.name: Carfax porch
locations.description: Front porch of the old house, with a step on which supplies are sorted.
locations.quote: When we got to the porch the Professor opened his bag and took out a lot of things

locations.name: Carfax hall
locations.description: Hall thick with dust inches deep, hobnail marks cracked in dust, webs like tattered rags, a table with a great bunch of time-yellowed labelled keys.
locations.quote: The floor was seemingly inches deep, except where there were recent footsteps

locations.name: Carfax chapel
locations.description: Reached through a low arched oaken door ribbed with iron bands; small, close, foul; holds the earth chests; vaulted door to a dark passage with solid walls and no hiding place.
features: arched oak door with iron bands
outer iron-bound oaken door with huge bolts and lock
locations.quote: a low, arched oaken door, ribbed with iron bands.

locations.name: Seward's lawn and mist
locations.description: Lawn where a white mist creeps toward the house against the walls.
locations.quote: a thin streak of white mist, that crept with almost imperceptible slowness across the grass towards the house

locations.name: Mina's bedroom
locations.description: Room above Renfield's, gaslight turned low, window closed, door with joinings.
locations.atmosphere: dank and cold in the dream
locations.quote: The gaslight which I had left lit for Jonathan, but turned down, came only like a tiny red spark through the fog

locations.name: Joseph Smollet's house, Walworth
locations.description: Modest workman's house; Smollet in shirtsleeves taking tea from a saucer, children present.
locations.quote: Mr. Joseph Smollet at home and in his shirtsleeves, taking a late tea out of a saucer.

locations.name: Corcoran's lodging-house, Potter's Court
locations.description: Doss-house in Walworth with a deputy at the door.
locations.quote: Corcoran’s lodging-house

locations.name: Cross Angel Street cold storage building
locations.description: New 'cold storage' warehouse under construction in Poplar with gatekeeper and foreman.
locations.quote: a new “cold storage” building

locations.name: No. 347 Piccadilly
locations.description: High stone-fronted house with a bow, high steps to the door, dusty windows and shutters, black framework, scaled paint, balcony with loose white-edged boards where a notice board was torn off; mews behind. Inside is a big empty hall.
locations.quote: It’s a ’igh ’un with a stone front with a bow on it, an’ ’igh steps up to the door.

locations.name: Mitchell, Sons & Candy office
locations.description: House agents in Sackville Street.
locations.quote: their office in Sackville Street

locations.name: Seward's study fireside
locations.description: Fireside gathering with smoke.
locations.quote: all gathered round the fire in the study

locations.name: The Harkers' bedroom
locations.description: Bedroom with a bed beside the window, a thick yellow blind and a gas lamp; the door locks from within.

locations.name: Asylum grounds with yew tree

locations.name: Old chapel at Carfax
locations.description: Neglected, dusty chapel in which the large earth-boxes sit.
locations.quote: in the old chapel the great boxes looked just as we had seen them last.

locations.name: Piccadilly house
locations.description: Deserted house among spruce neighbours with steps, a railing with spikes, a hall, a dining-room at the back and a stable at the rear across a stone-flagged yard.
locations.quote: looming up grim and silent in its deserted condition amongst its more lively and spruce-looking neighbours.

locations.name: Green Park
locations.description: Park near Arlington Street with benches in view of the house.
locations.quote: At the corner of Arlington Street our contingent got out and strolled into the Green Park.

locations.name: Asylum grounds and station route
locations.description: Lawn crossed on foot to reach the train; Mina's window visible from the lawn.
locations.quote: in the window of my own room saw Mina.

locations.name: Piccadilly house dining-room
locations.description: Back room with a window onto a stone-flagged yard and an open fireplace; door to the hall and one to the front room.
locations.quote: Van Helsing, Harker, and I were just behind the door

locations.name: Flagged yard and stable
locations.description: Narrow stone-flagged yard below the window with steps and a stable door with a rusty bolt; leads to a mews.
locations.quote: he, rushing up the steps, crossed the flagged yard, and pushed open the stable door.

locations.name: Seward's house sitting room
locations.description: Room where supper is held and Mina's plea is spoken.
locations.quote: We had a sort of perfunctory supper together

locations.name: The Harkers' room (watch)
locations.description: Room prepared by Van Helsing against the Vampire, with a bell and a gas flame lowered to a speck; dawn windows like sharp oblongs.
locations.quote: the grey of the coming dawn was making the windows into sharp oblongs

locations.name: Lloyd's
locations.description: Shipping register where all sailings, even small ships, are recorded.
locations.quote: where are note of all ships that sail, however so small.

locations.name: Doolittle's Wharf
locations.description: Thames wharf with a very small wooden office, gang-plank, truck for cargo; rough hot dockhands.
locations.quote: a man in an office of wood so small that the man look bigger than the office.

locations.name: The Czarina Catherine
locations.description: A sailing ship bound for Varna and then up the Danube.
locations.quote: She is the Czarina Catherine, and she sail from Doolittle’s Wharf for Varna

locations.name: Harkers' room
locations.description: Bedroom with a mirror in which Mina sees her scar.
locations.atmosphere: intimate, charged at sunrise and sunset
locations.quote: She had fallen back on her pillow asleep; she did not even wake when I had pulled up the blind

locations.name: Varna (planned)
locations.description: Black Sea port, unfamiliar to all of the party, where the box will be landed to agent Ristics.
locations.quote: The box we seek is to be landed in Varna, and to be given to an agent, one Ristics

locations.name: Mrs. Harker's sitting room at the asylum
locations.description: A room with a sofa where Mina half reclines; chairs are drawn up close around her.
locations.quote: she made the rest of us bring chairs up close.

locations.name: Orient Express train
locations.description: Long-distance night-and-day train from Paris to Varna.
locations.quote: took the places secured for us in the Orient Express.

locations.name: Hotel Odessus, Varna
locations.description: The party's hotel; rooms used for hypnotic sessions and planning.
locations.quote: this hotel—“the Odessus.”

locations.name: British Vice-Consulate / Lloyd's wire at Varna
locations.description: Office where Godalming receives daily telegrams about the ship.
locations.quote: care of H. B. M. Vice-Consul, Varna.

locations.name: The Czarina Catherine (at sea, imagined)
locations.description: Sailing/steam ship with canvas, cordage, masts, yards and shrouds, carrying the Count's earth-box; only known through Mina's trance.
locations.quote: Canvas and cordage strain and masts and yards creak.

locations.name: Czarina Catherine (anchored at Galatz)
locations.description: Sailing/steam cargo ship lying at anchor in the river harbour; deck, handspikes, captain's cabin.
locations.quote: which lay at anchor out in the river harbour.

locations.name: Hildesheim's office, Burgen-strasse 16
locations.description: Office of a Jewish agent in a fez, Adelphi-theatre type with a nose like a sheep.
locations.quote: We found Hildesheim in his office

locations.name: St. Peter's churchyard wall, Galatz
locations.description: Wall of a churchyard where Skinsky's mutilated body is found.
locations.quote: inside the wall of the churchyard of St. Peter

locations.name: Galatz hotel
locations.description: Rooms ordered by telegraph; Mina types and plans here; sofa for Jonathan.
locations.quote: the hotel where our rooms had been ordered by telegraph

locations.name: Steam launch
locations.description: Lovely steam launch with furnace, electric lamp, Roumanian flag.
locations.quote: I am writing this in the light from the furnace door of the steam launch

locations.name: Sereth and Bistritza rivers
locations.description: Wide river with open boats, rapids on the Bistritza, junction at Fundu, snow-fed mountain streams.
locations.quote: There seem to be endless streams running down the mountains into this river

locations.name: Veresti
locations.description: Town where the carriage journey to the Borgo Pass begins, more than 70 miles away.
locations.quote: We have something more than 70 miles before us.

locations.name: Borgo Pass road
locations.description: Little-used by-road distinct from the wide hard coach road from the Bukovina to Bistritz; steep, rocky, neglected, lightly snowed.

locations.name: Camp below the castle (Holy circle)
locations.description: Fire, rugs, ring of crumbled wafer, tethered horses, wreathing snow and mist.

locations.name: Castle Dracula (exterior)
locations.description: Broken battlements on a summit of a sheer precipice a thousand feet up, with a gap between it and the adjoining mountain.
locations.quote: perched a thousand feet on the summit of a sheer precipice

locations.name: Castle chapel and tombs
locations.description: Old chapel with age-fretted tombs under centuries of dust, sulphurous odour, and one huge noble tomb lettered DRACULA.
locations.quote: On it was but one word DRACULA.

locations.name: Rock hollow shelter
locations.description: Natural hollow in rock with doorway-like entrance between two boulders; vantage rock above.
locations.quote: a sort of natural hollow in a rock, with an entrance like a doorway between two boulders.

locations.name: Plain below the castle
locations.description: White snowy waste with the river a black ribbon in kinks and curls, poor road with deep ruts.
locations.quote: I could see the river lying like a black ribbon in kinks and curls

locations.name: Farmhouse/Veresti stages
locations.description: Stop-over houses where horses are changed and food served.
locations.quote: We get hot soup, or coffee, or tea; and off we go.

characters.name: Gypsy (Szgany) leader

objects.name: Crucifix on rosary

objects.description: Plum brandy of the country under the calèche's seat.
objects.location_or_owner: Underneath the seat of the calèche
objects.quote: There is a flask of slivovitz (the plum brandy of the country) underneath the seat

objects.name: Cloak and rug
objects.description: Thrown over Harker's shoulders and knees in the calèche.
objects.quote: a cloak was thrown over my shoulders, and a rug across my knees

objects.description: Light carriage drawn by four coal-black horses.

objects.quote: the crazy coach rocked on its great leather springs

objects.quote: with its long, snake-like vertebra, calculated to suit the inequalities of the road

objects.quote: gathering a few stones, formed them into some device

objects.quote: I struck a match, and by its flame looked at my watch

objects.name: Carriage lamps
objects.description: Lamps lit by the driver; flickering light.

objects.name: Roadside crosses and shrines
objects.description: Crosses by the road and shrines before which peasants kneel.
objects.quote: By the roadside were many crosses

objects.name: Harker's luggage
objects.description: Bags handed to the calèche driver.
objects.quote: my bags were handed out and put in the calèche

objects.quote: an antique silver lamp, in which the flame burned without chimney or globe of any kind

objects.quote: A key was turned with the loud grating noise of long disuse

objects.name: Gold table service

objects.description: Supper for Harker; Tokay he drinks two glasses.
objects.quote: an excellent roast chicken. This, with some cheese and a salad and a bottle of old Tokay

objects.name: Cigar
objects.description: Offered by Count, who does not smoke.
objects.quote: begun to smoke a cigar which he offered me

objects.name: Card note

objects.quote: “I have to be absent for a while. Do not wait for me.—D.”

objects.name: Cold breakfast with coffee on the hearth
objects.description: Breakfast with pot of coffee kept hot on the hearth.
objects.quote: a cold breakfast laid out, with coffee kept hot by the pot being placed on the hearth

objects.description: Views taken from various points.
objects.quote: I have taken with my kodak views of it from various points

objects.name: Locked doors
objects.description: Every door in the castle locked and bolted.
objects.quote: doors, doors, doors everywhere, and all locked and bolted

objects.quote: the crow of a cock coming up with preternatural shrillness

objects.quote: I have placed the crucifix over the head of my bed

objects.quote: directed to Samuel F. Billington, No. 7, The Crescent, Whitby, another to Herr Leutner, Varna

objects.description: His journal and pen kept in a pocket.

objects.name: Lamp
objects.description: Lamp Harker takes to try all the doors; pale against moonlight.
objects.quote: taking a lamp, tried all the doors

objects.quote: sitting at a little oak table where in old times possibly some fair lady sat to pen

objects.name: Great couch

objects.description: Left unwound after the night.

objects.name: Harker's smuggled letters

objects.name: Lamp flame

objects.name: Clean envelope

objects.quote: handed me a clean envelope

objects.quote: he had on the suit of clothes which I had worn whilst travelling here

objects.quote: my letter of credit, in fact all that might be useful to me were I once outside the castle

objects.name: Great square boxes

objects.quote: great, square boxes, with handles of thick rope

objects.name: Leiter-wagons

objects.quote: two great leiter-wagons, each drawn by eight sturdy horses

objects.name: Crucifix
objects.description: Still on Harker's neck from ch. 1-2.

objects.quote: (Kept in phonograph)

objects.name: Wine-cup
