objects.quote: even for me a large-bore revolver

objects.name: Traveller's typewriter
objects.description: Portable typewriter obtained for Mina by Morris.
objects.quote: the “Traveller’s” typewriter

objects.name: Maps and appliances
objects.description: Maps of rivers, with Pruth, Sereth, Bistritza.
objects.quote: We have all the maps and appliances of various kinds that can be had.

objects.name: Steam launch electric lamp
objects.description: Searchlight to inspect passing boats.
objects.quote: we turned our electric lamp on them

objects.name: Roumanian flag
objects.description: Flag flown from the launch to appear official.
objects.quote: we got a Roumanian flag which we now fly conspicuously.

objects.name: Fur coats and wraps
objects.description: Warm clothing bought at Veresti.
objects.quote: such a wonderful lot of fur coats and wraps

objects.name: Provision basket
objects.description: Huge basket of food from the landlady.
objects.quote: a huge basket of provisions

objects.name: Saddle with movable horn
objects.description: Saddle adaptable for Mina.
objects.function_in_story: If the party must ride together.
objects.quote: One of the saddles has a movable horn

objects.name: Earth-box marked Galatz via Varna
objects.description: The Count's box, marked and taken by Skinsky.
objects.quote: it was marked Galatz via Varna

objects.name: Host Wafer
objects.description: Consecrated wafer crumbled to powder.
objects.function_in_story: Strewn on the circle, carried as protection, laid in Dracula's tomb to bar his return.
objects.quote: over the ring I passed some of the wafer, and I broke it fine

objects.name: Holy circle
objects.description: Ring drawn on the ground, sealed by crumbled wafer.
objects.function_in_story: Mina cannot leave nor the Brides enter.
objects.quote: They could not approach, me, whilst so armed, nor Madam Mina whilst she remained within the ring

objects.name: Blacksmith hammer
objects.description: Smith's hammer bought at Veresti.
objects.function_in_story: Breaks castle doors off hinges, wrenches tomb lids, drives stakes.
objects.quote: The blacksmith hammer which I took in the carriage from Veresti was useful

objects.name: Stakes and knife
objects.description: Stakes and a knife used on the Brides.
objects.quote: hardly had my knife severed the head of each

objects.name: Kukri
objects.description: Jonathan's great knife; used as pry bar and to cut the Count's throat.
objects.function_in_story: Opens the box lid and decapitates.
objects.quote: attempting to prize off the lid with his great Kukri knife

objects.name: Bowie knife
objects.description: Large hunting knife.
objects.function_in_story: Parries gypsy blades, prises box, pierces the Count's heart.
objects.quote: Mr. Morris’s bowie knife plunged into the heart.

objects.name: Mina's revolver
objects.description: Large-bore revolver.
objects.quote: I got out my revolver ready to hand

objects.name: Garlic in food
objects.description: Extra garlic added by superstitious farmwives.
objects.quote: an extra amount of garlic into our food; and I can’t abide garlic

objects.name: Firewood supply
objects.description: Wood brought in carriage for fires.
objects.function_in_story: Fire at camp; Van Helsing waves a brand at the Brides.
objects.quote: we have brought supply of wood with us

objects.name: Furs and rugs
objects.description: Heavy rugs and wraps.
objects.quote: I made a couch with furs

objects.name: Field-glasses
objects.description: Binoculars in a case.
objects.function_in_story: Spot the gypsies and the horsemen.
objects.quote: Taking his field-glasses from the case

objects.name: Great square chest
objects.description: The Count's coffin box, nailed shut, earth inside.
objects.quote: On the cart was a great square chest.

objects.name: Tomb marked DRACULA
objects.description: Large lordly empty tomb.
objects.function_in_story: Wafer laid inside to bar the Count's return.
objects.quote: On it was but one word DRACULA.

objects.name: Four-in-hand carriage
objects.description: Rude carriage with four horses.
objects.quote: now we have a rude four-in-hand.

objects.name: Van Helsing's memorandum
objects.description: Letter-record to Seward.
objects.quote: This to my old and true friend John Seward

objects.name: Safe with the papers
objects.description: Safe where the record (typescript, notebooks, memorandum) was kept since their return.
objects.quote: I took the papers from the safe where they had been ever since our return so long ago.

creatures.name: Wolves
creatures.description: Long, sinewy limbs, shaggy hair, white teeth and lolling red tongues; form a silent ring around the calèche.
creatures.behaviour: Howl in answer to the dogs at midnight; encircle prey in silence; obey the driver's arm sweeps.
creatures.quote: a ring of wolves, with white teeth and lolling red tongues, with long, sinewy limbs and shaggy hair

creatures.name: Village dogs
creatures.description: Farm dogs that howl at midnight.
creatures.behaviour: Take up one another's howls; fierce on the hills.
creatures.quote: a long, agonised wailing, as if from fear

creatures.name: Coal-black horses
creatures.description: Splendid coal-black team of four drawing the calèche.
creatures.behaviour: Rear and sweat with fear at wolves but are calmed by the driver's whispering.
creatures.quote: the horses were coal-black and splendid animals

creatures.name: Dracula (disguised as coachman)
creatures.description: Seemingly human driver with superhuman strength, red-gleaming eyes and sharp teeth.
creatures.behaviour: Controls animals, vanishes, appears at the right time.
creatures.quote: his strength must have been prodigious

creatures.name: Blue flames
creatures.description: Faint flickering blue flame over the ground that casts no light on its surroundings and does not obstruct when a person passes in front.
creatures.behaviour: Appear in the night; the driver marks each with stones.
creatures.quote: Suddenly, away on our left, I saw a faint flickering blue flame.

creatures.name: Wolves of the valley
creatures.description: Howling heard from the valley at dawn.
creatures.behaviour: Howl in chorus; Dracula calls them his children of the night.
creatures.quote: the howling of many wolves

creatures.name: Count Dracula
creatures.description: A vampire host who does not eat or drink, casts no reflection, has hairy palms, fangs, cold hand, rank breath, and reacts to blood and crucifix.
creatures.behaviour: Is absent by day, nocturnal, flies into fury at the sight of blood but is stopped by the crucifix.
weaknesses: throat cut and heart pierced by sunset
creatures.quote: his eyes blazed with a sort of demoniac fury, and he suddenly made a grab at my throat

creatures.name: Three vampire women
creatures.description: Beautiful women with no shadow, red-seeming eyes and pearl-white teeth; they lick lips and hover over the victim.
creatures.behaviour: Approach a sleeper, argue over who goes first, prefer a throat bite; obey the Count's authority; take a child in a bag.
creatures.quote: though the moonlight was behind them, they threw no shadow on the floor

creatures.name: Count Dracula as wall-crawler
creatures.description: Crawls head-down down the sheer castle wall, fingers and toes gripping eroded stones.
creatures.behaviour: Leaves the castle at night by his window, vanishes into a lower hole.
creatures.quote: just as a lizard moves along a wall

creatures.name: Child in the bag
creatures.description: A smothered child heard wailing in the bag.
creatures.quote: a gasp and a low wail, as of a half-smothered child

creatures.name: Wolves of the courtyard
creatures.description: Pack flooding through the wide entrance; red jaws, champing teeth, blunt-clawed feet.
creatures.behaviour: Called by the Count's harsh metallic whisper; kill the mother; stream away singly licking their lips; howl at the Count's raised hand.
creatures.quote: a pack of them poured, like a pent-up dam when liberated, through the wide entrance into the courtyard

creatures.name: Count Dracula (resting)
creatures.description: Lying open-eyed without pulse or breath in the earth-box by day; after feeding gorged like a leech.
creatures.behaviour: Sleeps in earth; wakes his gaze on being touched; scales the wall as a lizard.
weaknesses: resting in his box by day
head can be struck but a man-made blow glances
creatures.quote: He lay like a filthy leech, exhausted with his repletion.

creatures.name: Three women (phantoms)
creatures.description: Shapes emerging from dust in moonbeams.
creatures.behaviour: Wait outside Harker's door, laugh and run when he opens it.
creatures.quote: three terrible women licking their lips

creatures.name: Moonlight dust motes
creatures.description: Quaint specks that gather into clusters and take phantom shapes, hypnotising the watcher.
creatures.behaviour: Dance faster as dogs howl.
weaknesses: lamp light; Harker flees from moonlight to a lamp-lit room
creatures.quote: quaint little specks floating in the rays of the moonlight

creatures.name: The White Lady of the abbey
creatures.description: Legendary figure seen in an abbey window.
creatures.behaviour: Seen at a window (legend only; Swales dismisses it).
creatures.quote: there is a legend that a white lady is seen in one of the windows

creatures.name: Bell-ghosts at sea
creatures.description: Legend that bells are heard when a ship is lost.
creatures.behaviour: Heard out at sea.
creatures.quote: They have a legend here that when a ship is lost bells are heard out at sea.

creatures.name: Folk spirits (bans, wafts, boh-ghosts, barguests, bogles)
creatures.description: Local ghost types listed by Swales.
creatures.behaviour: Said to scare children and dizzy women.
creatures.quote: These bans an' wafts an' boh-ghosts an' barguests an' bogles

creatures.name: Renfield's swarm (flies, spiders, sparrows)
creatures.description: Chain of animals harvested by Renfield.
creatures.behaviour: Flies eaten by spiders, spiders by sparrows.
creatures.quote: He gave many flies to one spider and many spiders to one bird

creatures.name: The immense dog
creatures.description: Huge dog that springs from the hold on grounding and vanishes toward the churchyard; later a half-bred mastiff is killed in a fight with a savage opponent (implied the dog).
creatures.behaviour: Flees into darkness; savage killer with claw-like wounds on the mastiff.
creatures.quote: an immense dog sprang up on deck from below

creatures.name: The tall thin pale stranger (It / Him)
creatures.description: Tall, thin, ghastly pale figure that appears on the deck, bows, and in the hold; leaves no trace; intangible to a knife.
creatures.behaviour: Appears at night or fog, takes crew one by one from watch; fog seems to travel with the ship.
weaknesses: fears a crucifix (inferred: captain ties 'that which He dare not touch' to his hands)
creatures.quote: tall and thin, and ghastly pale

creatures.name: Terrified dog at the grave
creatures.description: Master's dog, furious and then cowering on the suicide's tombstone.
creatures.behaviour: Barks and howls with bristling hair, quiets in terror on the stone.
creatures.quote: in such a pitiable state of terror

creatures.name: Sea-fog
creatures.description: White wet clouds that seem like the hands of drowned dead.
creatures.behaviour: Sweeps in ghostly fashion; seems to follow the Demeter.
creatures.quote: the spirits of those lost at sea were touching their living brethren with the clammy hands of death

creatures.name: Dark figure with red eyes (Dracula, unnamed)
creatures.description: A long dark figure bending over Lucy, white face, red gleaming eyes; later a dark figure on the seat seems to have burning eyes.
creatures.behaviour: Vanishes within moments; comes to Lucy while she sleepwalks; sits on the window-sill as a bird-like thing.
creatures.quote: a white face and red, gleaming eyes

creatures.name: Great bat
creatures.description: Large bat circling the moonlit window; flits towards the abbey.
creatures.behaviour: Whirling circles; retreats when seen.
weaknesses: frightened by Mina's presence at the window
creatures.quote: a great bat, coming and going in great whirling circles

creatures.name: Bird-like thing on the sill
creatures.description: Good-sized bird shape on Lucy's window-sill.
creatures.behaviour: Sits by sleeping Lucy.
creatures.quote: something that looked like a good-sized bird

creatures.name: Howling dogs of Whitby
creatures.description: Whole town of dogs howling in Lucy's dream.
creatures.behaviour: Howl as she goes up the steps.
creatures.quote: the whole town seemed as if it must be full of dogs all howling at once

creatures.name: Renfield (frenzied)
creatures.description: Strong lunatic who sniffs like a setter, obeys a Master and fights like a tiger.
creatures.behaviour: Bids the Master, escapes, begs; violent when restrained.
creatures.quote: he fought like a tiger

creatures.name: Big bat
creatures.description: Large bat that flies silently and straight, not wheeling like ordinary bats, heading west from the moonlit sky.
creatures.behaviour: Purposeful; calms Renfield when seen; scratches or flaps at Lucy's window (implied).
creatures.quote: as if it knew where it was bound for or had some intention of its own

creatures.name: Flies and spiders
creatures.description: Renfield's collected insects; he looks for a spider.
creatures.behaviour: Drawn to sugar.
creatures.quote: is already examining the corners of his room to find a spider

creatures.name: Unseen bloodsucker (the vampire)
creatures.description: Not seen; leaves two punctures over Lucy's jugular with white worn edges.
creatures.behaviour: Feeds on Lucy at night while she sleeps; strikes again the night Seward sleeps.
creatures.quote: two punctures, not large, but not wholesome-looking

creatures.name: Bersicker (grey Norwegian wolf)
creatures.description: One of three grey wolves from Norway sold by Jamrach, escapes by bending cage rails and returns with a head full of broken glass.
creatures.behaviour: Calm with the keeper; howls at moonrise; follows the stranger with his eyes.
creatures.quote: I see the rails broken and twisted about and the cage empty.

creatures.name: Great gaunt grey wolf at the window
creatures.description: Head thrust through the broken panes, howls in the shrubbery.
creatures.behaviour: Smashes glass, withdraws, then specks enter.
creatures.quote: the head of a great, gaunt grey wolf

creatures.name: Dust-like specks
creatures.description: Myriad specks circling like a simoon pillar.
creatures.behaviour: Blow in through broken window, make the lights burn blue.
creatures.quote: a whole myriad of little specks seemed to come blowing in

creatures.name: Lucy, turning
creatures.description: Lucy sleeping: gums drawn back, canines look longer and sharper, lips open, stertorous breathing.
creatures.behaviour: Voluptuous voice; spasm of rage; champing teeth; tears garlic away asleep.
creatures.quote: the canine teeth looked longer and sharper than the rest

creatures.name: Vampire bat of the Pampas
creatures.description: South American bat that killed Quincey's mare by draining blood.
creatures.behaviour: Leaves an open vein; victim collapses.
creatures.quote: One of those big bats that they call vampires had got at her in the night

creatures.name: Count Dracula (young form)
creatures.description: Tall thin dark man with beaky nose, pointed teeth, red lips, rejuvenated.
creatures.behaviour: Stalks a young woman through Piccadilly, follows her by hansom.
creatures.quote: his big white teeth, that looked all the whiter because his lips were so red, were pointed like an animal’s.

creatures.name: The 'bloofer lady' (Lucy, implied)
creatures.description: Seen only through children's accounts; she lures them for walks on the Heath at night.
creatures.behaviour: Leaves small throat wounds; children weak and emaciated.
creatures.quote: they had been with a “bloofer lady.”

creatures.name: Vampire bats of the Pampas and Western isles
creatures.description: Bats that open the veins of cattle and horses; on islands hang like giant nuts or pods and attack sleeping sailors.
creatures.behaviour: flit down on sleepers, leave dead men white as Lucy
creatures.quote: there are bats that come at night and open the veins of cattle and horses

creatures.name: The great spider of the Spanish church
creatures.description: A spider that lived for centuries in the tower, drinking the oil of the church lamps.
creatures.behaviour: grew and grew
creatures.quote: one great spider lived for centuries in the tower of the old Spanish church

creatures.name: Lucy as the Un-Dead (implied)
creatures.description: The cause of the children's wounds, revealed in the last line.
creatures.behaviour: lures children at night
creatures.quote: They were made by Miss Lucy!

creatures.name: Lucy Westenra, Un-Dead
creatures.description: A corpse unchanged for a week, rosier than in life, with sharpened teeth; travels at night as a white figure.
creatures.behaviour: Leaves her coffin at sundown and lures children, returns before dawn; sleeping face shows no malice because she was bitten in a trance.
creatures.quote: The lips were red, nay redder than before

creatures.name: The dark mass (Van Helsing's side)
creatures.description: Mass moving toward the white streak - Van Helsing hurrying.
creatures.behaviour: intercepts the child
creatures.quote: a dark mass moved from the Professor’s side of the ground

creatures.name: The Count (mentioned)
creatures.description: The master who may seek Lucy's tomb for shelter, with strength of twenty men and ability to summon a wolf.
creatures.behaviour: cunning
weaknesses: can be killed by beheading and burning the heart or staking
creatures.quote: He have always the strength in his hand of twenty men

creatures.name: Lucy, the Bloofer Lady (Un-Dead)
creatures.description: Fully corporeal vampire woman in grave clothes, blood on lips, eyes of hell-fire, face turning to a Medusa-like 'passion mask' when thwarted.
creatures.behaviour: Carries off a child, drinks its blood, discards it when interrupted; tempts a loved one to embrace and die; snarls like a cat when surprised.
weaknesses: stake driven through the heart by a hand of love
creatures.quote: She recoiled from it, and, with a suddenly distorted face, full of rage

creatures.name: The Count (offstage)
creatures.description: Referred to as 'this Thing', not human, not beast.
creatures.behaviour: His lair is next to the asylum; Renfield's moods track his proximity.
creatures.quote: this Thing is not human—not even beast.

creatures.name: Renfield (zoophagous patient)
creatures.description: Eats flies and spiders; bound to the Count.
creatures.behaviour: Calm when the Count's triumph seems assured.
creatures.quote: he is himself zoöphagous

creatures.name: Count Dracula (described)
creatures.description: Strength of twenty men, ancient cunning, necromancy, no shadow or reflection, sees in the dark.
creatures.behaviour: Changes form to wolf, bat, mist, elemental dust, can become small; commands rat, owl, bat, moth, fox, wolf; directs storm, fog, thunder.
weaknesses: cannot enter uninvited the first time
power ceases at day; changes only at noon, sunrise, sunset when away from his lair
running water only at slack or flood of tide
needs native earth and cannot rest in soil barren of holy memories
creatures.quote: he is brute, and more than brute; he is devil in callous, and the heart of him is not

creatures.name: Bat at the window
creatures.description: Large bat on the sill.
creatures.behaviour: Flew into the wood after the shot.
creatures.quote: there came a big bat and sat on the window-sill.

creatures.name: Rats of Carfax
creatures.description: Thousands of rats with glittering baleful eyes, bodies dark, eyes shining like fireflies in lamplight.
creatures.behaviour: Appear from corners in a phosphorescent swarm and multiply by the minute; summoned by the Count.
weaknesses: not under the Count's spiritual power once dogs attack
creatures.quote: The rats were multiplying in thousands, and we moved out.

creatures.name: Terriers (3)
creatures.description: Dogs of Lord Godalming that howl at the chapel threshold but fight when placed inside.
creatures.behaviour: Kill rats by the score; frisk around once the evil leaves.
weaknesses: fear the threshold until carried in
creatures.quote: The instant his feet touched the ground he seemed to recover his courage

creatures.name: Mist (Count in dream)
creatures.description: White mist entering through door joins forming a pillar with two red eyes.
creatures.behaviour: Presses against walls and windows.
creatures.quote: a sort of pillar of cloud in the room

creatures.name: Shadow face illusion
creatures.description: A glimpse of the Count's face in the dark passage, pale with red eyes and lips.
creatures.behaviour: Only shadows.
creatures.quote: the high lights of the Count’s evil face, the ridge of the nose, the red eyes, the red lips, the awful pallor.

creatures.name: The Count as old man
creatures.description: Old man with white moustache, very thin, uncannily strong.
creatures.behaviour: Waits at both houses, opens doors himself, helps load boxes, threatens loafers.
creatures.quote: he took up ’is end o’ the boxes like they was pounds of tea

creatures.name: Renfield
creatures.description: Zoophagous madman linked to the Count.
creatures.behaviour: Fly-catching resumes; speaks of souls.
creatures.quote: Life is all I want.

creatures.name: Rat swarm
creatures.description: Thousands of rats with blazing red eyes spreading over the grass like a flame of fire.
creatures.behaviour: Called and stopped by the Count's raised hand; used as a temptation.
weaknesses: dispersed when the Count wills it
creatures.quote: there were thousands of rats with their eyes blazing red—like His, only smaller.

creatures.name: Death's-head moth
creatures.description: Large moth with a skull and cross-bones on its back (Acherontia Atropos).
creatures.behaviour: Sent in by the Count as a gift to Renfield.
creatures.quote: big moths, in the night, with skull and cross-bones on their backs.

creatures.name: Steel-and-sapphire flies
creatures.description: Great fat flies with steel and sapphire wings.
creatures.behaviour: Sent in by the Count in daylight.
creatures.quote: Great big fat ones with steel and sapphire on their wings

creatures.name: Dogs of Carfax
creatures.description: Dogs barking beyond the trees behind the asylum.
creatures.behaviour: Bark and howl when the Count arrives.
creatures.quote: I heard the dogs bark behind our house, but not where He was!

creatures.name: Bat
creatures.description: Bat form of the Count flying west from Renfield's window.
creatures.behaviour: Escape and scouting form.
creatures.quote: I saw a bat rise from Renfield’s window, and flap westward.

creatures.name: Count Dracula (in material form)
creatures.description: Solid, agile body that can leap like a panther.
creatures.behaviour: Cautious entry, then flight rather than fight.
weaknesses: kukri blade could cut his heart
creatures.quote: a horrible sort of snarl passed over his face, showing the eye-teeth long and pointed

creatures.name: Fog around the ship
creatures.description: Dense local fog that rises from the river and encloses only the Czarina Catherine and the wharf.
creatures.behaviour: Called by the Count to delay departure to full tide and hide him.
creatures.quote: a dense fog enveloped the ship and all around her.

creatures.name: Wolves of the Carpathians (anticipated)
creatures.description: Wolf packs expected on arrival.
creatures.behaviour: Hunting packs, as at Tobolsk.
creatures.quote: the Count comes from a wolf country

creatures.name: Count Dracula (in ship's earth-box)
creatures.description: Helpless in the box by day, possibly as bat at night; present only by Mina's hypnotic perception.
creatures.behaviour: Sends spirit to read Mina's mind, then cuts her off; hurries to his destination.
weaknesses: cannot cross running water of his own volition
must stay in the box by day
head cut off and stake through heart
creatures.quote: The Count, even if he takes the form of a bat, cannot cross the running water of his own volition

creatures.name: Count Dracula (on river in box)
creatures.description: Helpless in earth-box carried on an open boat by Slovaks.
creatures.behaviour: Murdered Skinsky; avoided customs; summons fog and storm at night.
weaknesses: running water would engulf him if wrecked
dependent on carriers who might throw him in the river
creatures.quote: On the water he is powerless except at night; even then he can only summon fog and storm and snow and his wolves.

creatures.name: Cattle
creatures.description: Lowing near the river in the trance.
creatures.quote: Cattle low far off.

creatures.name: The three Brides
creatures.description: Three vampire women (two fair, one dark) formerly seen in Harker's castle room, now in tombs by day.
creatures.behaviour: By night appear as snow and mist taking shape, lure Mina, circle the Holy ring.
creatures.quote: the wheeling figures of mist and snow came closer, but keeping ever without the Holy circle.

creatures.name: Szgany gypsies
creatures.description: Mounted peasants and gypsies escorting the cart, armed with knives and pistols.
creatures.behaviour: Race for the sunset, scatter after the Count turns to dust.
creatures.quote: turned, without a word, and rode away as if for their lives.

vampire_lore.rule: Eve of St. George's Day: evil things have full sway at midnight
vampire_lore.detail: Local belief reported by the landlady; the night of 4-5 May.
vampire_lore.quote: all the evil things in the world will have full sway

vampire_lore.rule: The evil-eye guard: cross and two pointed fingers
vampire_lore.detail: Crowd makes the sign of the cross and points two fingers at Harker as a charm against the evil eye.
vampire_lore.quote: a charm or guard against the evil eye

vampire_lore.rule: Crucifix and protective plants given as wards
vampire_lore.detail: Crucifix, rosary, and (named later) garlic, wild rose, mountain ash.
vampire_lore.quote: each was given in simple good faith, with a kindly word, and a blessing

vampire_lore.rule: Names for the undead
vampire_lore.detail: Ordog (Satan), pokol (hell), stregoica (witch), vrolok (Slovak) and vlkoslak (Servian) meaning were-wolf or vampire.
vampire_lore.quote: “vrolok” and “vlkoslak”—both of which mean the same thing

vampire_lore.rule: Dracula commands wolves and horses
vampire_lore.detail: Wolves fall back at his arm-sweep; horses calm at his whisper.
vampire_lore.quote: the wolves fell back and back further still

vampire_lore.rule: Superhuman strength
vampire_lore.detail: Grip of steel, lifts and handles luggage easily.
vampire_lore.quote: a hand which caught my arm in a grip of steel

vampire_lore.rule: Blue flame marks hidden treasure on this night
vampire_lore.detail: Folk belief explained in chapter 2; the driver follows the flames.
vampire_lore.quote: a faint flickering blue flame

vampire_lore.rule: Eyes glow red; very red lips and sharp white teeth
vampire_lore.detail: Visible tells at first meeting.
vampire_lore.quote: a pair of very bright eyes, which seemed red in the lamplight

vampire_lore.rule: The dead travel fast
vampire_lore.detail: Line from Burger's Lenore whispered by a passenger who recognises the driver.
vampire_lore.quote: Denn die Todten reiten schnell

vampire_lore.rule: Flame passes through him
vampire_lore.detail: When the driver stood between Harker and the flame he did not obstruct it; he seems insubstantial to light.
vampire_lore.quote: when he stood between me and the flame he did not obstruct it

vampire_lore.rule: Must be invited to enter, of free will
vampire_lore.detail: The Count ritually invites Harker to enter freely; he does not step forward until Harker has crossed the threshold.
vampire_lore.quote: Enter freely and of your own will!

vampire_lore.rule: Icy hand, great strength
vampire_lore.detail: His handshake is cold as the dead and crushing.
vampire_lore.quote: more like the hand of a dead than a living man

vampire_lore.rule: Does not eat, drink or smoke
vampire_lore.detail: He claims to have dined; Harker later notes he has never seen him eat or drink.
vampire_lore.quote: I do not sup.

vampire_lore.rule: No reflection
vampire_lore.detail: No image in the shaving glass.
vampire_lore.quote: The whole room behind me was displayed; but there was no sign of a man in it, except myself.

vampire_lore.rule: Mirrors absent in the castle
vampire_lore.detail: No mirror anywhere, not even a toilet glass.
vampire_lore.quote: in none of the rooms is there a mirror

vampire_lore.rule: Blood sends him into fury
vampire_lore.detail: On seeing Harker's cut he lunges at his throat.
vampire_lore.quote: his eyes blazed with a sort of demoniac fury

vampire_lore.rule: Crucifix halts his attack
vampire_lore.detail: Touching the crucifix's cord instantly ends his fury.
vampire_lore.quote: It made an instant change in him

vampire_lore.rule: Dawn and cock-crow end his night
vampire_lore.detail: The crow of a cock makes him spring up and leave quickly.
vampire_lore.quote: Count Dracula, jumping to his feet

vampire_lore.rule: Physical tells: hairy palms, pointed nails and ears, rank breath, canine teeth
vampire_lore.detail: Detailed during the fireside observation.
vampire_lore.quote: there were hairs in the centre of the palm

vampire_lore.rule: Absent by day
vampire_lore.detail: The Count is always absent in the afternoon and Harker does not see him by daylight.
vampire_lore.quote: I have to be away till the afternoon

vampire_lore.rule: Commands wolves
vampire_lore.detail: Wolves howl at his remark.
vampire_lore.quote: Listen to them—the children of the night.

vampire_lore.rule: Blue flames mark treasure on St. George's night
vampire_lore.detail: Folk-belief given by the Count.
vampire_lore.quote: a blue flame is seen over any place where treasure has been concealed

vampire_lore.rule: No shadow
vampire_lore.detail: The three women cast no shadow in bright moonlight.
vampire_lore.quote: they threw no shadow on the floor

vampire_lore.rule: Bite at the throat; sweet breath tinged with blood
vampire_lore.detail: The fair woman's breath is honey-sweet with a bitter blood smell.
vampire_lore.quote: a bitter offensiveness, as one smells in blood

vampire_lore.rule: Seductive trance of the victim
vampire_lore.detail: Harker feels desire and awaits the kiss.
vampire_lore.quote: a wicked, burning desire that they would kiss me

vampire_lore.rule: Dematerialise into moonlight
vampire_lore.detail: They fade into the moonbeams and pass through the window.
vampire_lore.quote: They simply seemed to fade into the rays of the moonlight

vampire_lore.rule: Wall-crawling like a lizard
vampire_lore.detail: The Count descends sheer walls head-first.
vampire_lore.quote: just as a lizard moves along a wall

vampire_lore.rule: Sleeping outside the Count's rooms is dangerous
vampire_lore.detail: The Count warns Harker not to sleep elsewhere or there will be bad dreams (washing-hands gesture).
vampire_lore.quote: you will not by any chance go to sleep in any other part of the castle

vampire_lore.rule: Crucifix gives safety
vampire_lore.detail: Harker feels comfort and freer rest with it over his bed.
vampire_lore.quote: it is a comfort and a strength to me whenever I touch it

vampire_lore.rule: The Count rules the others
vampire_lore.detail: His gesture drives the women back as it did the wolves.
vampire_lore.quote: it was the same imperious gesture that I had seen used to the wolves

vampire_lore.rule: Vampires feed on infants
vampire_lore.detail: The women are given a bag with a living child.
vampire_lore.quote: Are we to have nothing to-night?

vampire_lore.rule: The Count's eyes glow red in anger
vampire_lore.detail: Lurid hell-fire light behind them.
vampire_lore.quote: The red light in them was lurid, as if the flames of hell-fire blazed behind them.

vampire_lore.rule: Active at night (nocturnal existence)
vampire_lore.detail: The Count's work is at night; Harker's own routine is being destroyed.
vampire_lore.quote: this nocturnal existence

vampire_lore.rule: Sleeps by day in earth-filled boxes
vampire_lore.detail: The Count is found in a box on freshly dug earth; the earthy smell is fresh.
vampire_lore.quote: on a pile of newly dug earth, lay the Count!

vampire_lore.rule: Deathlike sleep: eyes open, no pulse or breath, but warm
vampire_lore.detail: Open stony eyes, warm cheeks, red lips, no heartbeat.
vampire_lore.quote: no pulse, no breath, no beating of the heart

vampire_lore.rule: Feeding rejuvenates him
vampire_lore.detail: After feeding, hair turns dark iron-grey, cheeks fuller.
vampire_lore.quote: looking as if his youth had been half renewed

vampire_lore.rule: Wall-crawling
vampire_lore.detail: He descends the wall lizard-fashion, in Harker's clothes.
vampire_lore.quote: As he went down the wall, lizard fashion

vampire_lore.rule: Man-made weapons are ineffective (Harker's belief)
vampire_lore.detail: Harker thinks no weapon wrought by man alone would harm him; the shovel glances off.
vampire_lore.quote: no weapon wrought alone by man’s hand would have any effect on him

vampire_lore.rule: Paralysing gaze
vampire_lore.detail: His look makes the blade turn in Harker's hand.
vampire_lore.quote: The sight seemed to paralyse me, and the shovel turned in my hand

vampire_lore.rule: Moonlight hypnosis and moon-dust apparitions
vampire_lore.detail: The women's shapes materialise from moonbeam dust.
vampire_lore.quote: I was becoming hypnotised!

vampire_lore.rule: Cock-crow means safety from night threats
vampire_lore.detail: Morning and cock-crow bring relief.
vampire_lore.quote: Then came the welcome cock-crow, and I felt that I was safe.

vampire_lore.rule: Daylight he is not seen
vampire_lore.detail: Harker has never seen him in daylight and suspects he sleeps while others wake.
vampire_lore.quote: I have not yet seen the Count in the daylight.

vampire_lore.rule: Cannot be seen through locked-room routine; uses his own window and wall
vampire_lore.detail: He leaves by his window by night.
vampire_lore.quote: I saw the whole man emerge.

vampire_lore.rule: Lid nailed down for transport
vampire_lore.detail: The box with the body is nailed down by the carters.
vampire_lore.quote: There is a sound of hammering; it is the box being nailed down.

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire victims create semi-demons
vampire_lore.detail: The Count's purpose in London: create 'a new and ever-widening circle of semi-demons'.
vampire_lore.quote: create a new and ever-widening circle of semi-demons to batten on the helpless

vampire_lore.rule: Feeds on children
vampire_lore.detail: The mother's child taken in the bag.
vampire_lore.quote: I knew now what had become of her child

vampire_lore.rule: Renfield believes eating living things grants life
vampire_lore.detail: He eats a blow-fly and claims it is life, strong life; accumulates lives cumulatively.
vampire_lore.quote: it was life, strong life, and gave life to him

vampire_lore.rule: Lucy sleepwalks and seeks the key; the suicide's grave is her seat
vampire_lore.detail: Foreshadows nightly summoning; sleepwalking intensifies once the storm and ship approach.
vampire_lore.quote: even in her sleep she seems to be watching me

vampire_lore.rule: A suicide's grave on cliff edge
vampire_lore.detail: Folk belief of a bad burial; later site of Dracula's attacks (inferred).
vampire_lore.quote: I must go on sitting over the grave of a suicide.

vampire_lore.rule: Dracula travels in boxes of his native earth
vampire_lore.detail: The only cargo is great wooden boxes of mould, hidden in the hold, labelled clay.
vampire_lore.quote: a number of great wooden boxes filled with mould

vampire_lore.rule: Ordinary weapons pass through his shape
vampire_lore.detail: The mate's knife goes through It, 'empty as the air'.
vampire_lore.quote: the knife went through It, empty as the air

vampire_lore.rule: Holy objects are feared
vampire_lore.detail: The captain ties a crucifix with his hands to the wheel to keep It from touching him.
vampire_lore.quote: that which He—It!—dare not touch

vampire_lore.rule: Appears and vanishes through closed hatchways
vampire_lore.detail: The stranger leaves the deck with all hatches closed.
vampire_lore.quote: the hatchways were all closed

vampire_lore.rule: Controls weather: fog and storm accompany him
vampire_lore.detail: Fog moves with the ship; storm rises as it nears England.
vampire_lore.quote: the fog, which seems to move with us

vampire_lore.rule: Takes the form of an immense dog
vampire_lore.detail: A large dog leaps from the ship on landing and vanishes; the mastiff is torn (inferred identification).
vampire_lore.quote: an immense dog sprang up on deck

vampire_lore.rule: Kills his victims from the crew one per night
vampire_lore.detail: A man is lost after each watch, with no struggle recorded.
vampire_lore.quote: Like the first, he came off his watch and was not seen again.

vampire_lore.rule: Animals fear the suicide's grave / sense evil
vampire_lore.detail: The dog rages at the grave seat, then cowers when placed on the tombstone.
vampire_lore.quote: it became quiet and fell all into a tremble

vampire_lore.rule: Running water crossing at the harbour mouth
vampire_lore.detail: The ship only enters port when the wind shifts and drives it; the fog melts exactly then (weak inference, unstated).
vampire_lore.quote: the remnant of the sea-fog melted in the blast

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire feeds on sleepwalking victim from throat
vampire_lore.detail: Two tiny puncture marks, white-edged red centres, do not heal; victim weakens, pale, gasps.
vampire_lore.quote: They are like little white dots with red centres.

vampire_lore.rule: Victim is drawn to the vampire by a trance
vampire_lore.detail: Lucy walks asleep to the churchyard, sits at the window, points at it and remembers a dreamlike drowning feeling.
vampire_lore.quote: I only wanted to be here in this spot—I don't know why, for I was afraid of something.

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire appears with red eyes
vampire_lore.detail: Long dark figure with red gleaming eyes; Lucy: 'His red eyes again!'
vampire_lore.quote: His red eyes again! They are just the same.

vampire_lore.rule: Takes bat form
vampire_lore.detail: Great bat at the window in moonlight, bird-like shape on sill.
vampire_lore.quote: something that looked like a good-sized bird

vampire_lore.rule: Dogs howl in his presence
vampire_lore.detail: Dogs howl all over Whitby as Lucy climbs the steps.
vampire_lore.quote: I heard a lot of dogs howling

vampire_lore.rule: Moves at night under moon and cloud, vanishes in shadow
vampire_lore.detail: Disappears as clouds cover the moon; gone when Mina arrives.
vampire_lore.quote: shadow shut down on light almost immediately

vampire_lore.rule: His earth boxes must be placed in consecrated/ancient chapel soil of Carfax
vampire_lore.detail: Fifty boxes delivered to the ruined chapel of Carfax; Renfield haunts the chapel door.
vampire_lore.quote: the ancient chapel of the mansion

vampire_lore.rule: Servants (Renfield) feel the Master's approach
vampire_lore.detail: Renfield becomes haughty, sniffs, announces the Master is at hand, flees to the chapel.
vampire_lore.quote: the Master is at hand

vampire_lore.rule: Victim's blood loss shows as anaemia without anaemic cause
vampire_lore.detail: Mina notes Lucy fades though she eats, sleeps and breathes the fresh air.
vampire_lore.quote: She eats well and sleeps well, and enjoys the fresh air; but all the time the roses in her cheeks are fading

vampire_lore.rule: Marks have dreamy memory of sweet and bitter scent
vampire_lore.detail: Something very sweet and very bitter all around.
vampire_lore.quote: something very sweet and very bitter all around me at once

vampire_lore.rule: Renfield's moods follow moonrise/sunrise and noon/sunset
vampire_lore.detail: Calm from moonrise to sunrise, violent by day; later paroxysms at high noon and at sunset, suggesting a link to the Count's presence or waking.
vampire_lore.quote: Three nights has the same thing happened—violent all day then quiet from moonrise to sunrise.

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire can appear as a bat and act purposefully
vampire_lore.detail: A bat flying straight west controls Renfield's calm.
vampire_lore.quote: a big bat, which was flapping its silent and ghostly way to the west

vampire_lore.rule: Victim suffers sleepwalking, pallor, weakness and neck pain while normal tests find nothing
vampire_lore.detail: Lucy's blood is normal but she is bloodless in appearance.
vampire_lore.quote: My face is ghastly pale, and my throat pains me.

vampire_lore.rule: Scratching or flapping at the window at midnight precedes bad nights
vampire_lore.detail: Sign of the visitor.
vampire_lore.quote: There was a sort of scratching or flapping at the window

vampire_lore.rule: Two puncture wounds on the neck over the jugular
vampire_lore.detail: Edges white and worn as if by trituration; little visible blood loss on the bed.
vampire_lore.quote: the edges were white and worn-looking, as if by some trituration

vampire_lore.rule: Garlic repels the visitor
vampire_lore.detail: Rubbed on sashes, door jamb and fireplace so every breath of air carries garlic; also worn as wreath. Van Helsing hints it is a spell to keep out an evil spirit.
vampire_lore.quote: Perhaps I am!

vampire_lore.rule: Victim's sleep is where the weakness occurs
vampire_lore.detail: Lucy's weakness comes in sleep and she fears it; a watched night passes safely.
vampire_lore.quote: All this weakness comes to me in sleep

vampire_lore.rule: Victims must be kept sealed in room: no open window or door
vampire_lore.detail: The visitor enters via window (earlier scratching), so garlic and latches block it.
vampire_lore.quote: do not to-night open the window or the door.

vampire_lore.rule: Transfused blood is drained again
vampire_lore.detail: Arthur's blood only partly restored her, and it was gone by the next morning.
vampire_lore.quote: All our work is undone; we must begin again.

vampire_lore.rule: Control over wolves
vampire_lore.detail: Calms and commands wolves; Bersicker breaks out the night the stranger visits.
vampire_lore.quote: Old Bersicker kep' a-lookin' arter 'im till 'e was out of sight

vampire_lore.rule: Wolves and dogs howl at his coming
vampire_lore.detail: Howling at moonrise and dogs howling around the neighbourhood.
vampire_lore.quote: the wolves here all began a-'owling

vampire_lore.rule: Transformation into mist/specks
vampire_lore.detail: Specks wheeling like a dust-pillar enter by the broken window; lights burn blue.
vampire_lore.quote: the lights burn blue and dim

vampire_lore.rule: Garlic works when it stays in place
vampire_lore.detail: With the window sealed and garlic worn Lucy sleeps in peace; when removed, she is drained.
vampire_lore.quote: Four days and nights of peace.

vampire_lore.rule: Paralyzing spell on victim
vampire_lore.detail: Lucy cannot stir, as if under a spell.
vampire_lore.quote: there was some spell upon me

vampire_lore.rule: Appearance of the Count in London
vampire_lore.detail: Tall, thin, hooked nose, pointed beard with white hairs, red eyes, sharp teeth, white kid gloves.
vampire_lore.quote: He had a 'ard, cold look and red eyes

vampire_lore.rule: Blood is the life
vampire_lore.detail: Renfield's creed, tied to the Count's influence.
vampire_lore.quote: The blood is the life!

vampire_lore.rule: Mail to Carfax signals Count's property
vampire_lore.detail: Telegram sent to Carfax, Sussex only added by mistake; mentioned as a setback.
vampire_lore.quote: Sent to Carfax, Sussex, as no county given

vampire_lore.rule: Blood drained faster than it can be replaced
vampire_lore.detail: Four men's blood put into Lucy within ten days, none remains.
vampire_lore.quote: the blood of four strong men. Man alive, her whole body wouldn't hold it.

vampire_lore.rule: Wounds vanish at the point of vampiric change
vampire_lore.detail: The throat punctures disappear.
vampire_lore.quote: The wounds on the throat had absolutely disappeared.

vampire_lore.rule: Teeth lengthen, gums recede
vampire_lore.detail: Canines look longer and sharper in the vampire state.
vampire_lore.quote: the pale gums, drawn back, made the teeth look longer and sharper than ever

vampire_lore.rule: Dual state: sleep-vampire vs. waking self
vampire_lore.detail: Asleep she repels garlic and speaks voluptuously; awake she is herself and clutches it.
vampire_lore.quote: she put the flowers from her; but that when she waked she clutched them close

vampire_lore.rule: Kiss from the victim is dangerous
vampire_lore.detail: Lucy's seductive plea to Arthur; Van Helsing hurls him back.
vampire_lore.quote: Not for your life! not for your living soul and hers!

vampire_lore.rule: Locked houses and drugged servants
vampire_lore.detail: The attack is helped by drugged servants and an opened window; bars and locks protect but wolf breaks glass.
vampire_lore.quote: Every window and door was fastened and locked

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire servant madman senses master and boxes
vampire_lore.detail: Renfield reacts violently to the cart carrying boxes; 'my Lord and Master'.
vampire_lore.quote: I'll fight for my Lord and Master!

vampire_lore.rule: Moonlight and bats
vampire_lore.detail: The bat returns on full-moon nights.
vampire_lore.quote: There was a full moonlight

vampire_lore.rule: Death does not end it
vampire_lore.detail: Van Helsing: Lucy's death is only the beginning.
vampire_lore.quote: Not so; alas! not so. It is only the beginning!

vampire_lore.rule: Garlic is placed around a suspected vampire's body.
vampire_lore.detail: Van Helsing scatters wild garlic among the flowers and in the coffin.
vampire_lore.quote: placed the flowers amongst the others on and around the bed.

vampire_lore.rule: Crucifix on the mouth of the dead.
vampire_lore.detail: A gold crucifix is laid over Lucy's mouth.
vampire_lore.quote: placed it over the mouth.

vampire_lore.rule: Beheading and heart removal are the cure for the bitten dead.
vampire_lore.detail: Van Helsing's stated plan; not carried out yet.
vampire_lore.quote: I want to cut off her head and take out her heart.

vampire_lore.rule: Vampires' victims keep unnatural beauty after death.
vampire_lore.detail: Lucy's face grows more beautiful hours after death.
vampire_lore.quote: Every hour seemed to be enhancing her loveliness.

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire can grow younger.
vampire_lore.detail: Jonathan sees the Count rejuvenated in London.
vampire_lore.quote: I believe it is the Count, but he has grown young.

vampire_lore.rule: Bitten victims show small throat punctures.
vampire_lore.detail: Children have slight torn wounds in the throat, like rat or small dog bites.
vampire_lore.quote: slightly torn or wounded in the throat.

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire wounds are small punctures in the throat.
vampire_lore.detail: Seward sees the Gazette description and recognises Lucy's wounds.
vampire_lore.quote: small punctured wounds on their throats.

vampire_lore.rule: Victims die of blood loss or waste.
vampire_lore.detail: Lucy died of nervous prostration after great loss of blood; four men's blood could not save her for one more day.
vampire_lore.quote: with four men’s blood in her poor veins, could not live even one day

vampire_lore.rule: Some beings live far beyond natural age.
vampire_lore.detail: Methuselah, Old Parr, the tortoise, the elephant, the parrot, men and women who cannot die.
vampire_lore.quote: there are men and women who cannot die?

vampire_lore.rule: Sleep-walking is the vampire's opening.
vampire_lore.detail: Mina's Whitby journal ties Lucy's sleep-walking to the cliff night.
vampire_lore.quote: in that diary she traces by inference certain things to a sleep-walking

vampire_lore.rule: The Un-Dead look more beautiful than the dead.
vampire_lore.detail: Lucy in coffin: red lips, bloom, sharper teeth.
vampire_lore.quote: The lips were red, nay redder than before

vampire_lore.rule: Sharp canines are used to bite.
vampire_lore.detail: Van Helsing shows the canine teeth.
vampire_lore.quote: they are even sharper than before

vampire_lore.rule: The Un-Dead can only move at sundown and must return.
vampire_lore.detail: Van Helsing spent time before sundown and guarded.
vampire_lore.quote: for at sundown the Un-Dead can move

vampire_lore.rule: Lucy was bitten while in a trance.
vampire_lore.detail: The vampire takes blood best during sleep-walking; she died in trance.
vampire_lore.quote: in trance could he best come to take more blood

vampire_lore.rule: Kill: behead, garlic mouth, stake.
vampire_lore.detail: Van Helsing's plan; kill Un-Dead in sleep.
vampire_lore.quote: I shall cut off her head and fill her mouth with garlic, and I shall drive a stake through her body.

vampire_lore.rule: Garlic and crucifix keep Un-Dead from leaving; they may fail against one trying to enter.
vampire_lore.detail: Van Helsing: desperate Un-Dead find the line of least resistance.
vampire_lore.quote: these are only to prevent her coming out

vampire_lore.rule: Master vampire strength of twenty men; can summon a wolf.
vampire_lore.detail: From Harker's journals.
vampire_lore.quote: He can summon his wolf and I know not what.

vampire_lore.rule: Master vampire slain by beheading plus burning heart or stake.
vampire_lore.detail: Instruction to Seward.
vampire_lore.quote: cut off his head and burn his heart or drive a stake through it

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire must be at 'home' in coffin during sleep.
vampire_lore.detail: The Un-Dead sleep at home, face shows what they are.
vampire_lore.quote: when the Un-Dead sleep at home

vampire_lore.rule: Crucifix halts the Un-Dead.
vampire_lore.detail: Lucy recoils and cannot move past the lifted crucifix.
vampire_lore.quote: She recoiled from it

vampire_lore.rule: Host seal bars the tomb entrance.
vampire_lore.detail: Strips of Host and putty stop Lucy from entering her tomb; removing it lets her slip through a crack.
vampire_lore.quote: I am closing the tomb, so that the Un-Dead may not enter.

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire can pass through a crevice in corporeal form.
vampire_lore.detail: Lucy enters through a gap scarcely wide enough for a knife-blade.
vampire_lore.quote: with a corporeal body as real at that moment as our own

vampire_lore.rule: Garlic on the clamps prevents leaving.
vampire_lore.detail: Previous night nothing appeared.
vampire_lore.quote: garlic, which the Un-Dead cannot bear

vampire_lore.rule: At sundown the Un-Dead can move.
vampire_lore.detail: Van Helsing arrives before sundown.
vampire_lore.quote: for at sundown the Un-Dead can move

vampire_lore.rule: Victims of the Un-Dead become Un-Dead.
vampire_lore.detail: Circle widens like ripples; nosferatu.
vampire_lore.quote: all that die from the preying of the Un-Dead becomes themselves Un-Dead

vampire_lore.rule: Killing the vampire frees the victims and their souls.
vampire_lore.detail: Throat wounds disappear and the soul is freed.
vampire_lore.quote: if she die in truth, then all cease

vampire_lore.rule: Stake through heart, head cut off, mouth filled with garlic.
vampire_lore.detail: Performed with prayer; the true face returns.
vampire_lore.quote: Then we cut off the head and filled the mouth with garlic.

vampire_lore.rule: Vampires are mesmerising and seductive to the loved one.
vampire_lore.detail: Arthur is under a spell when she calls.
vampire_lore.quote: he seemed under a spell

vampire_lore.rule: The Un-Dead lies in her coffin by day; face shows corrupted nature by night.
vampire_lore.detail: Pointed teeth and bloodstained mouth by candlelight.
vampire_lore.quote: the pointed teeth, the bloodstained, voluptuous mouth

vampire_lore.rule: Renfield's moods are linked to the Count's proximity
vampire_lore.detail: All his outbreaks correlate with the Count's presence; calm may mean satisfied instinct.
vampire_lore.quote: All those outbreaks were in some way linked with the proximity of the Count.

vampire_lore.rule: The Count prepares meticulously
vampire_lore.detail: He prepared for every obstacle and 'took no chances'.
vampire_lore.quote: he had “taken no chances,”

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire lair is disused, foul and dusty
vampire_lore.detail: Carfax untouched for a century, chapel smells terrible, men flee after dark.
vampire_lore.quote: the ole chapel—that took the cike, that did!

vampire_lore.rule: Strength of twenty men
vampire_lore.detail: Cannot be hurt by mere strength; a stronger body of men can hold him only at certain times.
vampire_lore.quote: This vampire which is amongst us is of himself so strong in person as twenty men

vampire_lore.rule: Necromancy and command of the dead and animals
vampire_lore.detail: Commands rat, owl, bat, moth, fox, wolf and the elements.
vampire_lore.quote: he can command all the meaner things: the rat, and the owl, and the bat—the moth, and the fox, and the wolf

vampire_lore.rule: Shape changes
vampire_lore.detail: Wolf (Whitby dog), bat (Whitby window, Lucy's window), mist round himself only, moonlight dust, can grow small to slip hairbreadth gaps.
vampire_lore.quote: He can transform himself to wolf, as we gather from the ship arrival in Whitby, when he tear open the dog

vampire_lore.rule: Sees in the dark
vampire_lore.detail: No small power in a half-dark world.
vampire_lore.quote: He can see in the dark—no small power this

vampire_lore.rule: Feeds on blood and grows younger
vampire_lore.detail: Does not eat other food; plentiful blood refreshes him.
vampire_lore.quote: he can even grow younger

vampire_lore.rule: No shadow or reflection
vampire_lore.detail: Throws no shadow, no mirror image.
vampire_lore.quote: He throws no shadow; he make in the mirror no reflect

vampire_lore.rule: Must be invited in the first time
vampire_lore.detail: After that he can enter as he pleases.
vampire_lore.quote: He may not enter anywhere at the first, unless there be some one of the household who bid him to come

vampire_lore.rule: Power ceases at day
vampire_lore.detail: Away from his earth-home he can change only at noon, exact sunrise or sunset.
vampire_lore.quote: His power ceases, as does that of all evil things, at the coming of the day.

vampire_lore.rule: Running water crossing
vampire_lore.detail: He can pass running water only at slack or flood of the tide.
vampire_lore.quote: he can only pass running water at the slack or the flood of the tide

vampire_lore.rule: Garlic and sacred things
vampire_lore.detail: Garlic afflicts him; in presence of a crucifix he stays far off and silent.
vampire_lore.quote: in their presence he take his place far off and silent with respect.

vampire_lore.rule: Wild rose, sacred bullet, stake, beheading
vampire_lore.detail: Rose confines him to coffin; sacred bullet fired into coffin kills; stake or cut-off head gives rest.
vampire_lore.quote: a sacred bullet fired into the coffin kill him so that he be true dead

vampire_lore.rule: Needs his earth/coffin-home and unhallowed ground
vampire_lore.detail: Cannot rest in soil of holy memories; graves of his good descendants sanctify the earth where he can dwell.
vampire_lore.quote: in soil barren of holy memories it cannot rest.

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire origin: Voivode Dracula, Scholomance
vampire_lore.detail: Dracula family learned secrets in the Scholomance above Lake Hermanstadt where the devil claims the tenth scholar.
vampire_lore.quote: where the devil claims the tenth scholar as his due.

vampire_lore.rule: Best time to strike: noon to sunset
vampire_lore.detail: Find him in man form between noon and sunset.
vampire_lore.quote: we may find him in his form of man between the hours of noon and sunset

vampire_lore.rule: Animals obey him but are not immune to ordinary foes
vampire_lore.detail: Rats flee from small dogs; his spiritual power does not shield them.
vampire_lore.quote: the brute beasts which are to the Count’s command are yet themselves not amenable to his spiritual power

vampire_lore.rule: Count can handle earth boxes himself
vampire_lore.detail: (Chapter 20 confirms); here boxes were taken out by the door where dust was disturbed.
vampire_lore.quote: the boxes which had been taken out had been brought this way.

vampire_lore.rule: Fog and mist as entry
vampire_lore.detail: Mist enters via the door joins; Mina's dream foreshadows his access.
vampire_lore.quote: pouring in, not through the window, but through the joinings of the door.

vampire_lore.rule: Lair's air is corrupt
vampire_lore.detail: The stench of the Count's resting place is unbearable.
vampire_lore.quote: corruption had become itself corrupt.

vampire_lore.rule: Eyes glow red
vampire_lore.detail: Two red eyes in the mist.
vampire_lore.quote: the fire divided, and seemed to shine on me through the fog like two red eyes

vampire_lore.rule: Count can move earth boxes himself
vampire_lore.detail: He lifts them as if light and travels ahead of the carter.
vampire_lore.quote: the Count could, it was evident, handle the earth-boxes himself.

vampire_lore.rule: Count distributes lairs across London
vampire_lore.detail: Boxes sent east, south and Piccadilly; plan likely covers all quarters.
vampire_lore.quote: The north and west were surely never meant to be left out of his diabolical scheme

vampire_lore.rule: Alias and cash purchase
vampire_lore.detail: Uses the name Count de Ville, pays in notes.
vampire_lore.quote: paying the purchase money in notes ‘over the counter,’

vampire_lore.rule: Sterilise earth between sunrise and sunset
vampire_lore.detail: Catch him at weakest without refuge.
vampire_lore.quote: We must sterilise all the imported earth between sunrise and sunset

vampire_lore.rule: Renfield's cravings link to Count
vampire_lore.detail: His changes follow the Count's doings; the Count has promised him a higher life.
vampire_lore.quote: His moods have so followed the doings of the Count

vampire_lore.rule: Casts little shadow
vampire_lore.detail: The thin old man could 'hardly throw a shadder'.
vampire_lore.quote: you would think he couldn’t throw a shadder.

vampire_lore.rule: The vampire is stopped by the Sacred Wafer and crucifixes
vampire_lore.detail: The Count halts and cowers when the Wafer is held out and crucifixes raised together.
vampire_lore.quote: The Count suddenly stopped, just as poor Lucy had done outside the tomb, and cowered back.

vampire_lore.rule: The vampire can become mist and slide under or through gaps
vampire_lore.detail: He enters through a window open one inch and leaves as vapour under a door.
vampire_lore.quote: He slid into the room through the sash, though it was only open an inch wide

vampire_lore.rule: The vampire must be invited in
vampire_lore.detail: The Count begins to ask Renfield, who finally says 'Come in, Lord and Master!' and opens the window.
vampire_lore.quote: I found myself opening the sash and saying to Him: ‘Come in, Lord and Master!’

vampire_lore.rule: Vampires can command animals
vampire_lore.detail: He sends flies, moths, rats and dogs and controls the mist.
vampire_lore.quote: He raised his hands, and seemed to call out without using any words.

vampire_lore.rule: Hypnotic stupor on sleepers
vampire_lore.detail: Jonathan lies in a stupor the vampire can produce; cold water flicked on his face rouses him.
vampire_lore.quote: Jonathan is in a stupor such as we know the Vampire can produce.

vampire_lore.rule: The vampire's gaze overwhelms the strong
vampire_lore.detail: Renfield's strength turns to water when he meets the Count's eyes.
vampire_lore.quote: They burned into me, and my strength became like water.

vampire_lore.rule: Blood exchange binds the victim to the vampire's call
vampire_lore.detail: Count opens a vein on his breast and makes Mina drink so she must answer his mental summons across land and sea.
vampire_lore.quote: When my brain says “Come!” to you, you shall cross land or sea to do my bidding

vampire_lore.rule: The vampire's touch dulls the victim's will
vampire_lore.detail: Mina does not want to resist while he bites.
vampire_lore.quote: I did not want to hinder him. I suppose it is a part of the horrible curse

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire departs before dawn
vampire_lore.detail: Quincey reasons he will not return that night because the east is reddening.
vampire_lore.quote: He will not be back to-night; for the sky is reddening in the east

vampire_lore.rule: The vampire has a changed smell and a drained victim shows paleness
vampire_lore.detail: Renfield notes the Count smelled different; Mina looked pale and bloodless the afternoon before.
vampire_lore.quote: I don’t care for the pale people; I like them with lots of blood in them, and hers had all seemed to have run out.

vampire_lore.rule: By day the vampire is confined to his earthly form
vampire_lore.detail: Until sunset he cannot melt into air or pass through cracks and must open doors like a mortal.
vampire_lore.quote: Until it sets to-night, that monster must retain whatever form he now has.

vampire_lore.rule: Earth-boxes can be sterilised with the Host
vampire_lore.detail: A piece of Sacred Wafer on the soil makes the box useless to him.
vampire_lore.quote: We must sterilise this earth, so sacred of holy memories

vampire_lore.rule: A fed vampire sleeps late
vampire_lore.detail: After heavy feeding the Count sleeps late, giving the party a window.
vampire_lore.quote: last night he banqueted heavily, and will sleep late?

vampire_lore.rule: Sacred objects burn the marked
vampire_lore.detail: The Wafer sears Mina's forehead, showing she is tainted.
vampire_lore.quote: it had seared it—had burned into the flesh as though it had been a piece of white-hot metal.

vampire_lore.rule: The Count has many lairs and keeps documents
vampire_lore.detail: He holds deeds, keys and paper at the central Piccadilly house.
vampire_lore.quote: The Count may have many houses which he has bought.

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire's lair smells vile
vampire_lore.detail: The Piccadilly house smells like the Carfax chapel.
vampire_lore.quote: It did indeed smell vilely—like the old chapel at Carfax

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire victims develop sharper teeth and thin
vampire_lore.detail: Mina's teeth show prominently; no sharpening yet.
vampire_lore.quote: As yet there was no sign of the teeth growing sharper

vampire_lore.rule: Vampirism spreads through love
vampire_lore.detail: Harker reflects that one vampire meant many through love.
vampire_lore.quote: the holiest love was the recruiting sergeant for their ghastly ranks.

vampire_lore.rule: The Count in life was soldier, statesman and alchemist who attended the Scholomance
vampire_lore.detail: His brain survived death and grows; memory incomplete; child-brain.
vampire_lore.quote: in him the brain powers survived the physical death; though it would seem that memory was not all complete.

vampire_lore.rule: A vampire must be invited the first time
vampire_lore.detail: After the first invitation he may come when and how he will.
vampire_lore.quote: must at the first make entry only when asked thereto by an inmate.

vampire_lore.rule: The Count learns by experiment, moves boxes himself, scatters graves
vampire_lore.detail: Initially others moved them; now he moves alone and may bury them.
vampire_lore.quote: he try to move them all alone.

vampire_lore.rule: By day before sunset the Count may not change form
vampire_lore.detail: Till sunset he is limited to man's powers.
vampire_lore.quote: till sunset he may not change.

vampire_lore.rule: He can cross running water only at slack or full tide
vampire_lore.detail: Van Helsing deduces he crossed the river at slack tide; a ship must touch land at tide.
vampire_lore.quote: he could only do so at slack of tide

vampire_lore.rule: Holy symbols repel in a shared gesture
vampire_lore.detail: Holding Crucifix and Wafer sends a mighty power along the arm and makes him cower.
vampire_lore.quote: I felt a mighty power fly along my arm

vampire_lore.rule: A bitten victim sees through his senses in trance
vampire_lore.detail: Under hypnosis Mina perceives the ship around the Count; strongest at sunrise.
vampire_lore.quote: I do not know. Sleep has no place it can call its own.

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire is helpless at the moment of daylight transit
vampire_lore.detail: The Count is 'still' like death in his box aboard ship (Mina's trance) as the sun rises.
vampire_lore.quote: I am still—oh, so still. It is like death!

vampire_lore.rule: Blade can harm him
vampire_lore.detail: The kukri would have cut through his heart had he not leaped back; its effect is untested.
vampire_lore.quote: A second less and the trenchant blade had shorne through his heart.

vampire_lore.rule: The Count seeks to return to his castle and uses ships
vampire_lore.detail: He needs earth-box and sea passage, cannot cross water except as ship reaches land at full or slack tide.
vampire_lore.quote: for there are waters between us which he do not want to pass

vampire_lore.rule: Wild rose on the box prevents emerging
vampire_lore.detail: A fastened wild-rose branch keeps him in, per superstition.
vampire_lore.quote: when it is there none can emerge; so at least says the superstition.

vampire_lore.rule: Best time to attack is in the box between sunrise and sunset
vampire_lore.detail: In the box by day he can make no struggle.
vampire_lore.quote: Our best hope is to come on him when in the box between sunrise and sunset

vampire_lore.rule: Weather control: fog at his command
vampire_lore.detail: Could shorten the voyage by about two days.
vampire_lore.quote: our enemy is on the sea, with the fog at his command

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire's baptism of blood causes transformation and mental link
vampire_lore.detail: Mina grows sharper teeth and hard eyes, falls silent; may be compelled to disclose what she knows.
vampire_lore.quote: I can see the characteristics of the vampire coming in her face.

vampire_lore.rule: The Count can summon victims mentally
vampire_lore.detail: When he wills, Mina must go, even by guile.
vampire_lore.quote: I know that when the Count wills me I must go.

vampire_lore.rule: Sunrise and sunset open a window of clarity for Mina
vampire_lore.detail: She can speak freely only as the sun rises; uneasiness at sunset.
vampire_lore.quote: I can tell you now, whilst the sun is coming up; I may not be able again.

vampire_lore.rule: A sacred wafer scar remains while the vampire lives
vampire_lore.detail: The red scar stays on Mina's forehead.
vampire_lore.quote: Whilst that lasts, there can be no disbelief.

vampire_lore.rule: The Count's power derives from his homeland's occult geology
vampire_lore.detail: Caverns, fissures, volcanic springs and gases, magnetic or electric forces.
vampire_lore.quote: There are deep caverns and fissures that reach none know whither.

vampire_lore.rule: He cannot pass running water except at tide
vampire_lore.detail: Safe to rest while he is on the sea.
vampire_lore.quote: he be not in the same land with us.

vampire_lore.rule: Mina's twilight freedom
vampire_lore.detail: A half hour or more before sunrise/sunset she is free of the Count's influence; she then falls into hypnosis easily.
vampire_lore.quote: sunrise and sunset are to her times of peculiar freedom

vampire_lore.rule: Killing a vampire requires stake and beheading
vampire_lore.detail: Stake through the heart and cut off the head; body falls to dust soon after.
vampire_lore.quote: drive a stake through me and cut off my head

vampire_lore.rule: Cannot cross running water unaided
vampire_lore.detail: Even as a bat he can't leave the ship on his own will.
vampire_lore.quote: cannot cross the running water of his own volition

vampire_lore.rule: Helpless in the box during day
vampire_lore.detail: After sunrise the box can be opened and he is at their mercy before he wakes.
vampire_lore.quote: If, then, we can come on board after sunrise, he is at our mercy

vampire_lore.rule: Sharpening teeth indicate vampirism
vampire_lore.detail: Van Helsing checks Mina's teeth under hypnosis; as long as they do not sharpen there is no active danger.
vampire_lore.quote: so long as they do not begin to sharpen there is no active danger of a change in her.

vampire_lore.rule: Blood bond lets Mina sense the Count
vampire_lore.detail: The 'baptism of blood' gives her a link that works under Van Helsing's will at dawn/dusk.
vampire_lore.quote: That terrible baptism of blood which he give you makes you free to go to him in spirit

vampire_lore.rule: Count can cut her off
vampire_lore.detail: He can withdraw from her mind and see through her trance.
vampire_lore.quote: he cut her off—take her, as he can do, out of his own power

vampire_lore.rule: Mind of a habitual criminal
vampire_lore.detail: The Count repeats strategies: flee home then return stronger.
vampire_lore.quote: he be of child-brain in much

vampire_lore.rule: Fog accompanies the Count's ship
vampire_lore.detail: Fog fell on the ship and travelled with it for five days, giving a favourable wind and fast passage.
vampire_lore.quote: a fog fell on us and travelled wi’ us

vampire_lore.rule: Evil eye gesture
vampire_lore.detail: Roumanian sailors put out two fingers at the old man who loaded the box.
vampire_lore.quote: put out their twa fingers when they saw him, to guard against the evil eye.

vampire_lore.rule: Count powerless by water in day
vampire_lore.detail: On water he is helpless except at night, can summon fog, storm, snow, wolves.
vampire_lore.quote: he can only summon fog and storm and snow and his wolves.

vampire_lore.rule: Wrecked in running water he'd be lost
vampire_lore.detail: Living water would engulf him.
vampire_lore.quote: the living water would engulf him, helpless

vampire_lore.rule: Cannot leave box in day without risking carriers
vampire_lore.detail: If carriers suspect they would throw him in the stream.
vampire_lore.quote: he may not leave his box lest those who carry him may suspect

vampire_lore.rule: Trance power waning
vampire_lore.detail: Mina's trance grows hard; at dawn the sun forces her out.
vampire_lore.quote: the risen sun was reddening even Mrs. Harker’s pale face.

vampire_lore.rule: Mina's scar forbids carrying a holy weapon
vampire_lore.detail: She cannot carry the same arms as others.
vampire_lore.quote: the scar on my forehead forbids that.

vampire_lore.rule: Count needs to be carried to land
vampire_lore.detail: If not carried ashore at night he can fly or jump; else lose the day.
vampire_lore.quote: he can jump or fly on shore, as he did at Whitby.

vampire_lore.rule: Holy circle of wafer protects
vampire_lore.detail: Vampires cannot enter the ring; the tainted Mina cannot leave it.
vampire_lore.quote: which she could not leave no more than they could enter.

vampire_lore.rule: Host wafer in a tomb banishes a vampire permanently
vampire_lore.detail: Placed in Dracula's tomb so he cannot return.
vampire_lore.quote: I laid in Dracula’s tomb some of the Wafer, and so banished him from it, Un-Dead, for ever.

vampire_lore.rule: Vampires materialise from mist and snow
vampire_lore.detail: Brides take shape from snow flurries and mist at night.
vampire_lore.quote: the snow-flurries and the wreaths of mist took shape as of women with trailing garments.

vampire_lore.rule: Vampires' beauty hypnotises hunters
vampire_lore.detail: Staring at sleeping vampires paralyses the will; delay until sunset is fatal.
vampire_lore.quote: the mere beauty and the fascination of the wanton Un-Dead have hypnotise him

vampire_lore.rule: Staking and beheading destroys them; bodies crumble
vampire_lore.detail: Stake drives with screeching, head cut, body turns to dust; face shows peace.
vampire_lore.quote: the whole body began to melt away and crumble in to its native dust

vampire_lore.rule: Mina's hypnosis fails nearer the castle and she becomes drowsy by day
vampire_lore.detail: Increasing vampire taint; sleeps in day, wakes bright at night, refuses food, eats alone.
vampire_lore.quote: the power has grown less and less with each day

vampire_lore.rule: Fire and wood as defence
vampire_lore.detail: Van Helsing advances with firewood and wafer; they draw back laughing.
vampire_lore.quote: They drew back before me, and laughed their low horrid laugh.

vampire_lore.rule: Animals sense vampires
vampire_lore.detail: Horses scream, cower, and die of fear; calmed by human touch.
vampire_lore.quote: the horses began to scream, and tore at their tethers

vampire_lore.rule: Sunset frees the Count
vampire_lore.detail: At sunset the Count in his box takes new freedom and can elude pursuit.
vampire_lore.quote: at sunset the Thing, which was till then imprisoned there, would take new freedom

vampire_lore.rule: Death of the Count removes Mina's mark
vampire_lore.detail: When Dracula dies the scar vanishes.
vampire_lore.quote: the snow is not more stainless than her forehead! The curse has passed away!

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire lairs have sulphurous odour
vampire_lore.detail: Horrid odour in the chapel.
vampire_lore.quote: some sulphurous fume, which at times made me dizzy.

scenes.title: Rail journey to Klausenburgh
scenes.location: Train Munich - Vienna - Buda-Pesth - Klausenburgh; Hotel Royale
scenes.summary: Harker travels east, notes the Danube bridges and the feeling of leaving the West, and eats paprika hendl at the Hotel Royale.
scenes.key_quote: The impression I had was that we were leaving the West and entering the East

scenes.title: Night at Hotel Royale and morning train
scenes.time: night of 3 May to morning of 4 May
scenes.summary: A dog howls under his window all night; thirsty from paprika he drains the carafe. Breakfast of mamaliga and impletata; the late train dawdles through hill country with castles and flooded riverbeds; stations full of costumed peasants and Slovaks.
scenes.key_quote: There was a dog howling all night under my window

scenes.title: Arrival at Bistritz and the Golden Krone
scenes.summary: At twilight Harker reaches the old frontier town, is greeted by the landlady who hands over Dracula's letter announcing the diligence at three next day and a carriage at the Borgo Pass.
scenes.mood: quaint, expectant, first hint of strangeness
scenes.key_quote: Welcome to the Carpathians. I am anxiously expecting you.

scenes.title: The landlady's warning and the crucifix
scenes.summary: The couple cross themselves at the Count's name and refuse to speak. The landlady kneels, explains it is the eve of St. George's Day when evil has full sway at midnight, and forces her crucifix and rosary on him.
scenes.key_quote: Do you not know that to-night, when the clock strikes midnight, all the evil things in the world will have full sway?

scenes.title: The inn-yard crowd and the coach departs
scenes.location: Inn-yard of the Golden Krone, with oleander and orange trees in tubs
scenes.summary: Harker overhears words like Ordog, pokol, stregoica, vrolok and vlkoslak; the crowd crosses itself and points two fingers at him against the evil eye as the four-horse coach leaves.
scenes.key_quote: all made the sign of the cross and pointed two fingers towards me

scenes.title: Drive through the Mittel Land and into the Carpathians
scenes.location: Mittel Land road to Borgo Pass
scenes.summary: Orchards in bloom, pine woods like tongues of flame, snowy peaks, wayside crosses and shrines, hay-ricks in trees, leiter-wagons. The driver refuses to let Harker walk because of fierce dogs and rushes the horses.
scenes.key_quote: No, no, you must not walk here; the dogs are too fierce

scenes.title: Gifts of protection in the Borgo Pass
scenes.summary: As darkness falls the passengers urge the driver faster and press odd gifts on Harker with blessings. The pass opens under thundery clouds; there is no carriage waiting and the driver says to go on to Bukovina.
scenes.key_quote: It seemed as though the mountain range had separated two atmospheres

scenes.title: The Count's calèche arrives
scenes.summary: Horses scream and plunge as a calèche with four coal-black horses overtakes the coach. The tall bearded driver with red-glinting eyes, sharp white teeth and steel grip takes Harker's bags; a passenger murmurs the Lenore line about the dead travelling fast.
scenes.key_quote: Denn die Todten reiten schnell

scenes.title: Circling drive and midnight howling
scenes.location: Roads of the Pass, in the calèche
scenes.summary: Cloak and rug, a flask of slivovitz under the seat. The carriage seems to double back over the same ground. At midnight dogs howl, then wolves; the driver soothes the panicked horses with whispers and then turns down a narrow road under arching trees as snow begins.
scenes.key_quote: it was within a few minutes of midnight

scenes.title: Blue flames and the ring of wolves
scenes.location: Narrow wooded road and rocky ground beside the Pass
scenes.summary: Faint blue flames appear; the driver stops, vanishes into the dark and arranges stones into a device (the flame does not flicker when he stands in front of it). Later wolves ring the carriage in silence; Harker shouts and beats the calèche; the driver stands in the road and sweeps his arms, and the wolves fall back and vanish.
scenes.key_quote: As he swept his long arms, as though brushing aside some impalpable obstacle, the wolves fell back and back further still.

scenes.title: Arrival at the ruined castle
scenes.summary: The carriage climbs steadily and halts in the courtyard of a vast ruined castle with tall black windows and broken battlements.
scenes.key_quote: a vast ruined castle, from whose tall black windows came no ray of light

scenes.title: Waiting at the great door
scenes.location: Castle courtyard and great studded door
scenes.summary: Harker, dazed, stands before a worn carved stone doorway with no bell or knocker and reflects on being a newly qualified solicitor.
scenes.key_quote: Of bell or knocker there was no sign

scenes.title: The Count opens the door
scenes.location: Entry hall and passage of Castle Dracula
scenes.summary: Chains, bolts and a long-unused key; an old man in black with an antique silver lamp invites him to enter of his own will, grips his hand with icy strength, and carries his luggage up the winding stair.
scenes.key_quote: Welcome to my house! Enter freely and of your own will!

scenes.title: Supper by the fire
scenes.summary: Harker hands over Mr. Hawkins's letter, eats roast chicken, cheese, salad and old Tokay, smokes a cigar; the Count does not eat. Harker studies the Count's features, notices hairy palms, long pointed nails, rank breath and a wave of nausea. Wolves howl and the Count calls them children of the night.
scenes.key_quote: Listen to them—the children of the night. What music they make!

scenes.title: Day in the empty castle; the library
scenes.time: 7 May, between five and six o'clock
scenes.summary: Harker finds a cold breakfast and a note, gold table service, no mirrors, no servants, no bell. In the library he finds English books; the Count enters and asks Harker to teach him English intonation, permits him to roam except behind locked doors.
scenes.key_quote: You may go anywhere you wish in the castle, except where the doors are locked

scenes.title: Blue flames explained
scenes.summary: The Count explains blue flames mark hidden treasure on one night a year, and tells how patriots hid treasure in the soil fought over by Wallachian, Saxon and Turk.
scenes.key_quote: a blue flame is seen over any place where treasure has been concealed

scenes.title: The Carfax purchase
