scenes.summary: Plans and deeds are signed; Harker reads aloud his description of Carfax at Purfleet. The Count approves of the old chapel and gloom. Harker finds an atlas with rings at London, Exeter and Whitby. Cockcrow ends the evening.
scenes.key_quote: I am glad that it is old and big.

scenes.title: The shaving glass
scenes.summary: Count appears behind Harker without reflection; Harker cuts himself, the Count lunges at his throat, touches the crucifix cord and changes; he hurls the mirror from the window.
scenes.key_quote: But there was no reflection of him in the mirror!

scenes.title: Discovering the prison
scenes.location: Castle stairs, south room with precipice view
scenes.summary: Harker explores, sees a thousand-foot drop and endless forest from a south room, and finds every door locked and bolted.
scenes.key_quote: The castle is a veritable prison, and I am a prisoner!

scenes.title: Realising he is a prisoner
scenes.summary: Harker rushes about trying every door, then calms and decides to keep his knowledge secret and watch.
scenes.key_quote: I behaved much as a rat does in a trap.

scenes.title: The Count does the housework
scenes.summary: Through a hinge-chink Harker watches the Count make the bed and lay the table, proving there are no servants and that the Count was the coachman. He recalls the wards given at Bistritz.
scenes.key_quote: it must have been the Count himself who was the driver of the coach that brought me here

scenes.title: The Count tells his family history
scenes.summary: Excited, the Count speaks as if he fought at every battle, tracing the Szekelys back to Attila and the Dracula voivode who beat the Turks; he pulls his moustache and grips things as if to crush them.
scenes.key_quote: What devil or what witch was ever so great as Attila, whose blood is in these veins?

scenes.title: Legal questions and the letters
scenes.summary: The Count quizzes Harker on using several solicitors for banking and shipping to Newcastle, Durham, Harwich and Dover, then insists he stay a month and write reassuring letters on thin foreign paper.
scenes.key_quote: write now, my young friend

scenes.title: Spying on the letters; the warning
scenes.summary: Alone, Harker reads the addresses of four letters. The Count returns, stamps them, and warns him never to sleep in any other part of the castle.
scenes.key_quote: there are bad dreams for those who sleep unwisely. Be warned!

scenes.title: The Count crawls down the wall
scenes.location: South stone stair window; castle wall
scenes.summary: From a tall mullioned window Harker sees the Count emerge from his own window and crawl face-down down the sheer wall, cloak spread like wings, like a lizard.
scenes.key_quote: begin to crawl down the castle wall over that dreadful abyss, face down with his cloak spreading out around him like great wings

scenes.title: Exploring the castle; the great door
scenes.summary: Harker sees the Count go out again, tests all doors (new locks), finds the hall door's bolts and chains easy but the door locked with key gone, and some small rooms of moth-eaten furniture.
scenes.key_quote: the door was locked, and the key was gone!

scenes.title: The sunken door and the ladies' rooms
scenes.summary: A seemingly locked door at the top of the stairs is only jammed, its fallen hinges resting on the floor; Harker forces it and enters a suite of south and west rooms with diamond-paned windows and comfortable old furniture.
scenes.key_quote: This was evidently the portion of the castle occupied by the ladies in bygone days

scenes.title: The three women
scenes.location: The ladies' room, on a great couch
scenes.summary: Harker sleeps against the warning. Three women with no shadows appear; the fair one kneels to bite his throat. The Count seizes her neck, flings her back, claims Harker and gives them a living bag. Harker faints.
scenes.key_quote: This man belongs to me!

scenes.title: Waking in his own bed
scenes.summary: Harker notices folded clothes, an unwound watch, intact pockets; he decides the room is a sanctuary compared to the women.
scenes.key_quote: My watch was still unwound

scenes.title: The sealed room
scenes.location: Top of the stairs, south wing door
scenes.summary: The door to the ladies' rooms is driven against the jamb, splintered, fastened from inside with the bolt unshot. Harker concludes it was no dream.
scenes.key_quote: I fear it was no dream, and must act on this surmise.

scenes.title: The three post-dated letters
scenes.summary: Dracula asks Harker to write letters saying he is leaving: 12 June, 19 June, 29 June. Harker pretends to agree to prolong his chances.
scenes.key_quote: I know now the span of my life.

scenes.title: The Szgany and the smuggled letters
scenes.summary: Harker throws two letters (to Hawkins and Mina) with a gold piece to a Szgany; the man pockets them in his cap. The Count burns the one to Mina in the lamp flame and returns the Hawkins letter for re-addressing; then locks the door.
scenes.key_quote: And he calmly held letter and envelope in the flame of the lamp till they were consumed.

scenes.title: The stolen belongings
scenes.summary: All paper, notes, letter of credit, the travelling suit, overcoat and rug are gone.
scenes.key_quote: Every scrap of paper was gone

scenes.title: Slovaks unload the boxes
scenes.summary: Two leiter-wagons each drawn by eight horses bring great square boxes with rope handles; Harker's door is fastened from outside; the Slovaks ignore his cries.
scenes.key_quote: my door was fastened on the outside.

scenes.title: The Count in Harker's clothes; the moon-dust hypnosis
scenes.summary: Harker sees the Count climb out in his travelling suit with the bag over his shoulder. Dust motes in moonbeams hypnotise him and form the three women's phantom shapes; he flees to his lamp-lit room.
scenes.key_quote: the phantom shapes ... were those of the three ghostly women to whom I was doomed

scenes.title: The mother and the wolves
scenes.summary: A distraught woman cries 'Monster, give me my child!' and beats on the door. The Count calls from the tower in a harsh metallic whisper; wolves flood in and she dies.
scenes.key_quote: Monster, give me my child!

scenes.title: Daylight resolve and the climb to the Count's room
scenes.summary: Harker takes off his boots and traverses the narrow ledge around the building to the Count's window and enters an empty, dusty room with a heap of old gold.
scenes.key_quote: I did not feel dizzy—I suppose I was too excited

scenes.title: Down to the chapel crypt
scenes.location: Stone passage, circular stair, tunnel passage, ruined chapel, vaults
scenes.summary: Via a heavy corner door, a stair lit by loopholes and a tunnel smelling of fresh earth, Harker reaches the broken-roofed chapel graveyard, with fifty boxes, and in the third vault finds the Count motionless with open stony eyes and no pulse.
scenes.key_quote: There, in one of the great boxes, of which there were fifty in all, on a pile of newly dug earth, lay the Count!

scenes.title: The mock release
scenes.summary: The Count announces Harker leaves tomorrow, then opens the unlocked door to howling wolves; Harker cries to shut it. At night the Count orders the women to wait: tomorrow night is theirs.
scenes.key_quote: To-night is mine. To-morrow night is yours!

scenes.title: The shovel blow
scenes.summary: The hall door is locked again. Harker scales down to the Count's room and the vault, finds the Count gorged and renewed, strikes at his face with a shovel; the Count's eyes paralyse him and the blade only gashes the forehead.
scenes.key_quote: He lay like a filthy leech, exhausted with his repletion.

scenes.title: The boxes are carried away
scenes.summary: A gust slams the stair door shut and traps Harker. He hears the Szgany and Slovaks nail down the box and carry the boxes out, lock the door and leave, singing.
scenes.key_quote: I am alone in the castle with those awful women.

scenes.title: Resolve to climb
scenes.summary: Harker decides to take some gold and scale the wall further than before, to find a way home or die in the fall.
scenes.key_quote: At least God’s mercy is better than that of these monsters

scenes.title: Mina's letter of shorthand and ambition
scenes.summary: Mina apologises for the delay, describes her shorthand and typewriter practice, plans a journal, and mentions a short note from Jonathan in Transylvania saying he will return in about a week.
scenes.key_quote: I want to keep up with Jonathan's studies, and I have been practising shorthand very assiduously.

scenes.title: Lucy admits she loves Arthur
scenes.summary: Lucy explains the curly-haired man is Mr. Holmwood, describes the clever young asylum doctor who stares into faces, and confesses her love in a blushing rush.
scenes.key_quote: Oh, Mina, couldn't you guess? I love him.

scenes.title: Proposal one: Dr. Seward
scenes.summary: Seward, outwardly cool but nervous, nearly sits on his silk hat and plays with a lancet while proposing. Lucy refuses; he asks if she loves another, and leaves offering friendship.
scenes.key_quote: He kept playing with a lancet in a way that made me nearly scream.

scenes.title: Proposal two: Quincey Morris
scenes.summary: The Texan jokes in horse-harness slang, then earnestly asks if there is another. Lucy says yes; he asks for one kiss, receives it, and leaves as a friend without looking back.
scenes.key_quote: Little girl, I hold your hand, and you've kissed me, and if these things don't make us friends nothing ever will.

scenes.title: Proposal three: Arthur accepted
scenes.summary: Arthur comes in and in a moment has both arms around her; Lucy is overjoyed. Told only in a postscript.
scenes.key_quote: I am very, very happy, and I don't know what I have done to deserve it.

scenes.title: Seward's diary: study of Renfield
scenes.location: Seward's lunatic asylum (Purfleet, not named in this chapter)
scenes.summary: Seward, unable to eat or rest, throws himself into work, questions his quaint patient more closely than ever, and notes he was almost cruel in keeping him to his hallucination. He records a first clinical sketch of Renfield.
scenes.key_quote: R. M. Renfield, ætat 59.—Sanguine temperament; great physical strength; morbidly excitable.

scenes.title: Camp-fire invitation and telegram
scenes.summary: Quincey invites Arthur to a camp-fire dinner with Seward to drink to Arthur's happiness; Arthur wires acceptance with a hint of news.
scenes.key_quote: Count me in every time. I bear messages which will make both your ears tingle.

scenes.title: Arrival at Whitby and the view
scenes.location: The Crescent, Whitby; Esk valley; East Cliff
scenes.summary: Lucy meets Mina at the station; they drive to rooms at the Crescent. Mina describes the viaduct, red-roofed old town, Whitby Abbey ruin and the clifftop churchyard.
scenes.key_quote: Right over the town is the ruin of Whitby Abbey, which was sacked by the Danes.

scenes.title: The harbour and the bell-buoy
scenes.location: Whitby harbour seen from the churchyard
scenes.summary: Mina describes the two piers with lighthouses, the tidal harbour, the reef with a bell buoy and the legend that bells are heard when a ship is lost.
scenes.key_quote: At the end of it is a buoy with a bell, which swings in bad weather, and sends in a mournful sound on the wind.

scenes.title: First meeting with the old man
scenes.summary: Nearly-hundred-year-old ex-whaler dismisses the White Lady and sea bells as 'fool-talk' and hobbles home for tea down the hundreds of curved steps.
scenes.key_quote: I wouldn't fash masel' about them, miss. Them things be all wore out.

scenes.title: Swales on tombstones and Geordie's grave
scenes.summary: Swales rants that half the tombstones cover empty graves because men were lost at sea, and exposes the slab where Lucy sits as the grave of George Canon, a suicide who shot himself with a crow-scaring musket and fell from Kettleness rocks.
scenes.key_quote: Won't it make Gabriel keckle when Geordie comes pantin' up the grees with the tombstean balanced on his hump.

scenes.title: Night view of Whitby
scenes.summary: Mina, sad with no letter from Jonathan, watches the lights, hears sheep, a donkey, a harsh waltz and a Salvation Army meeting.
scenes.key_quote: The clock has just struck nine. I see the lights scattered all over the town.

scenes.title: Renfield's flies and spiders
scenes.summary: Renfield collects flies, then spiders to eat the flies, and eats a blow-fly, saying it is life. He keeps a notebook of columns of figures and tames a sparrow.
scenes.key_quote: it was very good and very wholesome; that it was life, strong life, and gave life to him.

scenes.title: The kitten request and eaten birds
scenes.summary: Renfield begs for a kitten, then a cat, and when refused sits gnawing his fingers. Next morning the sparrows are gone, with feathers and a drop of blood on his pillow; he vomits feathers. Seward drugs him with an opiate, takes his notebook and names him zoophagous.
scenes.key_quote: He has eaten his birds, and that he just took and ate them raw!

scenes.title: Anxiety, sleepwalking and the locked door
scenes.location: Mina and Lucy's shared room at the Crescent
scenes.summary: Jonathan's only word is a line from Castle Dracula saying he is starting home, via Mr. Hawkins. Lucy sleepwalks again; Mina locks the door, and Lucy searches the room for the key while asleep.
scenes.key_quote: She tries the door, and finding it locked, goes about the room searching for the key.

scenes.title: Grey storm day, Swales's change, the strange ship
scenes.summary: Mina describes the grey sea under massing clouds. Swales confesses his mocking was to cheer himself and feels death in the wind; the coastguard points out an erratically steered Russian ship.
scenes.key_quote: She doesn't know her mind a bit; she seems to see the storm coming, but can't decide whether to run up north in the open, or to put in here.

scenes.title: The calm before the storm
scenes.location: Whitby, East Cliff churchyard and sea
scenes.summary: Mares'-tails appear in the sky; a flamboyant sunset gathers crowds on the cliff; the wind dies to a dead calm and boats stay in harbour. A foreign schooner under full sail idles at sea.
scenes.key_quote: As idle as a painted ship upon a painted ocean.

scenes.title: The tempest breaks
scenes.summary: A hollow booming, then the storm hits: giant waves overtop the piers, sea-fog rolls in, lightning flashes; the piers are cleared and the new East Cliff searchlight guides boats into harbour.
scenes.key_quote: The sea, running mountains high, threw skywards with each wave mighty masses of white foam.

scenes.title: The schooner enters the harbour
scenes.summary: Wind shifts to north-east and the schooner leaps between the piers, a corpse lashed to the helm, and drives onto Tate Hill Pier.
scenes.key_quote: lashed to the helm was a corpse, with drooping head, which swung horribly to and fro at each motion of the ship.

scenes.title: The dog leaps ashore
scenes.location: Tate Hill Pier and East Cliff
scenes.summary: As the keel touches sand an immense dog springs from below deck, leaps off the bow and bolts toward the churchyard cliff into the dark beyond the searchlight.
scenes.key_quote: an immense dog sprang up on deck from below, as if shot up by the concussion.

scenes.title: The coastguard and the dead steersman
scenes.location: Deck of the Demeter at Tate Hill Pier
scenes.summary: The coastguard recoils from the corpse; hands tied to a wheel spoke over a crucifix and beads, flesh cut to the bone; a doctor says dead two days; a corked bottle with a roll of paper is found in his pocket.
scenes.key_quote: Between the inner hand and the wood was a crucifix, the set of beads on which it was fastened being around both wrists and wheel.

scenes.title: Cargo and the dead mastiff
scenes.summary: The ship is the Demeter of Varna, ballast of silver sand and great wooden boxes of mould for Billington of 7 The Crescent. The dog has vanished; a coal merchant's half-bred mastiff is found with throat torn and belly slit.
scenes.key_quote: its throat was torn away, and its belly was slit open as if with a savage claw.

scenes.title: Log of the Demeter: departure to the Mediterranean
scenes.location: Aboard the Demeter: Varna, Bosphorus, Dardanelles, Cape Matapan
scenes.summary: Cargo of silver sand and earth boxes loaded; Turkish customs bribed; the crew grow scared and cross themselves; Petrofsky vanishes on watch.
scenes.key_quote: they only told him there was something, and crossed themselves.

scenes.title: The stranger sighted and the ship search
scenes.location: Aboard the Demeter, deck-house, hold with big boxes
scenes.summary: Olgaren sees a tall thin man on deck who vanishes; the whole crew searches with lanterns stem to stern and finds only the big boxes.
scenes.key_quote: he saw a tall, thin man, who was not like any of the crew, come up the companion-way, and go along the deck forward, and disappear.

scenes.title: Men disappear in Biscay and the Channel
scenes.location: Atlantic, Bay of Biscay, English Channel, fog
scenes.summary: Storm and fog; crewmen vanish after each watch (second mate, watch and steersman, more); the captain and mate arm themselves; a fog seems to move with the ship.
scenes.key_quote: There seems some doom over this ship.

scenes.title: The mate and the box
scenes.location: Hold and deck of the Demeter
scenes.summary: The mate stabs the pale tall figure but the knife passes through; he opens a box with a tool-chest, screams, sees It, and leaps into the sea.
scenes.key_quote: I saw It, like a man, tall and thin, and ghastly pale... I gave It my knife; but the knife went through It, empty as the air.

scenes.title: The captain ties himself to the wheel
scenes.summary: Alone, the captain sees Him, decides to lash his hands and a holy object to the wheel to save his soul, and writes the log into a bottle.
scenes.key_quote: I shall tie my hands to the wheel... and along with them I shall tie that which He—It!—dare not touch.

scenes.title: Verdict and public funeral planned
scenes.summary: An open verdict; the captain is a local hero, with a procession of over a hundred boats and burial in the cliff churchyard. The great dog is never found.
scenes.key_quote: The folk here hold almost universally that the captain is simply a hero.

scenes.title: Lucy sleepwalks in the storm
scenes.location: Mina and Lucy's room, the Crescent; Whitby harbour
scenes.summary: Lucy dresses twice in her sleep and Mina puts her back to bed; at dawn they see grim waves bullying through the harbour mouth.
scenes.key_quote: Lucy did not wake; but she got up twice and dressed herself.

scenes.title: Funeral, Swales's death, and the dog on the tombstone
scenes.summary: The captain is buried near Lucy's seat. Swales is found dead on the seat with neck broken and a look of horror. A dog howls and rages until thrown onto the tombstone, where it cowers in terror; Lucy is distressed.
scenes.key_quote: The moment it touched the stone the poor thing became quiet and fell all into a tremble.

scenes.title: Walk to Robin Hood's Bay
scenes.location: Cliff path, field by the lighthouse, inn at Robin Hood's Bay
scenes.summary: Lucy and Mina are frightened by cows, take tea at a bow-windowed inn over seaweedy rocks, and return exhausted, only to host the curate for supper.
scenes.key_quote: We had a capital 'severe tea' at Robin Hood's Bay in a sweet little old-fashioned inn.

scenes.title: Lucy missing in the night
scenes.location: The Crescent, North Terrace, West Cliff, fish market, bridge
scenes.summary: Mina finds the bed empty, the room door unlocked and the hall door's catch not caught; she takes a heavy shawl and runs through the empty town under a full moon with driving clouds.
scenes.key_quote: The bed was empty. I lit a match and found that she was not in the room.

scenes.title: The dark figure bending over Lucy
scenes.location: West Cliff edge; the steps to the abbey; the churchyard seat
scenes.summary: From the West Cliff Mina sees a white figure on the seat with something dark bending over it; as she climbs the endless steps she cries out and sees a white face with red gleaming eyes. When she enters the churchyard Lucy is alone.
scenes.key_quote: something raised a head, and from where I was I could see a white face and red, gleaming eyes.

scenes.title: Waking Lucy and the safety-pin
scenes.summary: Mina wraps Lucy in the shawl pinned at her throat, puts her shoes on Lucy's feet, wakes her, hides her own muddy feet, evades a drunk man and tucks her in; Lucy begs for secrecy. Mina ties the locked-door key to her wrist.
scenes.key_quote: I have locked the door, and the key is tied to my wrist.

scenes.title: The two little marks
scenes.summary: Two red points on Lucy's throat with a drop of blood on her nightdress; by 17 August the marks are open, larger, with faintly white edges.
scenes.key_quote: They are like little white dots with red centres.

scenes.title: The bat at the window
scenes.summary: Lucy sits up asleep pointing at the window; a great bat circles in the moonlight and flits off toward the abbey.
scenes.key_quote: Between me and the moonlight flitted a great bat, coming and going in great whirling circles.

scenes.title: His red eyes again
scenes.location: Top of the steps from West Pier; East Cliff seat
scenes.summary: Lucy murmurs 'His red eyes again!' as a dark seated figure on their seat seems to have burning eyes, a trick of the sun on St. Mary's windows. That night Mina sees Lucy asleep at the window with a bird-like thing on the sill.
scenes.key_quote: His red eyes again! They are just the same.

scenes.title: Mrs. Westenra's secret
scenes.summary: Arthur's father is better and the wedding is hastened; Mrs. Westenra confides her doctor says her heart will kill her within months.
scenes.key_quote: She has got her death-warrant.

scenes.title: Lucy fading
scenes.summary: Lucy grows pale and weak, gasping at night, found fainting at the open window despite the key on Mina's wrist.
scenes.key_quote: all the time the roses in her cheeks are fading

scenes.title: The boxes go to Carfax
scenes.location: Whitby solicitors, Great Northern Railway, King's Cross, Carfax chapel
scenes.summary: Fifty boxes are railed to King's Cross and carted to Carfax near Purfleet, placed in the ruined ancient chapel marked 'A', keys left in the main hall; £1 17s. 9d returned.
scenes.key_quote: You will please deposit the boxes, fifty in number, which form the consignment, in the partially ruined building.

scenes.title: Lucy remembers the dream
scenes.summary: Lucy recalls crossing the bridge, dogs howling, something long and dark with red eyes, sweet and bitter scent, sinking into green water, her soul floating above the West Lighthouse.
scenes.key_quote: something long and dark with red eyes, just as we saw in the sunset

scenes.title: News of Jonathan
scenes.summary: Mr. Hawkins forwards Sister Agatha's letter: Jonathan has had six weeks of brain fever, raved of wolves, poison, blood, demons, and arrived on a train from Klausenburg. Mina leaves to join him.
scenes.key_quote: his ravings have been dreadful; of wolves and poison and blood; of ghosts and demons

scenes.title: Renfield speaks of the Master
scenes.summary: Renfield sniffs like a hound, haughty, saying 'the Master is at hand'; then recites a line about bride-maidens.
scenes.key_quote: I don't want to talk to you: you don't count now; the Master is at hand.

scenes.title: Renfield escapes to Carfax
scenes.location: Asylum window, belt of trees, wall, Carfax grounds, chapel door
scenes.summary: Renfield wrenches out his window; Seward follows feet first, sees him scale the wall into Carfax, and finds him pressed against the ironbound oak door of the chapel, begging his Master.
scenes.key_quote: I am here to do Your bidding, Master. I am Your slave, and You will reward me, for I shall be faithful.

scenes.title: Capturing Renfield
scenes.summary: The men close in, Renfield fights like a tiger; he is placed in a strait-waistcoat chained to the wall of the padded room and says 'It is coming'.
scenes.key_quote: I shall be patient, Master. It is coming—coming—coming!

scenes.title: Mina finds Jonathan in the hospital
scenes.location: Hospital of St. Joseph and Ste. Mary, Buda-Pesth (convent nursing sisters)
scenes.summary: Mina nurses a thin, pale Jonathan. Sister Agatha refuses to repeat his ravings, saying they are secrets of God, but assures Mina his fear was of great and terrible things, not of any wrong he did.
scenes.key_quote: His fear was of great and terrible things, which no mortal can treat of.

scenes.title: The notebook and the wedding
scenes.summary: Jonathan gives Mina the notebook containing his secret and asks her never to tell him unless duty requires. They marry within the hour; Mina wraps the book in white paper, ties it with pale blue ribbon and seals it with her wedding ring.
scenes.key_quote: Take it and keep it, read it if you will, but never let me know

scenes.title: Lucy's cheerful letter
scenes.summary: Lucy reports she has stopped sleepwalking, Arthur is visiting, and the wedding is set for 28 September.
scenes.key_quote: We are to be married on 28 September.

scenes.title: Renfield quiet by moon, violent by day
scenes.summary: Renfield turns calm at moonrise murmuring 'Now I can wait', refuses a kitten, and grows violent again before dawn. Seward decides to give him a chance to escape.
scenes.key_quote: Now I can wait; now I can wait.

scenes.title: Renfield escapes to the chapel door
scenes.location: Grounds of the deserted house (Carfax), old chapel door
scenes.summary: Renfield dashes past an attendant, runs to the old chapel door and presses against it. Held by attendants he redoubles then suddenly calms as a big bat flies silently west across the moon.
scenes.key_quote: a big bat, which was flapping its silent and ghostly way to the west

scenes.title: Lucy's relapse
scenes.summary: Lucy has bad dreams, hears scratching or flapping at the window as the clock strikes twelve, and wakes pale, weak, with a sore throat and air hunger.
scenes.key_quote: There was a sort of scratching or flapping at the window

scenes.title: Arthur's plea and Seward's examination
scenes.summary: Seward lunches at Hillingham, sees Lucy drop her cheerful mask in the boudoir, accidentally obtains a few drops of her blood from a broken window-cord cut, finds it normal, and writes to Van Helsing.
scenes.key_quote: The qualitative analysis gives a quite normal condition

scenes.title: Van Helsing examines Lucy
scenes.summary: Van Helsing charms Lucy, sends Seward to smoke in the garden, examines her privately, notes blood loss but no anaemia, asks to question her maid, and goes home to think while demanding daily telegrams.
scenes.key_quote: This is no jest, but life and death, perhaps more.

scenes.title: Renfield's noon and sunset fits
scenes.summary: Renfield is violent at noon, then collects flies with sugar on the window sill, then at sunset collapses as the sun dips, throws away his fly-box and declares he is done with flies, saying 'He has deserted me'.
scenes.key_quote: All over! all over! He has deserted me.

scenes.title: Telegrams: Lucy worsens
scenes.summary: Two reassuring telegrams are followed by an urgent call on 6 September.
scenes.key_quote: Terrible change for the worse. Come at once; do not lose an hour.

scenes.title: Liverpool Street: the husbandman's corn
scenes.summary: Van Helsing tells Seward to keep knowledge to himself, compares his silence to a husbandman who does not dig up planted corn, and urges Seward to keep careful case notes.
scenes.key_quote: Nothing is too small. I counsel you, put down in record even your doubts and surmises.

scenes.title: Lucy found near death
scenes.summary: Lucy is chalky pale, lips and gums bloodless, breathing laboured. Van Helsing declares she needs a transfusion at once.
scenes.key_quote: She will die for sheer want of blood to keep the heart's action as it should be.

scenes.title: First transfusion (Arthur)
scenes.summary: Arthur arrives; Van Helsing recruits him. Lucy drinks a narcotic, Arthur kisses her, and Van Helsing transfuses blood without defibrinating it. Colour returns to Lucy.
scenes.key_quote: Then with swiftness, but with absolute method, Van Helsing performed the operation.

scenes.title: The marks on the throat
scenes.summary: The black velvet band with a diamond buckle slips, revealing a red mark. Seward loosens it and finds two small punctures with white, worn edges over the external jugular vein.
scenes.key_quote: Just over the external jugular vein there were two punctures, not large, but not wholesome-looking.

scenes.title: Seward's vigil
scenes.summary: Van Helsing leaves for Amsterdam. Lucy fears sleep but trusts Seward's promise and sleeps peacefully all night.
scenes.key_quote: Afraid to go to sleep! Why so?

scenes.title: Seward sleeps; Lucy drained again
scenes.location: Hillingham, adjoining room then Lucy's bedroom
scenes.summary: Lucy talks Seward into resting on a sofa in the next room with both doors open. In the morning Van Helsing finds her swooned and nearly bloodless.
scenes.key_quote: All our work is undone; we must begin again.

scenes.title: Second transfusion (Seward)
scenes.summary: Brandy is used to revive her, then Seward gives blood with a morphia injection to keep Lucy asleep. Van Helsing insists Arthur must not know.
scenes.key_quote: Mind, nothing must be said of this.

scenes.title: The garlic flowers
scenes.summary: A parcel of garlic flowers from Haarlem arrives. Van Helsing rubs them on windows, door jamb and fireplace, latches the windows, and puts a wreath round Lucy's neck.
scenes.key_quote: Perhaps I am!

scenes.title: Lucy sleeps with garlic
scenes.summary: Lucy finds comfort in the garlic and feels no fear of the flapping outside the window.
scenes.key_quote: I never liked garlic before, but to-night it is delightful!

scenes.title: Mrs. Westenra removes the garlic
scenes.location: Hillingham morning room, dining-room, Lucy's room
scenes.summary: Mrs. Westenra proudly says she removed the stuffy flowers and opened the window. Van Helsing weeps in despair in the dining-room, then locks Lucy's door and performs a third transfusion on his own arm.
scenes.key_quote: Devils or no devils, or all the devils at once, it matters not; we fight him all the same.

scenes.title: Four days of peace
scenes.summary: Lucy recovers; a boxful of garlic arrives daily from Haarlem; Van Helsing sleeps in a chair; bats nap against the panes.
scenes.key_quote: the boughs or bats or something napped almost angrily against the window-panes

scenes.title: The Escaped Wolf interview
scenes.location: Zoological Gardens, keeper's cottage behind the elephant-house
scenes.summary: Bilder describes the tall stranger who calmed the wolves and stroked Bersicker, the howling at moonrise and the broken cage. Bersicker returns by himself, head cut with broken glass.
scenes.key_quote: a tall, thin chap, with a 'ook nose and a pointed beard, with a few white hairs runnin' through it.

scenes.title: Renfield attacks Seward
scenes.summary: Renfield bursts in with a dinner-knife, cuts Seward's left wrist, is floored, and licks the spilt blood from the carpet.
scenes.key_quote: The blood is the life! The blood is the life!

scenes.title: Misdirected telegram
scenes.summary: Van Helsing's telegram, sent to Carfax, Sussex, arrives 22 hours late; Seward loses a night.
scenes.key_quote: Do not fail to be at Hillingham to-night.

scenes.title: The night the wolf came
scenes.summary: Lucy hears howling and a bat at the window; her mother joins her in bed; the window shatters and a gaunt grey wolf's head appears; Mrs. Westenra tears off the garlic wreath, points, and dies on top of Lucy.
scenes.key_quote: in the aperture of the broken panes there was the head of a great, gaunt grey wolf.

scenes.title: The drugged maids
scenes.summary: Lucy finds all four maids unconscious beside a decanter of sherry laced with laudanum from Mrs. Westenra's empty bottle, and returns to her dead mother, hearing the wolf's howl; lights burn blue and specks swirl.
scenes.key_quote: It smelt of laudanum

scenes.title: The locked house
scenes.summary: Seward rings and knocks without answer; windows and doors are locked. Van Helsing arrives by swift horse and fears they are too late.
scenes.key_quote: If there be no way open to get in, we must make one.

scenes.title: Cutting through the kitchen window
scenes.summary: Van Helsing hands Seward a small surgical saw; Seward cuts three iron bars. A long thin knife pushes back the sash fastening. They enter and find the four drugged maids.
scenes.key_quote: The Professor took a small surgical saw from his case

scenes.title: Two women on the bed
scenes.summary: Mrs. Westenra lies dead under a white sheet; the garlic is on her bosom and Lucy's throat is bare with two white mangled wounds. Van Helsing hears a heartbeat and calls for brandy.
scenes.key_quote: It is not yet too late! Quick! quick! Bring the brandy!

scenes.title: The hot bath
scenes.summary: Seward wakes three maids with a wet towel; they heat water. Lucy is warmed in a bath, her heart beats audibly; Van Helsing ties a silk handkerchief round her throat. A messenger from Holmwood is left waiting at the door.
scenes.key_quote: The first gain is ours! Check to the King!

scenes.title: Quincey Morris arrives; fourth transfusion
scenes.location: Hillingham dining-room and Lucy's new room
scenes.summary: Quincey is on the dining-room sofa with Arthur's telegram. He offers blood and Van Helsing performs the fourth transfusion with a subcutaneous morphia injection.
scenes.key_quote: A brave man's blood is the best thing on this earth when a woman is in trouble.

scenes.title: The paper from Lucy's breast
scenes.summary: Van Helsing reads Lucy's memorandum, replaces it in her breast, and in sleep Lucy tears it and scatters imaginary pieces.
scenes.key_quote: It dropped from Lucy's breast when we carried her to the bath.

scenes.title: Death certificate and Quincey's questions
scenes.summary: Seward arranges registration and undertaker. Quincey deduces four men's blood has gone into Lucy and recalls his mare killed by a vampire bat on the Pampas.
scenes.key_quote: One of those big bats that they call vampires had got at her in the night

scenes.title: Mina's letters and Hennessey's report
scenes.summary: Hawkins leaves everything to the Harkers and then dies. Renfield, enraged by the carriers delivering great boxes to the empty house, escapes through his window and attacks them.
scenes.key_quote: I'll fight for my Lord and Master!

scenes.title: Arthur at Lucy's bedside
scenes.summary: Arthur arrives at sunset and speaks with Lucy; they take turns watching.
scenes.key_quote: I fear that to-morrow will end our watching

scenes.title: The bat and the garlic
scenes.summary: A great bat strikes the window in full moonlight; Lucy tears the garlic off asleep and clutches it awake. Her canines look longer.
scenes.key_quote: whenever she got into that lethargic state ... she put the flowers from her; but that when she waked she clutched them close

scenes.title: Death of Lucy
scenes.summary: Lucy's wounds vanish; she wakes asking Arthur for a kiss in a voluptuous voice, Van Helsing hurls him back; she then asks Van Helsing to guard Arthur and dies.
scenes.key_quote: It is only the beginning!

scenes.title: Preparing the dead
characters: woman who laid out the dead
scenes.summary: Seward handles the funeral formalities with the obsequious undertaker; the layer-out praises Lucy as a beautiful corpse. Van Helsing hovers nearby and insists on examining Lucy's papers himself.
scenes.key_quote: She makes a very beautiful corpse, sir. It’s quite a privilege to attend on her.

scenes.title: Searching the papers
scenes.location: Mrs. Westenra's house, study / Lucy's old room
scenes.summary: Van Helsing shows the torn memorandum from Lucy's breast, tells Seward to seal Mrs. Westenra's papers and write her solicitor, and keeps Lucy's letters, memoranda and a newly begun diary for himself.
scenes.key_quote: It is not well that her very thoughts go into the hands of strangers.

scenes.title: The chapelle ardente
scenes.summary: The room is turned into a chapel of white flowers. Lucy's beauty has returned in death. Van Helsing fetches wild garlic from an unopened box in the hall, scatters it among the flowers, and lays his little gold crucifix over her mouth.
scenes.key_quote: All Lucy’s loveliness had come back to her in death

scenes.title: The request to behead Lucy
scenes.summary: Van Helsing asks for post-mortem knives and reveals he wants to cut off her head and take out her heart, planning to do it secretly after Arthur has seen her. He pleads for Seward's trust and Seward promises. A maid is seen going to sit with the body.
scenes.key_quote: I want to cut off her head and take out her heart.

scenes.title: The stolen crucifix
scenes.summary: Van Helsing cancels the operation because the crucifix was stolen in the night; he recovered it from the thieving woman, who is not to be punished by him.
scenes.key_quote: This was stolen in the night.

scenes.title: The solicitor and the will
scenes.summary: Marquand of Wholeman, Sons, Marquand & Lidderdale explains the will leaves everything except the entailed property to Arthur Holmwood, and gladly takes the funeral details off their hands.
scenes.key_quote: I am rejoiced at the result, perfectly rejoiced.

scenes.title: Arthur's farewell to Lucy
scenes.summary: Arthur arrives broken. He asks 'is she really dead?' on seeing her unnaturally radiant face, kisses her hand and forehead, and the coffin is screwed up by the undertaker's men.
scenes.key_quote: Jack, is she really dead?

scenes.title: Dinner and the trust of Arthur
scenes.summary: Van Helsing asks Arthur's permission to keep and read all of Lucy's papers; Arthur grants it and promises to trust him. Van Helsing patrols the house all night while Lucy lies in her coffin strewn with garlic.
scenes.key_quote: will have to pass through the bitter water before we reach the sweet

scenes.title: Hawkins's funeral at Exeter
scenes.summary: A simple service for Mr. Hawkins with servants, old friends, his London agent and a representative of Sir John Paxton, President of the Incorporated Law Society.
scenes.key_quote: we felt that our best and dearest friend was gone from us

scenes.title: Jonathan sees the Count in Piccadilly
scenes.summary: After the Row at Hyde Park Corner, Jonathan recognises a tall thin man with a beaky nose, black moustache, pointed beard and pointed white teeth staring at a girl in a victoria. The man follows her in a hansom. Jonathan sleeps on a Green Park bench and wakes with no memory. Mina decides to open the parcel with his Transylvania journal.
scenes.key_quote: It is the man himself!

scenes.title: Telegram of death
scenes.summary: Mina receives Van Helsing's telegram announcing that Mrs. Westenra and Lucy have died and been buried.
scenes.key_quote: Mrs. Westenra died five days ago, and that Lucy died the day before yesterday.

scenes.title: King Laugh in the carriage
scenes.location: Railway carriage, London bound; Seward's diary
scenes.summary: After the burial Van Helsing laughs and cries hysterically in the carriage, then explains the grim irony of the funeral. Seward closes his diary with 'FINIS'. Lucy lies in the family tomb in a lonely churchyard, the sun rising over Hampstead Hill.
scenes.key_quote: Ah, you don’t comprehend, friend John.

scenes.title: The Hampstead mystery
scenes.summary: Two Westminster Gazette items report children missing in the evening on the Heath, lured by a 'bloofer lady' and found with small throat wounds; one found emaciated under a furze bush.
scenes.key_quote: they had been with a “bloofer lady.”

scenes.title: Mina reads the journal
scenes.summary: Mina locks herself in to read Jonathan's foreign journal, is shaken, and decides to prepare for a 'solemn duty' by typing a copy.
scenes.key_quote: There may be a solemn duty; and if it come we must not shrink from it.

scenes.title: Van Helsing's letter and Mina's telegram
scenes.summary: Van Helsing writes confidentially asking to meet; Mina telegrams him to come by the quarter-past ten train.
scenes.key_quote: Come to-day by quarter-past ten train if you can catch it.

scenes.title: The interview in Exeter
scenes.summary: Mina plays a small joke with her shorthand diary then gives him the typewritten copy. He reads it, is overjoyed, praises her; she breaks down about Jonathan; he consoles her over lunch and she gives him Jonathan's journal.
scenes.key_quote: This paper is as sunshine. It opens the gate to me.

scenes.title: Van Helsing's verdict letters
scenes.summary: He writes that Jonathan's diary is true; she replies that Jonathan returns by the 6:25 from Launceston and invites him to breakfast at eight.
scenes.key_quote: Strange and terrible as it is, it is true!

scenes.title: Jonathan meets Van Helsing
scenes.location: Hotel in Exeter, then the station
scenes.summary: Jonathan is relieved to be believed and promises full help vs the Count. He gives the bundle of papers. At the station Van Helsing reads the Westminster Gazette and mutters 'Mein Gott! So soon!'
scenes.key_quote: Then I am with you heart and soul.

scenes.title: Renfield and the newspaper
scenes.summary: Seward notes Renfield is stable with his fly and spider business. Van Helsing bursts in with the Westminster Gazette and points out the throat punctures on Hampstead children.
scenes.key_quote: It is like poor Lucy’s.

scenes.title: Van Helsing's thesis: believe
scenes.summary: Van Helsing lists wonders: Methuselah, Old Parr, the great spider in the Spanish church, vampire bats of the Pampas, toads in rock, the buried fakir; asks Seward to believe. He ends with the revelation that Lucy made the wounds.
scenes.key_quote: They were made by Miss Lucy!

scenes.title: The accusation
scenes.summary: Seward slams the table; Van Helsing proposes to prove it and produces the tomb key.
scenes.key_quote: Dare you come with me?

scenes.title: North Hospital
scenes.summary: Dr. Vincent shows the throat punctures and suggests a rat, bat or escaped wolf; the child asks to go play with the bloofer lady.
scenes.key_quote: he said he wanted to play with the ‘bloofer lady.’

scenes.title: Dinner at Jack Straw's Castle
scenes.summary: They dine among noisy bicyclists, then walk through the dark with scattered lamps.
scenes.key_quote: We dined at “Jack Straw’s Castle”

scenes.title: Opening the coffin
scenes.summary: They climb the wall; Van Helsing opens the falling-lock door, lights a candle, unscrews the coffin lid, saws the lead casing, and shows an empty coffin.
scenes.key_quote: The coffin was empty.

scenes.title: The vigil and the child
scenes.summary: Seward hides behind a yew; a white streak glides between yews, a dark mass moves; Van Helsing catches a tiny child. They leave it for a policeman on the Heath.
scenes.key_quote: Are you satisfied now?

scenes.title: The sleeping Un-Dead
scenes.summary: After the noon funeral and sexton's lock-up, they find Lucy in her coffin, more radiant, lips red, canines sharp. Van Helsing explains the Un-Dead and tells of the cure but delays.
scenes.key_quote: Are you convinced now?

scenes.title: The note in the portmanteau
scenes.summary: Van Helsing leaves instructions in case he is killed: find the great Un-Dead and cut off his head and burn or stake his heart.
scenes.key_quote: cut off his head and burn his heart or drive a stake through it

scenes.title: Seward doubts again
scenes.summary: Next morning Seward is again sceptical and wonders if Van Helsing is mad.
scenes.key_quote: Is it possible that the Professor can have done it himself?

scenes.title: Persuading Arthur and Quincey
scenes.summary: Van Helsing asks them to enter the tomb and open the coffin; Arthur is furious but finally agrees to go and wait.
scenes.key_quote: But, I beseech you, do not go forth in anger with me.

scenes.title: Return to the empty coffin
scenes.time: 11:45 pm, 29 September, dark with moon gleams
scenes.summary: Van Helsing leads them in, closes the door, lights a dark lantern, removes the lid and lets Arthur see the cut lead and the empty coffin.
scenes.key_quote: The coffin was empty!

scenes.title: Quincey's challenge and Van Helsing's account
scenes.summary: Quincey asks if Van Helsing did this; he swears no and explains the garlic on the clamps last night and its removal tonight.
scenes.key_quote: I swear to you by all that I hold sacred that I have not removed nor touched her.

scenes.title: Sealing the tomb with the Host
scenes.summary: Van Helsing crumbles consecrated wafers into putty and lays strips in the door crevices so the Un-Dead cannot enter.
scenes.key_quote: The Host. I brought it from Amsterdam. I have an Indulgence.

scenes.title: The Bloofer Lady returns
scenes.location: Avenue of yews and tomb door
scenes.summary: A white figure with a child advances; moonlight shows Lucy with bloody lips. She throws down the child, invites Arthur to her arms, is stopped by the crucifix, and cannot pass the sealed door.
scenes.key_quote: Come to me, Arthur. Leave these others and come to me.

scenes.title: Lucy enters the tomb
scenes.summary: Arthur gives consent; Van Helsing removes some Host and Lucy passes through the crack as a corporeal body; he restores the seal.
scenes.key_quote: pass in through the interstice where scarce a knife-blade could have gone.

scenes.title: Returning the child
scenes.summary: The child is left where police will find it; Van Helsing tells Arthur he is in the 'bitter waters'.
scenes.key_quote: You are now in the bitter waters, my child.

scenes.title: Preparations for the stake
scenes.summary: All in black, the men wait out the funeral and sexton, then Van Helsing lays out solder, lamp, knives, stake and hammer and explains the curse of the Un-Dead.
scenes.key_quote: they cannot die, but must go on age after age adding new victims

scenes.title: Arthur drives the stake
scenes.summary: Arthur holds the stake over the heart; with the prayer for the dead he strikes; Lucy shrieks and writhes, blood spurts, then lies still and becomes sweet Lucy again.
scenes.key_quote: He looked like a figure of Thor

scenes.title: Finishing the work
scenes.summary: Arthur kisses her; Arthur and Quincey leave; Van Helsing and Seward saw off the stake top, cut off the head, fill the mouth with garlic, solder the lead coffin and screw the lid.
scenes.key_quote: Then we cut off the head and filled the mouth with garlic.

scenes.title: The vow
scenes.summary: Van Helsing proposes the hunt for the author of their sorrow; each takes his hand; dinner is set for two nights hence at seven, he will bring two unknown helpers.
scenes.key_quote: once our feet are on the ploughshare we must not draw back.

scenes.title: Telegram at the Berkeley Hotel
scenes.summary: Van Helsing finds Mina's telegram, orders Seward to meet her, gives him typescripts of Jonathan's and Mina's diaries and leaves for Liverpool Street and Whitby.
scenes.key_quote: may be the beginning of the end to you and me and many another; or it may sound the knell of the Un-Dead who walk the earth.

scenes.title: Meeting at Paddington
scenes.location: Paddington station, then Underground to Fenchurch Street, then Purfleet asylum
scenes.summary: Mina recognises Seward from Lucy's description; they travel with her typewriter to the asylum, where she shudders on entering.
scenes.key_quote: I knew you from the description of poor dear Lucy; but——

scenes.title: The phonograph in the study
scenes.summary: Mina discovers the phonograph, asks to hear Lucy's death; Seward refuses in horror until she points to her own typescripts. He gives her the wax cylinders, the first half-dozen being personal.
scenes.key_quote: Tell you of her death? Not for the wide world!

scenes.title: Mina hears the cylinders
scenes.summary: Mina listens through the forked ear-tubes, is overcome by the story of Lucy's death and revived with brandy, then types all cylinders from the seventh in three manifold copies. She borrows newspaper files.
scenes.key_quote: In this matter dates are everything

scenes.title: Harker's trail of the boxes
scenes.location: Whitby, King's Cross, Carter Paterson's central office
scenes.summary: Jonathan inspects invoices, coastguards, station-masters and carriers; every tally confirms fifty cases of earth reached Carfax chapel. A carrier describes the house as the 'rummiest' he was ever in.
scenes.key_quote: Fifty cases of common earth, to be used for experimental purposes.

scenes.title: Seward reads the typescripts and visits Renfield
scenes.summary: Seward realises Carfax is next door. Renfield is unnaturally calm, speaks of discharge, and Seward orders the attendant to keep a strait-waistcoat ready.
scenes.key_quote: I mistrust these quiet moods of his

scenes.title: Mina comforts Godalming and Morris
scenes.summary: Mina gives both suitors of Lucy the typed record. Godalming weeps on her shoulder; Morris kisses her hand and calls her 'little girl'.
scenes.key_quote: Little girl, you will never regret that true-hearted kindness, so long as ever you live!

scenes.title: Mina visits Renfield
scenes.summary: Renfield swallows his flies and spiders to 'tidy up', asks Mina to leave, then gives a lucid account of his old delusion about consuming life.
scenes.key_quote: For the blood is the life.

scenes.title: Van Helsing arrives
scenes.location: Station and carriage to the asylum
scenes.summary: Van Helsing learns the Count's house is next door and decides Mina must be kept out after tonight.
scenes.key_quote: Oh that we had known it before!

scenes.title: The committee and the pact
scenes.summary: Van Helsing lays his golden crucifix on the table; all clasp hands in a solemn compact. He lectures on the enemy, the vampire's limits and Dracula's history.
scenes.key_quote: There are such beings as vampires; some of us have evidence that they exist.

scenes.title: The bat and the pistol shot
scenes.summary: Morris sees a big bat on the window-sill and fires from outside, shattering the glass; it flies into the wood.
scenes.key_quote: a big bat came and sat on the window-sill.

scenes.title: Campaign planned; Mina excluded
scenes.summary: Plan: trace each box, capture or kill the Count, or sterilise the earth; he is weakest between noon and sunset. Mina is told to rest.
scenes.key_quote: we must, so to speak, sterilise the earth, so that no more he can seek safety in it.

scenes.title: Renfield begs to be released
scenes.summary: Renfield, courtly and lucid, introduces himself to each man and pleads to be freed immediately. Refused, he throws himself on his knees, then collapses into sullen silence.
scenes.key_quote: Don’t you know that I am sane and earnest now; that I am no lunatic in a mad fit, but a sane man fighting for his soul?

scenes.title: Silence after Renfield
scenes.summary: The men debate whether Renfield was sane; Van Helsing chooses caution. Godalming fetches the silver whistle.
scenes.key_quote: That old place may be full of rats, and if so, I’ve got an antidote on call.

scenes.title: Arming on the porch
scenes.summary: Van Helsing lays out four sets of weapons and wards and distributes them.
scenes.key_quote: we need arms of many kinds. Our enemy is not merely spiritual.

scenes.title: Opening the door
scenes.summary: Seward finds a skeleton key; rusty bolt clangs back. The party enters, Van Helsing crossing himself and saying 'In manus tuas, Domine!'. Dust shows hobnail prints and a table with a bunch of labelled keys.
scenes.key_quote: “In manus tuas, Domine!” he said, crossing himself as he passed over the threshold.

scenes.title: The chapel and the stench
scenes.summary: Using Jonathan's map they find the iron-banded oak door; the foul air; only twenty-nine of fifty boxes remain. Godalming thinks he sees the Count's face in the passage, but it is shadows.
scenes.key_quote: it seemed as though corruption had become itself corrupt.

scenes.title: The rats and the terriers
scenes.location: Chapel and its outer iron-bound oaken door
scenes.summary: A phosphorescent mass of rats swarms. Godalming opens the outer door and blows the silver whistle; terriers come but halt howling at the threshold until carried in, then kill rats until the horde vanishes.
scenes.key_quote: the place made look like a bank of earth set with fireflies.

scenes.title: Withdrawal at dawn
scenes.summary: The house is searched; nothing more. Van Helsing locks the hall door and keeps the key, observing that rats flee from small dogs.
scenes.key_quote: we have reason to be content with our first night’s work.

scenes.title: Van Helsing visits Renfield
scenes.summary: Renfield sullenly insults Van Helsing and falls silent.
scenes.key_quote: you are the old fool Van Helsing.

scenes.title: Mina's mist dream
scenes.summary: Mist creeps across the lawn and pours through the door joins; a pillar of cloud with two red eyes forms and a livid white face bends over her.
scenes.key_quote: The last conscious effort which imagination made was to show me a livid white face bending over me out of the mist.

scenes.title: Mina takes a sleeping draught
scenes.summary: Renfield kisses her hand and blesses her in the afternoon; Seward gives her a mild sleeping draught.
scenes.key_quote: I might want it.

scenes.title: Snelling and Smollet
scenes.summary: Snelling is drunk. Smollet checks his notebook: six boxes to 197 Chicksand Street, Mile End New Town, six to Jamaica Lane, Bermondsey. Hint of a further job by Sam Bloxam at Purfleet.
scenes.key_quote: there were, he said, six in the cartload which he took from Carfax and left at 197, Chicksand Street, Mile End New Town

scenes.title: Phonetic address hunt
scenes.summary: The scrap reads 'Sam Bloxam, Korkrans, 4, Poters Cort, Bartel Street, Walworth. Arsk for the depite.' Jonathan decodes the misspellings and tips the deputy.
scenes.key_quote: phonetic spelling had again misled me

scenes.title: Finding Bloxam at Poplar
scenes.location: Cross Angel Street cold storage building
scenes.summary: Bloxam says he made two trips from Carfax to Piccadilly with nine boxes, helped by a strong thin old man with a white moustache who needed no key.
scenes.key_quote: he was the strongest chap I ever struck, an’ him a old feller, with a white moustache, one that thin you would think he couldn’t throw a shadder.

scenes.title: The Piccadilly house
scenes.location: Piccadilly, near the Junior Constitutional and mews behind
scenes.summary: Jonathan finds the dusty untenanted house with shutters up and a torn notice board; the grooms recall a 'For Sale' board from Mitchell, Sons & Candy.
scenes.key_quote: The windows were encrusted with dust, and the shutters were up.

scenes.title: The house agents
scenes.summary: The suave agent refuses to name the buyer until Jonathan says he acts for Lord Godalming.
scenes.key_quote: The affairs of their clients are absolutely safe in the hands of Mitchell, Sons, & Candy.

scenes.title: Council by the fire
scenes.summary: Party debates how to break into Piccadilly and reads aloud Jonathan's diary; plan to wait for the agent's letter.
scenes.key_quote: Say! how are we going to get into that house?

scenes.title: Renfield on souls and life
scenes.summary: Renfield disclaims wanting souls, stops at the word 'drink', fears the burden of souls; Seward deduces he expects a human life from the Count. Later Renfield sings and folds a scrap of paper into a notebook.
scenes.key_quote: Merciful God! the Count has been to him, and there is some new scheme of terror afoot!

scenes.title: Agency letter
scenes.summary: The letter gives No. 347 Piccadilly, former owner executors of Archibald Winter-Suffield, purchaser Count de Ville paying cash.
scenes.key_quote: The purchaser is a foreign nobleman, Count de Ville

scenes.title: Plan and Renfield's accident
scenes.summary: Horses are readied; Van Helsing researches ancient medicine at the British Museum. A wild yell from Renfield; he is found face down in blood.
scenes.key_quote: found him lying on his face on the floor, all covered with blood.

scenes.title: Renfield found dying
scenes.summary: Seward finds Renfield on his left side in a glittering pool of blood, face bruised, back apparently broken, right arm and leg paralysed. The attendant cannot reconcile the face wounds with a broken back.
scenes.key_quote: he had received some terrible injuries; there seemed none of that unity of purpose between the parts of the body which marks even lethargic sanity.

scenes.title: Trephining
scenes.summary: Van Helsing sends the attendant away, diagnoses a depressed skull fracture over the motor area and trephines just above the ear while Arthur and Quincey wait on the bed.
scenes.key_quote: We shall operate just above the ear.

scenes.title: Renfield's confession
scenes.summary: Revived with brandy and water, Renfield tells how the Count came through the mist, showed him rats and promised lives for worship, how he let the Count in, and how he fought him on realising Mina was being drained.
scenes.key_quote: I must not deceive myself; it was no dream, but all a grim reality.

scenes.title: Arming and the corridor
scenes.summary: Everyone fetches the same kit used at Carfax. Van Helsing resolves to break the Harkers' door despite propriety.
scenes.key_quote: All chambers are alike to the doctor; and even were they not they are all as one to me to-night.

scenes.title: The Count in the Harkers' bedroom
scenes.time: Night, bright moonlight through yellow blind
scenes.summary: The door bursts open on the Count forcing Mina's mouth to his bleeding breast. Van Helsing holds up the Sacred Wafer, the others raise crucifixes, the Count cowers, a cloud covers the moon and he escapes as vapour under the door.
scenes.key_quote: The attitude of the two had a terrible resemblance to a child forcing a kitten’s nose into a saucer of milk to compel it to drink.

scenes.title: Aftermath in the bedroom
scenes.summary: Van Helsing wakes Jonathan with a wet towel; Mina calls herself unclean; Jonathan holds her; Van Helsing shields them with the golden crucifix.
scenes.key_quote: Unclean, unclean! I must touch him or kiss him no more.

scenes.title: Reports of the damage
scenes.summary: Arthur reports the study ransacked, manuscript burned, phonograph cylinders thrown on the fire and Renfield dead. Quincey saw a bat fly west from Renfield's window.
scenes.key_quote: I saw a bat rise from Renfield’s window, and flap westward.

scenes.title: Mina's testimony
scenes.summary: Mina recounts waking to find the Count in the mist, his threats against Jonathan, the bite, and being made to drink from his opened vein as punishment.
scenes.key_quote: When my brain says “Come!” to you, you shall cross land or sea to do my bidding

scenes.title: Council and Mina's resolve
scenes.summary: The party decides Mina must be in full confidence. Mina vows she will die if she becomes a danger; Van Helsing forbids it.
scenes.key_quote: You must not die. You must not die by any hand; but least of all by your own.

scenes.title: Van Helsing's plan of the day
scenes.summary: Explains daylight limits the Count; arranges the locksmith ruse, cabs rather than a heraldic carriage and a split of forces.
scenes.key_quote: He cannot melt into thin air nor disappear through cracks or chinks or crannies. If he go through a doorway, he must open the door like a mortal.

scenes.title: The Wafer burns Mina
scenes.summary: Van Helsing touches the Sacred Wafer to her forehead; it sears a mark like white-hot metal.
scenes.key_quote: it had seared it—had burned into the flesh as though it had been a piece of white-hot metal.

scenes.title: The oath
scenes.summary: All kneel, hold hands and swear to be true to each other and to raise the veil from Mina.
scenes.key_quote: We men pledged ourselves to raise the veil of sorrow from the head of her whom, each in his own way, we loved

scenes.title: Sterilising Carfax
scenes.summary: With screwdriver and wrench Van Helsing opens each earth-box, lays a piece of Host on the soil and screws the lid down.
scenes.key_quote: Thus we defeat him with his own weapon, for we make it more holy still.

scenes.title: Waiting in the Green Park
scenes.location: Green Park opposite the Piccadilly house
scenes.summary: The trio smoke cigars on a bench while Godalming and Morris bring a locksmith.
scenes.key_quote: We sat down on a bench within good view, and began to smoke cigars so as to attract as little attention as possible.

scenes.title: The locksmith
scenes.summary: A workman tries a selection of keys, opens the door, cuts a new key, is paid and leaves unnoticed.
scenes.key_quote: not a soul took the slightest notice of the whole transaction.

scenes.title: Search of the Piccadilly house
scenes.summary: Eight of nine boxes found in the dining-room and sanctified; the Count's effects are examined; keys taken to Bermondsey and Mile End.
scenes.key_quote: Eight boxes only out of the nine, which we sought!

scenes.title: Van Helsing on the Count's nature
scenes.summary: Van Helsing explains the Count was soldier, statesman and alchemist, a child-brain growing, now experimenting, including moving boxes himself.
scenes.key_quote: He dared even to attend the Scholomance, and there was no branch of knowledge of his time that he did not essay.

scenes.title: Mina's telegram
scenes.summary: Telegraph boy delivers a warning that the Count left Carfax at 12:45 for the south.
scenes.key_quote: Look out for D. He has just now, 12:45, come from Carfax hurriedly and hastened towards the South.

scenes.title: Godalming and Quincey return
scenes.summary: Both lairs found, six boxes in each destroyed.
scenes.key_quote: We found both places; six boxes in each and we destroyed them all!

scenes.title: The ambush
scenes.summary: Quincey positions the party; the Count bounds in, Harker's kukri cuts his coat spilling money, crucifix and Wafer drive him back, he dives through the window and escapes via the stable.
scenes.key_quote: There was something so panther-like in the movement—something so unhuman

scenes.title: The Count's threat
scenes.summary: He taunts them and bolts the stable door behind him, vanishing.
scenes.key_quote: My revenge is just begun! I spread it over centuries, and time is on my side.

scenes.title: Clearing the house
scenes.summary: Van Helsing pockets the remaining money, takes the title deeds and burns the rest in the fireplace.
scenes.key_quote: swept the remaining things into the open fireplace, where he set fire to them with a match.

scenes.title: Mina's plea for pity
scenes.summary: Over supper Mina asks them to be pitiful to the Count's soul; Jonathan, in rage, wishes his soul in hell; she rebukes him tenderly.
scenes.key_quote: it is not a work of hate. That poor soul who has wrought all this misery is the saddest case of all.

scenes.title: Night watch
scenes.summary: Van Helsing fixes the room and places a bell; the men take watches, Quincey lying on a mattress outside the door.
scenes.key_quote: One of us will be here all night. We don’t mean to take any chances!

scenes.title: Hypnotic trance
scenes.summary: Mina asks to be hypnotised. In trance at sunrise she reports darkness, lapping water, men stamping overhead, a chain and capstan; she is on a ship.
scenes.key_quote: The lapping of water. It is gurgling by, and little waves leap. I can hear them on the outside.

scenes.title: The deduction
scenes.summary: Van Helsing concludes the Count has taken his last box aboard a ship; he warns Mina that the Count can wait centuries while she is mortal.
scenes.key_quote: he can live for centuries, and you are but mortal woman.

scenes.title: Van Helsing's phonograph message
scenes.summary: Message left for Harker: the Count has returned toward his Castle; stay with Mina.
scenes.key_quote: He, our enemy, have gone away; he have gone back to his Castle in Transylvania.

scenes.title: Harker and Mina reread the diaries
scenes.summary: The scar on Mina's forehead prevents any disbelief.
scenes.key_quote: Whilst that lasts, there can be no disbelief.

scenes.title: Search at Lloyd's and Doolittle's Wharf
scenes.summary: Lloyd's list shows a single Black Sea ship leaving on the tide; at the wharf a bribe loosens the foreman's tongue.
scenes.key_quote: only one Black-Sea-bound ship go out with the tide. She is the Czarina Catherine

scenes.title: The Count loads his box (reported)
scenes.summary: The thin man in straw hat arranges passage, drives a cart with a great box, lifts it down himself, argues with the captain, then returns at full tide as fog covers the ship.
scenes.key_quote: A thin mist began to creep up from the river, and it grew, and grew; till soon a dense fog enveloped the ship and all around her.

scenes.title: Report meeting
scenes.summary: Van Helsing reports, explains Ristics the agent at Varna, argues the necessity of pursuit and compares the Count to a man-eater.
scenes.key_quote: This that we hunt from our village is a tiger, too, a man-eater, and he never cease to prowl.

scenes.title: Mina's mirror
scenes.summary: Feeling peace, Mina sees the red mark in the mirror and knows she is still unclean.
scenes.key_quote: I caught sight in the mirror of the red mark upon my forehead; and I knew that I was still unclean.

scenes.title: Van Helsing and Seward decide to exclude Mina
scenes.summary: They see vampire traits in Mina - sharper teeth, hard eyes, silences - and decide she must be kept out of plans.
scenes.key_quote: Madam Mina, our poor, dear Madam Mina is changing.

scenes.title: Plan of Campaign
scenes.summary: Overland journey to Varna in three days against a voyage of three weeks; leave by 17th at latest; add Winchesters.
scenes.key_quote: we must leave here on 17th at latest.

scenes.title: Mina's promise
scenes.summary: Mina makes Jonathan promise not to tell her the plans; a door shuts between them.
scenes.key_quote: I felt that from that instant a door had been shut between us.

scenes.title: Mina insists on going
scenes.summary: At sunrise, while she can speak freely, she says the Count's will compels her and she is safer with the party.
scenes.key_quote: I know that when the Count wills me I must go.

scenes.title: The wild-rose plan and wills
scenes.location: Van Helsing's room, then Harkers' room
scenes.summary: Van Helsing proposes to board the ship, place a wild-rose branch on the box and open it when unseen; Quincey will not wait. Harker makes his will.
scenes.key_quote: we shall place a branch of the wild rose on it. This we shall fasten, for when it is there none can emerge

scenes.title: The Oath at Sunset
scenes.location: Seward's asylum sitting room, Mrs. Harker's sofa
scenes.summary: In her half-hour of freedom before sunset Mina asks every man to promise to kill her by stake and decapitation when she is changed beyond saving, and to read the Burial Service over her. Quincey kneels first; all swear, Jonathan last. Jonathan reads the service while the group kneels.
scenes.key_quote: You must promise me, one and all—even you, my beloved husband—that, should the time come, you will kill me.

scenes.title: Journey to Varna
scenes.summary: The party leaves London on the 12th, takes the Orient Express from Paris and arrives at Varna on the 15th at about five o'clock. Mina sleeps almost the entire trip.
scenes.key_quote: We travelled night and day, arriving here at about five o’clock.

scenes.title: Hypnotic Watch at the Hotel Odessus
scenes.summary: Each dawn and dusk Van Helsing hypnotises Mina by will with little effort and asks what she sees and hears. She always reports lapping waves, rushing water, creaking masts. Godalming gets daily telegrams from Lloyd's: 'not reported'.
scenes.key_quote: I can hear the waves lapping against the ship, and the water rushing by.

scenes.title: Arranging the Boarding
scenes.location: Varna shippers' office and the agent's office
scenes.summary: Godalming tells the shippers the box may contain something stolen from a friend and gets half consent, plus a paper for the Captain and the Varna agent. The plan is fixed: Van Helsing and Seward behead and stake; Morris, Godalming and Harker keep off interference with arms.
scenes.key_quote: If the Count is there, Van Helsing and Seward will cut off his head at once and drive a stake through his heart.

scenes.title: Kukri Whetting and Mina's Lethargy
scenes.summary: Seward finds Harker whetting the Ghoorka knife. Mina falls into an unwakeable lethargy at noon; the doctors check and let her sleep. Van Helsing inspects her teeth under hypnosis to see whether they sharpen.
scenes.key_quote: an hour ago I found him whetting the edge of the great Ghoorka knife which he now always carries with him.

scenes.title: News of Galatz
scenes.summary: Telegram: the Czarina Catherine has entered Galatz, not Varna. Everyone reacts differently. Mina supplies the train time. Van Helsing assigns tasks: tickets, agent letters, vice-consul introductions.
scenes.key_quote: “At 6:30 to-morrow morning!” We all started, for the answer came from Mrs. Harker.

scenes.title: The Criminal Mind Lecture
scenes.summary: Van Helsing privately tells Seward that the Count has cut Mina off after learning through her trance that they were in Varna. Mina brings typed copies of Harker's castle journal; Van Helsing and Mina deduce the Count is a 'child-brained' criminal who repeats habit - fleeing home to return better equipped.
scenes.key_quote: The criminal always work at one crime—that is the true criminal who seems predestinate to crime.

scenes.title: Failing Trances on the Train
scenes.summary: Mina's reports: still water against the hawser, men calling, oars, a gun, light and wind; later cold wind passing and wolves; at dawn cattle lowing. Each trance is harder; sunrise cuts her off mid-sentence.
scenes.key_quote: Something is going out; I can feel it pass me like a cold wind.

scenes.title: Captain Donelson's Tale
scenes.location: Aboard the Czarina Catherine, anchored in the river harbour at Galatz
scenes.summary: The Scots captain describes the fog that travelled with the ship, the superstitious Roumanian crew making the sign against the evil eye at the old man who loaded the box, his handspike quelling the mutiny, and the receiver arriving before sun-up with papers for Count Dracula.
scenes.key_quote: It’s no canny to run frae London to the Black Sea wi’ a wind ahint ye, as though the Deil himself were blawin’ on yer sail

scenes.title: Hildesheim and Skinsky
scenes.location: Hildesheim's office, Burgen-strasse 16; Skinsky's neighbourhood; St. Peter's churchyard wall
scenes.summary: Bribed, Hildesheim reveals a letter from Mr. de Ville; box given to Skinsky; paid by English bank note cashed at the Danube International Bank. Skinsky has left, key and rent sent by messenger; his body is found with throat torn open.
scenes.key_quote: the body of Skinsky had been found inside the wall of the churchyard of St. Peter, and that the throat had been torn open as if by some wild animal.

scenes.title: Mina's Memorandum
scenes.summary: While the men rest, Mina types up everything, studies maps and writes a memorandum by exclusion (road, rail, water) concluding the Count goes by water upriver, probably the Sereth then the Bistritza near Fundu.
scenes.key_quote: We know from the record that he was on the water; so what we have to do is to ascertain what water.

scenes.title: Council of War
scenes.summary: Party divides: launch, horsemen, and Van Helsing with Mina through Bistritz and the Borgo Pass to the castle. Jonathan protests passionately, then yields. Money produces launch, horses, maps within three hours.
scenes.key_quote: Not for the world! Not for Heaven or Hell!

scenes.title: Steam Launch Pursuit
scenes.summary: They steam night and day, overhaul every boat, fly a Roumanian flag at Fundu to be treated as officials, and are delayed by a rapids accident.
scenes.key_quote: The men were scared every time we turned our electric lamp on them, and fell on their knees and prayed.

scenes.title: Horseback Along the Bank
scenes.summary: Three days on the road, news at Fundu that the launch went up the Bistritza, snow threatens; they would take a sledge if needed.
scenes.key_quote: In such case we must get a sledge and go on, Russian fashion.

scenes.title: Veresti Departure
scenes.summary: Van Helsing buys carriage, horses and furs; landlady packs a huge provision basket. Mina writes a farewell thought to Jonathan.
scenes.key_quote: We are truly in the hands of God.

scenes.title: Driving to the Borgo Pass
scenes.location: Road from Veresti to the Carpathians
scenes.summary: They change horses often, pay farmers, eat hot soup. Villagers make the sign of the evil eye at Mina's scar and add garlic to the food. A rude four-in-hand is assembled.
scenes.key_quote: she crossed herself and put out two fingers towards me, to keep off the evil eye.

scenes.title: Mina Knows the Way
scenes.location: Borgo Pass and the old by-road
scenes.summary: At the Pass Mina sees the right road from Jonathan's journal. She sleeps all day; at dusk she is suspiciously bright and says she has already eaten.
scenes.key_quote: “Have not my Jonathan travelled it and wrote of his travel?”

scenes.title: The Holy Circle Night
scenes.location: Camp below Castle Dracula, snow and mist
scenes.summary: Van Helsing draws a ring and crumbles the Host over it; Mina cannot step out. The horses scream and cower; mist and snow form the three women who beg Mina to come. Van Helsing holds firewood and wafer toward them; at dawn they dissolve and the horses are found dead.
scenes.key_quote: “Come, sister. Come to us. Come! Come!”

scenes.title: Staking the Brides
scenes.summary: Van Helsing breaks open the rusted doors with the blacksmith's hammer, finds the chapel, searches tombs, resists the fascination, hears Mina's wail, and stakes and beheads all three. He places wafer in Dracula's empty tomb and seals the castle entrances.
scenes.key_quote: Oh, my friend John, but it was butcher work

scenes.title: The Hollow in the Rocks
scenes.location: Rocky hollow downhill from the castle
scenes.summary: They descend, rest, and Van Helsing finds a natural hollow between two boulders as a shelter, draws a circle around the rock, and sights the approaching gypsies and the pursuers through field glasses.
scenes.key_quote: here you will be in shelter; and if the wolves do come I can meet them one by one.

scenes.title: Pursuit Across the Snow
scenes.location: Snowy slopes toward the Borgo Pass
scenes.summary: The launch group abandons the boat and takes horses; Seward sees the Szgany with the leiter-wagon racing from the river, wolves howling.
scenes.key_quote: We ride to death of some one.

scenes.title: The Final Battle at Sunset
scenes.location: Plain below Dracula's castle, between the hollow and the road
scenes.summary: Four men with Winchesters surround the gypsies; Van Helsing and Mina cover from the rock. Jonathan and Quincey break through the knife ring, throw the box from the cart, pry the lid with kukri and bowie; as the sun touches the mountains Jonathan cuts the Count's throat and Quincey stabs his heart; he turns to dust. Gypsies flee, wolves follow.
scenes.key_quote: before our very eyes, and almost in the drawing of a breath, the whole body crumbled into dust and passed from our sight.

scenes.title: Quincey's Death
scenes.summary: Wounded in the side, Morris is held by Jonathan; the setting sun lights Mina's forehead, now unmarked. He dies content.
scenes.key_quote: See! the snow is not more stainless than her forehead! The curse has passed away!

scenes.title: The journey back to Transylvania
scenes.summary: Every trace of what had been is blotted out; the castle stands as before above a waste of desolation.
scenes.key_quote: Every trace of all that had been was blotted out.

scenes.title: Van Helsing with the boy
scenes.summary: The papers are taken from the safe; Van Helsing declares no proofs are needed.
scenes.key_quote: We want no proofs. We ask none to believe us!

puzzles.name: The circling carriage
puzzles.setup: The calèche seems to loop back on the same road near midnight.
puzzles.obstacle: Harker is disoriented and unable to ask the driver.
puzzles.book_solution: He takes note of a salient point and confirms they are going in circles; the driver is stalling until midnight.
puzzles.game_idea: Memorise landmarks on a looping route to detect the stall; choose to speak up or stay silent.
puzzles.quote: I took note of some salient point, and found that this was so.

puzzles.name: Reading the village words
puzzles.setup: The crowd repeats strange words around Harker.
puzzles.book_solution: Harker looks them up in his polyglot dictionary.
puzzles.game_idea: Collect overheard words and match them in a dictionary UI to unlock lore entries.
puzzles.quote: I quietly got my polyglot dictionary from my bag and looked them out.

puzzles.name: Reading the road for the missing carriage
puzzles.setup: No carriage at the pass an hour before the stated time.
puzzles.obstacle: Driver wants to carry Harker on to Bukovina.
puzzles.book_solution: Dracula arrives and overrides the driver.
puzzles.game_idea: Timing puzzle: be at the pass at the right moment, choose to board the coach or wait.
puzzles.quote: “An hour less than the time.”

puzzles.name: No reflection
puzzles.setup: Harker shaves with a hand mirror.
puzzles.book_solution: Harker turns around and sees him but not in the glass; he notices blood.
puzzles.game_idea: Detection mini-game: use a mirror to identify who in a room is a vampire.
puzzles.quote: But there was no reflection of him in the mirror!

puzzles.name: The castle of locked doors
puzzles.setup: Explore the castle by day.
puzzles.obstacle: Every door locked or bolted; the great door key is missing.
puzzles.book_solution: Not solved; Harker only finds a south room with a view.
puzzles.game_idea: Maze of locked doors with key-hunting across later chapters; safe vs unsafe areas.
puzzles.quote: doors, doors, doors everywhere, and all locked and bolted

puzzles.name: Finding a bell and servants
puzzles.setup: Look for a way to call the servants.
puzzles.book_solution: Harker infers the Count does everything himself.
puzzles.game_idea: Observation puzzle collecting clues that the castle is empty (no bell, no mirror, no servants, fresh logs).
puzzles.quote: I looked for a bell, so that I might let the servants know I had finished; but I could not find one.

puzzles.name: Reading Dracula's atlas
puzzles.setup: Atlas lies open at England.
puzzles.book_solution: Harker notes London east, Exeter, Whitby.
puzzles.game_idea: Clue item that reveals future-chapter locations.
puzzles.quote: on examining these I noticed that one was near London on the east side

puzzles.name: Hinge-sagging door
puzzles.setup: A door at the top of the stairway seems locked.
puzzles.book_solution: Harker recognises the fallen hinges and forces it by repeated effort.
puzzles.game_idea: Physics puzzle: lift or wedge a sagging door to move it past its dropped hinges.
puzzles.quote: it was not really locked, but that the resistance came from the fact that the hinges had fallen somewhat

puzzles.name: Hall door with key missing
puzzles.setup: Bolts and chains easy but door locked.
puzzles.book_solution: Not solved; Harker infers the key is in the Count's room.
puzzles.game_idea: Multi-chapter key quest.
puzzles.quote: the door was locked, and the key was gone!

puzzles.name: Reading letters undetected
