puzzles.setup: Count's letters left face down.
puzzles.book_solution: Read addresses and replace them as found when the door-handle moves.
puzzles.game_idea: Stealth puzzle with a timer: read as many addresses as possible and restore state before the door opens.
puzzles.quote: I had just time to replace the letters as they had been

puzzles.name: Hidden writing
puzzles.setup: Count will read the letters.
puzzles.obstacle: Harker needs to warn people secretly.
puzzles.book_solution: Writes formal notes openly and uses shorthand for Mina.
puzzles.game_idea: Cipher puzzle: communicate only via a code the villain cannot read.
puzzles.quote: to her I could write in shorthand, which would puzzle the Count

puzzles.name: Observing the wall-crawl
puzzles.setup: Watching the Count from the stair window.
puzzles.obstacle: Angle of sight; he vanishes into a hole.
puzzles.book_solution: Harker watches from behind the stone mullion, then tries leaning out.
puzzles.game_idea: Stealth observation: hide behind stonework to track the Count's route.
puzzles.quote: I drew back behind the stonework, and looked carefully out.

puzzles.name: Smuggling a letter out
puzzles.setup: Szgany camp in the courtyard.
puzzles.obstacle: Harker is locked in with bars on the window; the Count may intercept.
puzzles.book_solution: Throws letters and a gold piece through the bars; the Szgany hands them to the Count.
puzzles.game_idea: Trust puzzle: choose which of several NPCs to pass the message; risk of betrayal.
puzzles.quote: The man who took them pressed them to his heart and bowed, and then put them in his cap.

puzzles.name: Reaching the Count's room by the ledge
puzzles.setup: The Count's door is locked.
puzzles.obstacle: A narrow ledge above the abyss.
puzzles.book_solution: Remove boots, traverse the ledge without looking down, enter by the sash window.
puzzles.game_idea: Balance/climbing mini-game with a vertigo meter and boots-off modifier.
puzzles.quote: I took off my boots, and ventured out on the desperate way.

puzzles.name: Searching the Count for the key
puzzles.setup: Count asleep in the box.
puzzles.book_solution: Searches the body; no key found.
puzzles.game_idea: Risk/reward search with a chance of waking the vampire.
puzzles.quote: I knew I must reach the body for the key

puzzles.name: Finding the chapel route
puzzles.setup: Count's room has a corner door.
puzzles.book_solution: Follow the stone passage, circular stair, tunnel and chapel by the smell of turned earth.
puzzles.game_idea: Navigation by scent clue.
puzzles.quote: the odour of old earth newly turned

puzzles.name: Choosing the date on the letters
puzzles.setup: Count asks for three letters.
puzzles.book_solution: Harker complies and asks what dates.
puzzles.game_idea: Dialogue choice with countdown to 29 June.
puzzles.quote: I asked him what dates I should put on the letters.

puzzles.name: The mock release test
puzzles.setup: Count offers to let him leave at once.
puzzles.book_solution: Harker shouts to shut the door and waits till morning.
puzzles.game_idea: Trap detection: decide whether the offered exit is safe.
puzzles.quote: Shut the door; I shall wait till morning!

puzzles.name: Breaking out when the stair door slams
puzzles.setup: Harker is in the Count's room as the workmen arrive.
puzzles.obstacle: A gust of wind blows the stair door shut and fast.
puzzles.book_solution: Fails; he waits and listens.
puzzles.game_idea: Timing puzzle: slip past the workmen before the exit closes.
puzzles.quote: I found that it was hopelessly fast.

puzzles.name: Reading Renfield's fixed idea
puzzles.setup: Seward questions Renfield to understand a hallucination whose centre he cannot identify.
puzzles.obstacle: Renfield's delusion is concealed behind gloom and excitability.
puzzles.book_solution: Seward pushes the patient to his point of madness and records observations; mystery unresolved.
puzzles.game_idea: Dialogue-deduction puzzle: choose questions to narrow Renfield's fixed idea while a cruelty meter rises and he closes up.
puzzles.quote: I questioned him more fully than I had ever done, with a view to making myself master of the facts of his hallucination.

puzzles.name: Renfield's chain of lives
puzzles.setup: Renfield's pets keep vanishing and growing in size.
puzzles.obstacle: Seward must decode the pattern behind the madness.
puzzles.book_solution: Seward watches the diminishing flies and spiders, finds the sparrows' feathers and blood, sedates Renfield and reads his notebook.
puzzles.game_idea: Deduction board: arrange pet counts over days to reveal the food chain and predict Renfield's next demand; success unlocks the diagnosis and lets the player pre-empt his next move.
puzzles.quote: He gave many flies to one spider and many spiders to one bird, and then wanted a cat to eat the many birds.

puzzles.name: Reading Whitby's tombstones
puzzles.setup: Swales claims half the stones are lies.
puzzles.obstacle: Find which gravestones are true or cenotaphs.
puzzles.book_solution: Swales reads inscriptions and tells stories behind them.
puzzles.game_idea: Investigation mini-game: read inscriptions, compare death places with burial and tell true graves from empty ones (and spot where new vampire graves would appear).
puzzles.quote: there be scores of these lay-beds that be toom as old Dun's 'bacca-box on Friday night.

puzzles.name: Locked room vs sleepwalker
puzzles.setup: Lucy walks at night.
puzzles.obstacle: Keep Lucy inside; she hunts for the key.
puzzles.book_solution: Mina locks the door every night; Lucy searches for the key.
puzzles.game_idea: Stealth/guard mini-game at night: hide the key, listen for movement and keep the sleepwalker safe before she reaches the cliff.
puzzles.quote: She tries the door, and finding it locked, goes about the room searching for the key.

puzzles.name: Reading the weather and the ship
puzzles.setup: A storm approaches and a strange ship wanders.
puzzles.book_solution: Coastguard observes with spy-glass, judges it Russian and badly steered.
puzzles.game_idea: Watch-tower observation puzzle: collect signs (sky colour, ship behaviour, fishermen) to forecast the ship's arrival.
puzzles.quote: She is steered mighty strangely, for she doesn't mind the hand on the wheel.

puzzles.name: Searching the ship
puzzles.setup: Crew believes a stranger is aboard.
puzzles.obstacle: A hidden presence with no hiding places except big boxes.
puzzles.book_solution: Whole crew with lanterns search stem to stern; find only the boxes.
puzzles.game_idea: Sweep-search puzzle on a ship cross-section: track light radius, mark rooms cleared and note which boxes cannot be opened yet.
puzzles.quote: we left no corner unsearched. As there were only the big wooden boxes

puzzles.name: Reading the weather
puzzles.setup: Mares'-tails, sunset colours and dead calm.
puzzles.obstacle: Predict the storm to protect boats.
puzzles.book_solution: An old fisherman and the coastguard read the signs and warn captains.
puzzles.game_idea: Observation puzzle: match sky signs to forecast and decide which boats to hold in harbour.
puzzles.quote: a sudden show of 'mares'-tails' high in the sky to the north-west

puzzles.name: Searchlight rescue
puzzles.setup: Boats run for harbour in tempest and fog.
puzzles.obstacle: Guide each boat past the piers.
puzzles.book_solution: The new searchlight sweeps the surface and lights the harbour mouth.
puzzles.game_idea: Real-time sweep mini-game: aim a searchlight beam to mark rocks and entrances as boats approach.
puzzles.quote: able, by the guidance of the sheltering light, to avoid the danger of dashing against the piers.

puzzles.name: The captain's last log
puzzles.setup: Corpse tied to wheel with bottle in pocket.
puzzles.book_solution: Inquest reads the log and bottle paper; verdict open.
puzzles.game_idea: Forensic reconstruction: sort dated entries, match vanished crew to times and bind the mystery into a timeline.
puzzles.quote: Of course the verdict was an open one. There is no evidence to adduce.

puzzles.name: The box in the hold
puzzles.setup: Mate says It is in a box.
puzzles.book_solution: Mate unscrews one with a tool-chest and flees screaming.
puzzles.game_idea: Risky unscrew puzzle: choose which box to open under time pressure; one holds the creature's earth.
puzzles.quote: I'll unscrew them one by one and see.

puzzles.name: Where has Lucy gone?
puzzles.setup: Lucy's bed is empty at night.
puzzles.obstacle: Deduce where a sleepwalker goes from her clothes and the doors.
puzzles.book_solution: Mina notes dressing-gown and dress still in place so she is in nightdress; the hall door catch is unfastened; checks rooms; scans from the West Cliff for the favourite seat.
puzzles.game_idea: Night search puzzle: examine wardrobe, doors and windows for clues to narrow the route, then race the clock across Whitby.
puzzles.quote: Dressing-gown would mean house; dress, outside.

puzzles.name: Shadow run across Whitby
puzzles.setup: Moon and clouds alternately reveal and hide the churchyard.
puzzles.obstacle: Reach the seat before it is too late, via stairs, fish-market and the single bridge.
puzzles.book_solution: Mina flies down the steps to the pier and fish-market, over the bridge and up the endless steps.
puzzles.game_idea: Timed traversal: move only when cloud shadow covers you or when the figure is looking away; stamina bar on the steps.
puzzles.quote: the bridge, which was the only way to reach the East Cliff

puzzles.name: Waking and concealing Lucy
puzzles.setup: Lucy is cold, barefoot and in a nightdress in a churchyard; people may see.
puzzles.book_solution: Shawl, safety-pin, shoes on Lucy, muddy feet for Mina, hide in a doorway from a drunk man.
puzzles.game_idea: Stealth escort: guide Lucy home dodging passers-by, hiding in doorways and wynds.
puzzles.quote: we hid in a door till he had disappeared up an opening

puzzles.name: Securing the sleepwalker
puzzles.setup: Lucy keeps trying the door and window.
puzzles.obstacle: Locked door isn't enough; she goes to the window.
puzzles.book_solution: Key tied to Mina's wrist, window fastened; Lucy still opens it later.
puzzles.game_idea: Room-security puzzle: lock the door, fasten windows, set a watch; discover each lock fails against the vampire's summons until you add wards.
puzzles.quote: I keep the key of our door always fastened to my wrist at night

puzzles.name: Diagnosing the wounds
puzzles.setup: Lucy's throat marks don't heal.
puzzles.obstacle: Find the true cause rather than the safety-pin.
puzzles.book_solution: Mina attributes them to the pin; unresolved.
puzzles.game_idea: Clue-comparison: match wound spacing and appearance to pin vs bite; choose to call a doctor.
puzzles.quote: the tiny wounds seem not to have healed. They are still open, and, if anything, larger than before

puzzles.name: Catching Renfield
puzzles.setup: Renfield flees out of a window into Carfax.
puzzles.obstacle: A strong lunatic must be tracked, followed over a wall and subdued without scaring him.
puzzles.book_solution: Seward squeezes out feet-first, the attendant watches the direction, a ladder crosses the wall, men surround and overpower him.
puzzles.game_idea: Chase and corner encounter: track his path across the grounds, set men at exits and avoid spooking him before closing the net.
puzzles.quote: Chasing an errant swarm of bees is nothing to following a naked lunatic

puzzles.name: Delivery orders for Carfax
puzzles.setup: Fifty boxes must reach the chapel.
puzzles.book_solution: Train 9:30 p.m., due 4:30 p.m. next day, teams ready, boxes to chapel 'A'.
puzzles.game_idea: Logistics puzzle for the opposing side or an investigator tracking the boxes by paperwork.
puzzles.quote: The goods leave by the train at 9:30 to-night, and will be due at King's Cross at 4:30 to-morrow afternoon.

puzzles.name: Why does Renfield rest only at night?
puzzles.setup: Renfield alternates between violence and calm in a daily pattern.
puzzles.obstacle: Find the cause of his moods.
puzzles.book_solution: Seward notes the pattern, lets him escape under watch, and links paroxysms to noon and sunset.
puzzles.game_idea: Timeline puzzle: log Renfield's behaviour over several in-game days to deduce the timing pattern and predict his next episode.
puzzles.quote: Can it be that there is a malign influence of the sun at periods

puzzles.name: Diagnose Lucy
puzzles.setup: Lucy is pale and weak with no disease.
puzzles.obstacle: Rule out anaemia and find the cause.
puzzles.book_solution: Seward tests the blood from a cut; Van Helsing examines her and concludes blood has been lost but she is not anaemic.
puzzles.game_idea: Clue-collecting diagnosis mini-game: examine symptoms, run blood test, question the maid, choose a hypothesis.
puzzles.quote: there has been much blood lost; it has been, but is not.

puzzles.name: Hidden throat marks
puzzles.setup: A velvet band hides the cause of Lucy's blood loss.
puzzles.obstacle: Discover the cause without alarming others.
puzzles.book_solution: Van Helsing sees the red mark when the band is dragged up; Seward loosens the band and examines the punctures.
puzzles.game_idea: Examine-inspect puzzle: move the band without waking Lucy, then compare puncture spacing against a clue card.
puzzles.quote: The velvet band again covered the red mark.

puzzles.name: Seal the bedroom
puzzles.setup: A visitor enters Lucy's room at night.
puzzles.book_solution: Latch the windows, rub garlic on sashes, door jamb and fireplace, and hang a garlic wreath.
puzzles.game_idea: Room-sealing puzzle: find all entries (window, door, chimney) and ward each within a limited quantity of garlic.
puzzles.quote: he rubbed them all over the sashes, as though to ensure that every whiff of air that might get in would be laden with the garlic smell

puzzles.name: Who gives blood?
puzzles.setup: Lucy needs a transfusion; donors differ in strength.
puzzles.obstacle: Pick the donor and keep it secret from Mrs. Westenra and Arthur.
puzzles.book_solution: Seward volunteers, Arthur supplants him; later Seward gives blood and takes only a measured amount.
puzzles.game_idea: Resource-management: donor health bars limit how much can be transfused each night.
puzzles.quote: You took a great deal more from Art.

puzzles.name: Keep the garlic in place
puzzles.setup: The household doesn't know why the garlic matters.
puzzles.obstacle: Mrs. Westenra removes it and opens the window.
puzzles.book_solution: Van Helsing instructs her not to touch anything; the failure happens before the warning.
puzzles.game_idea: Defensive-time puzzle: use dialogue and notes to persuade NPCs not to disturb wards; ward integrity changes nightly.
puzzles.quote: she must not remove anything from Lucy's room without consulting him

puzzles.name: Which animal escaped and why
puzzles.setup: A wolf escaped and returned with cut head.
puzzles.obstacle: Link the stranger to Bersicker's escape.
puzzles.book_solution: Reporter interview yields description of the stranger, the moonrise howling and glass-cut head.
puzzles.game_idea: Interview-clue puzzle: bribe or befriend the keeper to extract the stranger's description.
puzzles.quote: I took a sort of mislike to him

puzzles.name: Who drugged the maids?
puzzles.setup: Four maids lie unconscious.
puzzles.book_solution: Lucy smells laudanum in the decanter and finds the medicine bottle empty.
puzzles.game_idea: Smell and inspect puzzle on a sideboard.
puzzles.quote: It smelt of laudanum

puzzles.name: Break into the locked house
puzzles.setup: All doors and windows locked, servants unresponsive.
puzzles.book_solution: Saw through bars at the kitchen window, then slide a thin knife in to lift the sash catch.
puzzles.game_idea: Lockpicking/entry puzzle: pick the weakest point of the house and use the right tool.
puzzles.quote: I attacked them at once and had very soon cut through three of them.

puzzles.name: Revive the frozen victim
puzzles.setup: Lucy is cold, near death.
puzzles.obstacle: Restore body heat before a transfusion.
puzzles.book_solution: Brandy rubs, wake maids, heat water, warm bath, hot sheet, brandy drops.
puzzles.game_idea: Sequenced task: gather resources in the right order within turns while the patient's vitality ticks down.
puzzles.quote: She will need be heated before we can do anything more.

puzzles.name: Test for tampering
puzzles.setup: The decanter was drugged.
puzzles.book_solution: Smell and taste brandy before use.
puzzles.game_idea: Item-verification step before using consumables.
puzzles.quote: taking care to smell and taste it, lest it, too, were drugged

puzzles.name: The vanishing wounds
puzzles.setup: Wounds disappear before death.
puzzles.book_solution: Van Helsing lifts the handkerchief in light and sees them gone.
puzzles.game_idea: Inspection mini-game: compare wound states between nights to deduce the stage.
puzzles.quote: The wounds on the throat had absolutely disappeared.

puzzles.name: Deduce the blood count
puzzles.setup: Quincey asks what took the blood.
puzzles.book_solution: Quincey totals the donors and recalls the vampire bat.
puzzles.game_idea: Deduction board linking donors, nights and symptoms.
puzzles.quote: What took it out?

puzzles.name: The stolen crucifix
puzzles.setup: The golden crucifix placed on Lucy's mouth is gone in the morning.
puzzles.obstacle: Who took it and how to get it back; Lucy's coffin is unguarded.
puzzles.book_solution: Van Helsing recovers it from a thieving woman without punishing her.
puzzles.game_idea: A theft-investigation scene: check the room, interview staff, track the missing ward before a night encounter.
puzzles.quote: I get it back from the worthless wretch who stole it

puzzles.name: The solicitor's will
puzzles.setup: Mrs. Westenra's papers must be found and sealed.
puzzles.obstacle: Locate the solicitor name and address in an orderly desk.
puzzles.book_solution: Seward finds the name and address within half an hour and writes to him.
puzzles.game_idea: Desk-search puzzle: sort papers into legal / personal; hide the personal ones.
puzzles.quote: All the poor lady’s papers were in order

puzzles.name: Recognising the Count
puzzles.setup: Mina notices Jonathan's panic in Piccadilly.
puzzles.obstacle: Identify the stranger from clues and track the target.
puzzles.book_solution: Jonathan recognises him, a hansom carries the man away.
puzzles.game_idea: Stealth/tail mini-game: follow the dark man through Piccadilly without being seen.
puzzles.quote: “Do you see who it is?”

puzzles.name: Shorthand joke
puzzles.setup: Mina hands Van Helsing a shorthand diary.
puzzles.book_solution: She gives the typed copy.
puzzles.game_idea: A decoding mini-game: transcribe symbols to type a readable document before the visitor arrives.
puzzles.quote: I know not the shorthand.

puzzles.name: Train planning
puzzles.setup: Van Helsing needs to get back to London.
puzzles.book_solution: Mina cites exact trains and updates by letter.
puzzles.game_idea: Schedule puzzle: reorder train times so characters meet or avoid each other.
puzzles.quote: you could catch the quick 3:34 train

puzzles.name: Making Seward believe
puzzles.setup: Van Helsing must convince a sceptical scientist.
puzzles.book_solution: List of natural wonders and a request for open belief.
puzzles.game_idea: Persuasion dialogue puzzle: pick the right analogies to unlock Seward's belief.
puzzles.quote: I want you to believe.

puzzles.name: The empty coffin
puzzles.setup: Seward doubts Van Helsing; the coffin lid is unscrewed and a lead liner cut open.
puzzles.obstacle: Cut through lead without damaging; avoid gas.
puzzles.book_solution: Turnscrew punctures lead, fret-saw cuts two feet and across, flap bent back.
puzzles.game_idea: A timed lockpicking-style puzzle: cut through coffin liner without wasting candle or alerting the sexton.
puzzles.quote: he sawed down a couple of feet along one side of the lead coffin

puzzles.name: Falling lock vs spring lock
puzzles.setup: Entering the tomb at night.
puzzles.book_solution: Van Helsing checks lock type before closing the door.
puzzles.game_idea: Inspect the lock mechanism before entering or risk being trapped.
puzzles.quote: the lock was a falling, and not a spring, one.

puzzles.name: Hospital to churchyard timing
puzzles.setup: Sunset catches them.
puzzles.obstacle: Must be in position before midnight.
puzzles.book_solution: Dine, then walk by lamps.
puzzles.game_idea: Route-planning through dark Hampstead avoiding patrols.
puzzles.quote: patrol of horse police

puzzles.name: Disposing of the child
puzzles.setup: Rescued child; police station would demand statements.
puzzles.book_solution: Leave child on Heath path and watch until policeman finds it.
puzzles.game_idea: Stealth hand-off: drop the child within a patrol's route and slip away unseen.
puzzles.quote: we would then seek our way home as quickly as we could.

puzzles.name: The tomb door seal
puzzles.setup: Keep Lucy inside.
puzzles.book_solution: Garlic and crucifix on the clamps.
puzzles.game_idea: Choose which wards to place on each exit of a tomb.
puzzles.quote: I shall fix some things she like not

puzzles.name: Sealing the tomb
puzzles.setup: Stop Lucy re-entering the tomb until the men are ready.
puzzles.obstacle: Seal narrow door crevices with a ward she will respect.
puzzles.book_solution: Crumble Host with putty and roll thin strips.
puzzles.game_idea: Crafting-and-placement puzzle: fill every gap in a door frame with strips; leave one gap unsealed to let her in at the right time.
puzzles.quote: rolling it into thin strips, began to lay them into the crevices

puzzles.name: Choosing the hunter's hand
puzzles.setup: Who strikes the final blow.
puzzles.book_solution: Van Helsing frames it as a blessed act; Arthur steps forward.
puzzles.game_idea: Dialogue choice giving the killing blow to a party member, with stat effects.
puzzles.quote: Tell me if there be such a one amongst us?

puzzles.name: Soldering the coffin shut
puzzles.setup: Seal lead coffin after the destruction.
puzzles.book_solution: Blue-flame oil lamp heats soldering iron; solder the seam.
puzzles.game_idea: Seam-sealing mini-game: trace the lead seam with the iron without burning.
puzzles.quote: We soldered up the leaden coffin, screwed on the coffin-lid

puzzles.name: Waiting out the sexton
puzzles.setup: Funeral mourners and gate locking.
puzzles.book_solution: Dress in black, stroll about, hide until the gate is locked.
puzzles.game_idea: Timing/stealth puzzle: stay outside the sexton's line of sight until the gate is locked.
puzzles.quote: keeping out of official observation

puzzles.name: Trace the boxes by paperwork
puzzles.setup: Fifty earth boxes landed at Whitby.
puzzles.obstacle: Need to confirm where they went.
puzzles.book_solution: Harker follows invoice, station-masters, carriers' tally and way-bill to Carfax; tips loosen tongues.
puzzles.game_idea: Investigation puzzle: match documents and testimony tallies; each tip unlocks a witness.
puzzles.quote: Here again I found the tally agreeing exactly

puzzles.name: Collate evidence chronologically
puzzles.setup: Diaries, letters, cuttings are scattered.
puzzles.book_solution: Mina types and orders the cylinders and diaries; dates reveal Renfield's outbursts match the Count's visits.
puzzles.game_idea: Timeline puzzle: sort document fragments onto a calendar to reveal a hidden pattern.
puzzles.quote: if we get all our material ready, and have every item put in chronological order, we shall have done much.

puzzles.name: Win Seward's trust
puzzles.setup: Seward refuses to share Lucy's death account.
puzzles.book_solution: Mina shows her own typed diaries.
puzzles.game_idea: Dialogue puzzle: choose proofs of trustworthiness.
puzzles.quote: You do not know me... When you have read those papers... you will know me better.

puzzles.name: Interpreting Renfield
puzzles.setup: Renfield's lucidity and urgency.
puzzles.obstacle: Is his plea madness or a warning?
puzzles.book_solution: Seward and Van Helsing decide to keep him confined.
puzzles.game_idea: Judgement puzzle: weigh testimony and observed behaviour to decide whether to release him; hidden consequences.
puzzles.quote: I am no lunatic in a mad fit, but a sane man fighting for his soul

puzzles.name: Sterilise the earth
puzzles.setup: Fifty boxes across London.
puzzles.obstacle: Boxes must be traced and sanctified.
puzzles.book_solution: Plan only: trace each box; sterilise between sunrise and sunset.
puzzles.game_idea: Map-tracing planning puzzle with timed daylight windows.
puzzles.quote: We must trace each of these boxes

puzzles.name: Lock and key
puzzles.setup: Locked hall door and chapel door.
puzzles.obstacle: Must enter without breaking the house.
puzzles.book_solution: Seward tries skeleton keys until the bolt yields; Jonathan finds the chapel key on the bunch on the hall table.
puzzles.game_idea: Lockpick minigame plus key-matching using the label hints and the map.
puzzles.quote: After a little play back and forward the bolt yielded, and, with a rusty clang, shot back.

puzzles.name: Find the way to the chapel
puzzles.setup: Dark dusty house with wrong turnings.
puzzles.book_solution: Jonathan recalls the layout and checks the map.
puzzles.game_idea: Maze navigation with a map and lamp.
puzzles.quote: after a few wrong turnings found myself opposite a low, arched oaken door

puzzles.name: Count the boxes
puzzles.setup: Chapel with earth chests.
puzzles.obstacle: Finding how many are gone and where they went.
puzzles.book_solution: Count 29 left; disturbed dust shows route out of the outer door.
puzzles.game_idea: Footprint-and-dust trail reading to deduce which boxes left and how.
puzzles.quote: the dust had been much disturbed: the boxes which had been taken out had been brought this way.

puzzles.name: Rat swarm
puzzles.setup: Thousands of rats in the chapel.
puzzles.obstacle: Dogs refuse to cross the threshold.
puzzles.book_solution: Carry each dog in so its feet touch the floor.
puzzles.game_idea: Environmental puzzle: open the outer door, call dogs, and place them inside.
puzzles.quote: Lord Godalming lifted one of the dogs, and carrying him in, placed him on the floor.

puzzles.name: Decode the phonetic address
puzzles.setup: Misspelled directions 'Poters Cort', 'depite'.
puzzles.book_solution: Jonathan reads by sound: Potter's Court, Corcoran's, deputy.
puzzles.game_idea: Word puzzle where the player re-spells phonetic Cockney clues to find places and people.
puzzles.quote: Mr. Smollet’s spelling misled me, as I asked for Poter’s Court instead of Potter’s Court.

puzzles.name: Identify the house
puzzles.setup: Bloxam forgot the number.
puzzles.book_solution: Stone front with bow, high steps, near white church, beyond the Junior Constitutional; torn notice-board.
puzzles.game_idea: Street-scene matching puzzle with facade clues.
puzzles.quote: it was only a few doors from a big white church or somethink of the kind, not long built.

puzzles.name: Extract the buyer's name
puzzles.setup: Agent refuses disclosure.
puzzles.book_solution: Invokes Lord Godalming's name and address.
puzzles.game_idea: Social dialogue puzzle choosing credentials and tone.
puzzles.quote: These words put a different complexion on affairs.

puzzles.name: Get into Piccadilly
puzzles.setup: Unlike Carfax, no walled park.
puzzles.book_solution: Unsolved here; hope for key from agency.
puzzles.game_idea: Stealth/legitimacy puzzle: obtain key legitimately or enter at night unseen.
puzzles.quote: It will be a mighty different thing to commit burglary in Piccadilly, either by day or night.

puzzles.name: Decipher Renfield's behaviour
puzzles.setup: He avoids 'drink', fears souls.
puzzles.book_solution: Seward lists contradictions and deduces the Count visited.
puzzles.game_idea: Deduction board connecting statements to a conclusion.
puzzles.quote: Logically all these things point one way!

puzzles.name: Locked door of the Harkers' room
puzzles.setup: Mina and Jonathan are inside, the door is locked, the Count is within.
puzzles.book_solution: Van Helsing tries the handle, then all throw their shoulders against the door and burst it open.
puzzles.game_idea: Party-coordinated force-the-door timing minigame; each member adds strength before the Count's scene starts.
puzzles.quote: We threw ourselves against it; with a crash it burst open

puzzles.name: Where will the Count go
puzzles.setup: The Count vanishes as vapour at dawn.
puzzles.obstacle: Which lair does he flee to.
puzzles.book_solution: Quincey watches from the lawn and sees a bat rise from Renfield's window and fly west.
puzzles.game_idea: Stakeout puzzle: observe from hiding and read the direction of the flying bat to mark a lair on the map.
puzzles.quote: I expected to see him in some shape go back to Carfax; but he evidently sought some other lair.

puzzles.name: Timing the trephination
puzzles.setup: Renfield is dying; his words may be valuable.
puzzles.obstacle: Locate the spot, relieve pressure before he dies.
puzzles.book_solution: Van Helsing waits only long enough to fix the best spot, then trephines above the ear.
puzzles.game_idea: Surgery minigame: choose the incision spot on a head diagram before a timer runs out.
puzzles.quote: just long enough to fix the best spot for trephining, so that we may most quickly and perfectly remove the blood clot

puzzles.name: Rousing Jonathan from stupor
puzzles.setup: Jonathan is unconscious in a vampiric stupor.
puzzles.book_solution: Van Helsing flicks his face with a cold wet towel.
puzzles.game_idea: Use the right household item to break a status effect on a party member.
puzzles.quote: I must wake him!

puzzles.name: Entering the empty Piccadilly house
puzzles.setup: No key to a house that is legally someone else's.
puzzles.book_solution: Hire a locksmith in daylight, with a titled gentleman present, so the act looks legitimate. Van Helsing recounts the story of the thief who sold a whole house.
puzzles.game_idea: Social-stealth puzzle: pick the time of day, disguise and cover story to get past police and neighbours without alerting.
puzzles.quote: you go take the lock off a hundred empty house in this your London... and no one will interfere.

puzzles.name: Sterilising the boxes
puzzles.setup: Nine earth-boxes in several lairs.
puzzles.obstacle: Open, sanctify and reseal without the Count noticing.
puzzles.book_solution: Open each lid with screwdriver/wrench, lay a piece of Host on the earth and re-screw, leaving boxes looking undisturbed.
puzzles.game_idea: Timed multi-lair crafting-and-action puzzle: carry enough Host for each box.
puzzles.quote: One by one we treated in the same way each of the great boxes, and left them as we had found them to all appearance

puzzles.name: Assigning forces
puzzles.setup: Three lair sites and a house to search.
puzzles.obstacle: Not enough men; Harker wants to guard Mina.
puzzles.book_solution: Split: two to Walworth/Mile End with cabs, three hold Piccadilly.
puzzles.game_idea: Party-assignment planning screen.
puzzles.quote: the two doctors and I should remain there, whilst Lord Godalming and Quincey found the lairs at Walworth and Mile End

puzzles.name: Predict the Count's arrival
puzzles.setup: Telegram says he left Carfax at 12:45 for the south.
puzzles.book_solution: Van Helsing reasons he crossed at slack tide, visited Bermondsey then Mile End, so arrives later; Godalming and Quincey return first.
puzzles.game_idea: Deduction puzzle with a London map, tide table and timeline.
puzzles.quote: he went south from Carfax, that means he went to cross the river, and he could only do so at slack of tide

puzzles.name: Ambush positioning
puzzles.setup: The Count will enter by the hall door with a key.
puzzles.obstacle: Seat the party so he cannot get past.
puzzles.book_solution: Quincey places Van Helsing, Harker and Seward behind the door; Godalming behind and Quincey in front near the window.
puzzles.game_idea: Grid placement puzzle for an ambush.
puzzles.quote: Quincey Morris had always been the one to arrange the plan of action

puzzles.name: Hypnotic reading of the Count's surroundings
puzzles.setup: Mina in trance at sunrise answers questions.
puzzles.obstacle: Interpret sounds into location and vehicle.
puzzles.book_solution: Lapping water, tread overhead, chain, capstan imply a ship weighing anchor.
puzzles.game_idea: Audio-clue puzzle: identify the vessel type from ambient sounds.
puzzles.quote: The sound of men stamping overhead as they run about. There is the creaking of a chain, and the loud tinkle as the check of the capstan falls into the rachet.

puzzles.name: Why did he take the money
puzzles.setup: Count grabs gold as he flees.
puzzles.book_solution: Van Helsing concludes he plans to escape by ship.
puzzles.game_idea: Evidence-board inference quest.
puzzles.quote: Why take that money?

puzzles.name: Find the ship
puzzles.setup: Count believed to have left London by ship at night.
puzzles.obstacle: Dozens of vessels leave the Port of London.
puzzles.book_solution: Deduce Black Sea route, sailing ship, check Lloyd's for one ship leaving with the tide, then interview dockhands.
puzzles.game_idea: Investigation hub: filter shipping list by route, rig and tide time, then question NPCs with bribe options.
puzzles.quote: only one Black-Sea-bound ship go out with the tide.

puzzles.name: Travel schedule
puzzles.setup: Ship takes about three weeks, overland takes three days.
puzzles.obstacle: Arrive at Varna before the ship.
puzzles.book_solution: Subtract two days for supernatural weather, add one day for delays, leave by 17 October latest.
puzzles.game_idea: Logistics puzzle with route and day counter.
puzzles.quote: we must leave here on 17th at latest.

puzzles.name: Keeping Mina from the Count's mind
puzzles.setup: Mina may be compelled to speak what she knows.
puzzles.obstacle: Excluding her from planning without breaking her trust.
puzzles.book_solution: Mina herself asks to be excluded and extracts Jonathan's promise.
puzzles.game_idea: Information-control mechanic: certain NPCs must not receive plan flags.
puzzles.quote: Promise me that you will not tell me anything of the plans formed for the campaign against the Count.

puzzles.name: Sealing the box on the ship
puzzles.setup: Box in the hold of a crewed ship.
puzzles.book_solution: Board, identify box, fasten a wild rose branch, then open when none are near.
puzzles.game_idea: Stealth boarding mission with crew patrols.
puzzles.quote: We shall at the first board that ship; then, when we have identified the box, we shall place a branch of the wild rose on it.

puzzles.name: Reading the ship through Mina's trance
puzzles.setup: The ship is at sea; its position unknown; Mina can only report sounds and sensations at sunrise/sunset.
puzzles.obstacle: Only two short windows per day; information vague.
puzzles.book_solution: Van Helsing hypnotises her and asks what she sees and hears; daily comparison with Lloyd's telegrams.
puzzles.game_idea: Audio-clue puzzle: the player hears Mina's described sounds (waves, creaking, cattle, oars) and must deduce ship state/location on a map.
puzzles.quote: He always asks her what she can see and hear.

puzzles.name: Legal access to the sealed box
puzzles.setup: The box is aboard a foreign ship; shippers and captain may refuse.
puzzles.book_solution: Godalming tells shippers the box may hold stolen property and obtains an authorisation paper.
puzzles.game_idea: Social/dialogue puzzle to pick the cover story that convinces officials, with limited bribe budget.
puzzles.quote: got a half consent that he might open it at his own risk.

puzzles.name: Next train to Galatz
puzzles.setup: Ship has gone to Galatz; party must follow.
puzzles.book_solution: Mina recalls the only train leaves at 6:30 next morning.
puzzles.game_idea: Timetable-planning puzzle: assign errands to party members before the deadline.
puzzles.quote: I am the train fiend.

puzzles.name: The Count's pattern of behaviour
puzzles.setup: Count has vanished to Galatz.
puzzles.book_solution: Mina: as a criminal of habit he returns home and prepares again, as the historical Dracula did across the Danube.
puzzles.game_idea: Deduction board linking document excerpts to predict the next move.
puzzles.quote: Thus, in a difficulty he has to seek resource in habit.

puzzles.name: Trace the box through Galatz
puzzles.setup: Box left the ship before dawn.
puzzles.obstacle: Chain of agents: Captain, Hildesheim, Skinsky.
puzzles.book_solution: Follow receipt to Hildesheim, bribe him, learn of Skinsky, find the body.
puzzles.game_idea: Investigation chain: collect names and addresses by bribery to open each next location; time limit before witnesses close ranks.
puzzles.quote: His arguments were pointed with specie—we doing the punctuation

puzzles.name: Mina's Memorandum by exclusion
puzzles.setup: Count has left Galatz in the box.
puzzles.book_solution: Eliminate road and rail, use trance sounds (cattle, oars, creaking wood, water level with ears) to infer an open boat going upstream on Sereth/Bistritza.
puzzles.game_idea: Deduction puzzle: match sound clues against map features to choose the river route.
puzzles.quote: There would be no such sound if floating down stream.

puzzles.name: Find the boat
puzzles.setup: Many boats on the river.
puzzles.book_solution: Fly the Roumanian flag to be treated as officials and search every boat.
puzzles.game_idea: Boat-inspection mini-game: search cargo of each boat with limited time, use bluff.
puzzles.quote: With every boat which we have over-hauled since then this trick has succeeded

puzzles.name: Rapids
puzzles.setup: Launch tries to force a way up rapids.
puzzles.book_solution: Godalming repairs; local help and rope.
puzzles.game_idea: Engine-repair and rope-haul mini-game.
puzzles.quote: The Slovak boats get up all right, by aid of a rope and steering with knowledge.

puzzles.name: Reading Jonathan's diary as a map
puzzles.setup: Mina must find the unmarked by-road from the Pass.
puzzles.book_solution: Mina recognises the right road from Jonathan's diary; horses are given rein.
puzzles.game_idea: Navigation puzzle: match diary landmark descriptions against terrain at each fork.
puzzles.quote: I see that there be only one such by-road.

puzzles.name: Keep the fire and the circle
puzzles.setup: Night siege by the Brides.
puzzles.obstacle: Fire dying in the cold hour; leaving the ring is fatal.
puzzles.book_solution: Stay within the circle, feed fire from within reach, hold the wafer.
puzzles.game_idea: Survival defence: ration wood and wafer while waves of mist-forms test the ring edges; hold horses calm.
puzzles.quote: Do not go without. Here you are safe!

puzzles.name: Resist the fascination
puzzles.setup: The Brides sleep in tombs.
puzzles.obstacle: Their beauty puts the hunter into a trance.
puzzles.book_solution: Van Helsing hears Mina's wail; avoids looking too long.
puzzles.game_idea: Willpower meter: each second looking costs willpower; use quick actions to proceed.
puzzles.quote: I dared not pause to look on her as I had on her sister

puzzles.name: Find all the tombs
puzzles.setup: The chapel holds many tombs.
puzzles.book_solution: Search every tomb; three Un-Dead matched the three phantoms; Dracula's tomb is empty and gets wafer.
puzzles.game_idea: Chapel search puzzle with three active tombs and one empty lordly tomb.
puzzles.quote: By this time I had searched all the tombs in the chapel

puzzles.name: Seal the castle
puzzles.setup: Doors open.
puzzles.book_solution: Van Helsing breaks the doors off their hinges (the Wafer fixes the entrances).
puzzles.game_idea: Ritual sealing minigame at each entrance.
puzzles.quote: I so fixed its entrances that never more can the Count enter there Un-Dead.

puzzles.name: Reaching the cart before sunset
puzzles.setup: Box on cart racing to the castle.
puzzles.book_solution: Converge from four sides, cover with rifles, break through to the box and pry it open.
puzzles.game_idea: Timed boss approach: sun clock decreases as you cut through gypsy ring.
puzzles.quote: racing for the sunset.

combat.name: Wolf ring in the pass
weapons_used: Harker shouts and beats the calèche side
combat.tactics: Harker is helpless; wolves encircle silently while the driver is away; noise tries to open a gap; the driver ends it by command.
combat.outcome: Wolves retreat at Dracula's gesture.
combat.game_idea: Defensive survival encounter: protect the horses for 3 rounds by making noise/light; panic meter on horses; the ring breaks only when a scripted event triggers.
combat.quote: but the living ring of terror encompassed them on every side

combat.name: Throat grab over the cut
combat.tactics: Harker evades; the crucifix breaks the Count's frenzy.
combat.outcome: Count recovers, destroys the mirror, leaves.
combat.game_idea: Quick-time/turn event: bleeding raises the enemy's frenzy; using the crucifix cancels the attack.
combat.quote: his hand touched the string of beads which held the crucifix

combat.name: Three women vs sleeping Harker
combat.tactics: Harker is passive/entranced; the Count intervenes by force.
combat.outcome: Harker is saved by the Count for his own purposes and faints.
combat.game_idea: Resist-the-charm scenario: each turn a willpower check against enthrallment; the Count appears as a scripted deus ex machina or player must use the crucifix.
combat.quote: I closed my eyes in a languorous ecstasy and waited

combat.name: Shovel attack on the sleeping Count
combat.tactics: Strike while the Count lies in his box; his gaze paralyses Harker and the shovel glances off.
combat.outcome: Only a deep gash above the forehead; lid falls shut.
combat.game_idea: Single-turn boss strike with a 'gaze' save check; ordinary weapons deal tiny damage to Dracula.
combat.quote: the shovel turned in my hand and glanced from the face, merely making a deep gash above the forehead

combat.name: Wolves at the gateway
combat.tactics: The Count calls from the tower; wolves rush the courtyard.
combat.outcome: The woman is killed.
combat.game_idea: Spectator cutscene that teaches wolf-pack mechanics and the Count's summon call.
combat.quote: Before many minutes had passed a pack of them poured ... through the wide entrance into the courtyard.

combat.name: Wolves at the opened door
combat.tactics: Door opens to red jaws; Count stands in the gap.
combat.outcome: Harker shouts to close it.
combat.game_idea: Social/escape encounter: pick the right answer to avoid being fed to the wolves.
combat.quote: their red jaws, with champing teeth, and their blunt-clawed feet as they leaped, came in through the opening door

combat.name: Hypnotic moon-dust
combat.tactics: Mind attack through moonlit dust motes.
combat.outcome: Harker breaks the trance and flees to the lamp-lit room.
combat.game_idea: Resist trance: leave moonlit squares or lose sanity each turn; lamps are safe zones.
combat.quote: I was becoming hypnotised!

combat.name: Mate stabs the stranger
combat.tactics: Mate creeps behind the figure at the bows and stabs.
combat.outcome: Knife passes through It; no damage; mate goes mad.
combat.game_idea: Scripted fail encounter teaching that normal weapons do nothing; unlock crucifix or sacred items to inflict damage.
combat.quote: I crept behind It, and gave It my knife; but the knife went through It, empty as the air.

combat.name: The armed watch
combat.tactics: Go armed and wait for any sign of cause.
combat.outcome: Men keep vanishing; no fight happens.
combat.game_idea: Survival-horror night watch: stand watch in pairs in the fog; choose positions each turn while enemy picks off the weakest crew member.
combat.quote: Mate and I agreed to go armed henceforth and wait for any sign of cause.

combat.name: Mastiff vs the great dog
combat.tactics: Attack in the road near the pier.
combat.outcome: Mastiff killed, throat torn, belly slit.
combat.game_idea: Boss-intro cutscene or a defend-the-pier encounter against a huge dog form.
combat.quote: its throat was torn away, and its belly was slit open as if with a savage claw.

combat.name: Seizing Renfield at Carfax
combat.tactics: Surround and close in after he is distracted at the chapel door.
combat.outcome: Renfield fights like a tiger but is restrained and chained in the padded room.
combat.game_idea: Party non-lethal capture: encircle positions, use Subdue and Restrain actions; Renfield has high strength and an enrage when approached; each turn the surround tightens.
combat.quote: When we closed in on him he fought like a tiger. He is immensely strong.

combat.name: Dark figure at the seat
combat.tactics: Mina calls out; the figure raises its head and then withdraws.
combat.outcome: The figure disappears; Lucy survives with marks.
combat.game_idea: Pursuit and interrupt scene: shout/light/charge to interrupt a feeding; no kill possible yet, only disrupt.
combat.quote: I called in fright, 'Lucy! Lucy!' and something raised a head

combat.name: Restraining Renfield
combat.tactics: Several attendants hold him; he redoubles strength then drops calm when the bat appears.
combat.outcome: Held and returned to the asylum.
combat.game_idea: Non-lethal restraint encounter: reduce his agitation meter by timing grabs while a hidden trigger (the bat) can swing it.
combat.quote: it took all their strength to hold him

combat.name: Renfield's knife attack
combat.tactics: Seward keeps the table between them, Renfield is too quick, Seward punches him down.
combat.outcome: Seward's wrist cut; Renfield secured by attendants.
combat.game_idea: One-on-one encounter with a quick enemy; obstacle (table) grants dodge; ends with a bleeding status effect.
combat.quote: before I could get my balance he had struck at me and cut my left wrist rather severely

combat.name: Wolf at the window
combat.tactics: None; Lucy paralysed.
combat.outcome: Mrs. Westenra dies; Lucy isolated.
combat.game_idea: Scripted defeat or survival scene where the player's ward items decide whether the wolf can enter.
combat.quote: Mother cried out in a fright

combat.name: Renfield vs the carriers and attendants
combat.tactics: Renfield drags a carrier by the neck and batters his head; ignores a blow to the head; throws three men about; subdued when the waistcoat goes on.
combat.outcome: Hardy's finger broken; Renfield returned to the padded room.
combat.game_idea: Boss-like encounter with a damage-resistant enemy; player must apply a restraint item over several turns to end it.
combat.quote: struggled with the three of us, pulling us to and fro as if we were kittens

combat.name: Van Helsing blocks Arthur
combat.tactics: Hurl Arthur away from the kiss.
combat.outcome: Arthur saved; Lucy's rage flickers and she relaxes.
combat.game_idea: Scripted choice scene: protect an ally from a lethal temptation by acting first.
combat.quote: he stood between them like a lion at bay

combat.name: Vigil in Kingstead churchyard
combat.tactics: Split the watch on opposite sides of the churchyard; intercept the white figure that carries a child.
combat.outcome: Child saved, Lucy escapes unseen into her tomb.
combat.game_idea: Stealth encounter with two player-controlled hiders; success = child saved unharmed before dawn.
combat.quote: Suddenly, as I turned round, I thought I saw something like a white streak

combat.name: Confrontation at the tomb door
combat.tactics: Hide behind yews, reveal with lantern, line up before the tomb, hold the crucifix between her and the door; she stands paralysed between crucifix and sealed door.
combat.outcome: She cannot pass or flee; Van Helsing opens the seal and she retreats into the tomb.
combat.game_idea: Turn-based standoff: Lucy has seduce/charm and snarl moves against Arthur; party uses Crucifix (hold), Lantern (reveal), and Host seal (block) to pin her in place. Charm resist test for Arthur.
combat.quote: she remained between the lifted crucifix and the sacred closing of her means of entry

combat.name: The staking of Lucy
combat.tactics: Reveal body by lantern; Arthur places point over heart, Van Helsing reads the prayer, stake is struck on cue; later decapitate and fill mouth with garlic.
combat.outcome: Lucy writhes, screams, stills, regains her peaceful form; coffin soldered shut.
combat.game_idea: Ritual boss encounter with three phases: prayer (party chants, morale bar), strike (timing meter), post-ritual (behead, garlic, solder). Failure to maintain nerve causes Lucy's counter-screams to drain sanity.
combat.quote: Then he struck with all his might.

combat.name: Bat at the window
combat.tactics: Morris slips out and fires at the bat on the sill.
combat.outcome: Missed, bat escapes into the wood; window broken.
combat.game_idea: Single-shot skill check on a fleeing bat sprite; success reveals the form was Dracula's scout.
combat.quote: I went out to have a shot, as I have been doing of late of evenings, whenever I have seen one.

combat.name: Rat swarm in the chapel
combat.tactics: Retreat, open the door, summon dogs, lift them over the threshold to attack.
combat.outcome: Rats vanish; no casualties.
combat.game_idea: Swarm encounter with morale: players must use the dogs as summons; swarm size grows each turn until countered.
combat.quote: They fled before him so fast that before he had shaken the life out of a score, the other dogs, who had by now been lifted in the same manner, had but small prey

combat.name: Renfield versus the mist-Count
combat.tactics: Renfield grabbed the mist tight and held until the Count solidified; he lost when the Count's eyes drained his strength.
combat.outcome: Renfield thrown down and fatally injured; the Count slipped away.
combat.game_idea: Cutscene or tutorial defeat showing the Count's gaze attack and mist escape.
combat.quote: I saw the mist stealing in, and I grabbed it tight.

combat.name: Confrontation in the Harkers' bedroom
combat.tactics: Count springs at the party; Van Helsing holds out the Wafer, the others advance with crucifixes until the Count retreats and becomes vapour.
combat.outcome: Count driven off, Mina left bitten.
combat.game_idea: Boss encounter: he rushes the party, Wafer/crucifix stacking reduces his Menace until he flees as mist; party must protect Mina as a vulnerable ally with an HP bar.
combat.quote: The Count suddenly stopped, just as poor Lucy had done outside the tomb, and cowered back.

combat.name: Ambush at Piccadilly
combat.tactics: Party hidden behind door and window; Count leaps past the first line; Harker blocks the front-room door and slashes; holy symbols repel; Count dives through the window.
combat.outcome: Count escapes unhurt, his coat slit and money spilled.
combat.game_idea: Turn-based ambush: positioning phase then reaction attacks; the Count has a Flee action when Holy Resolve reaches a threshold; kukri strike has a chance to cut through unless he dodges.
combat.quote: A second less and the trenchant blade had shorne through his heart.

combat.name: Planned boarding of the Czarina Catherine
combat.tactics: Board between sunrise and sunset, open the box, behead and stake the Count at once, others suppress interference.
combat.outcome: Not carried out: the ship went to Galatz.
combat.game_idea: Timed stealth-and-execute mission: deal with crew within the daylight timer, then perform the staking and beheading mini-game.
combat.quote: Morris and Godalming and I shall prevent interference, even if we have to use the arms which we shall have ready.

combat.name: Handspike mutiny
combat.tactics: Captain faces down the sailors who tried to throw the box overboard.
combat.outcome: Sailors beaten back; box saved.
combat.game_idea: Optional flashback tutorial: crowd control with a single blunt weapon.
combat.quote: when the last o’ them rose off the deck wi’ his head in his hand

combat.name: Siege of the Holy Circle
combat.tactics: Stay inside ring, keep fire alive, advance with wafer only to repulse; the Brides cannot cross the ring.
combat.outcome: Brides dissolve at dawn; horses dead.
combat.game_idea: Wave-defence puzzle: protect Mina and the ring integrity, manage fire fuel and wafer uses.
combat.quote: They could not approach, me, whilst so armed

combat.name: Staking the three Brides
combat.tactics: Open each tomb, resist fascination, stake, behead.
combat.outcome: Brides turn to dust; wafer in Dracula's tomb.
combat.game_idea: Three sequential mini-bosses in sleep: willpower bar versus time; stake timing minigame.
combat.quote: I could not have endured the horrid screeching as the stake drove home

combat.name: Battle of the cart at sunset
enemy_types: Szgany gypsies with knives and pistols
combat.tactics: Encircle with rifle cover, two fighters rush the cart; break through gypsy ring; pry box open before sunset; behead and pierce heart.
combat.outcome: Count turns to dust; Morris fatally wounded.
combat.game_idea: Party turn-based encounter: Winchester pair suppress (cover), two melee characters push through, sun timer counts rounds; final attack on the box ends fight, Morris suffers a wound.
combat.quote: Jonathan’s impetuosity, and the manifest singleness of his purpose, seemed to overawe those in front of him

crafting.method: Tie hands one over the other to a wheel spoke with the crucifix between hand and wood, knots fastened with teeth.
crafting.purpose: Hold the wheel and hold the vampire at bay.
crafting.quote: Between the inner hand and the wood was a crucifix

crafting.method: Wrap the shawl tight around the neck and fasten with a pin, put shoes on her feet.
crafting.quote: I fastened the shawl at her throat with a big safety-pin

crafting.method: Daub each bare foot with mud using the other foot.
crafting.quote: I daubed my feet with mud, using each foot in turn on the other

crafting.method: Tie the bedroom key to wrist before sleeping.
crafting.purpose: Prevent Lucy from taking the key or leaving.
crafting.quote: the key is tied to my wrist

crafting.method: Wrap in white paper, tie ribbon, melt wax over knot, press ring.
crafting.quote: sealed it over the knot with sealing-wax, and for my seal I used my wedding ring

crafting.method: Braid the flowers into a wreath.
crafting.purpose: Wear round Lucy's neck to keep the visitor away.
crafting.quote: I put him in your window, I make pretty wreath, and hang him round your neck

ingredients: unspecified narcotic from Van Helsing's bag
crafting.method: Mixed and drunk from a glass while the patient is lifted.
crafting.quote: Then he mixed a narcotic

crafting.method: Rub flowers over sashes, door jamb (above, below, each side) and fireplace.
crafting.quote: with the wisp he rubbed all over the jamb of the door

crafting.method: Fill the bath with hot water, place the patient, chafe the limbs, roll in a hot sheet.
crafting.purpose: Restore body heat before a transfusion.
crafting.quote: Fortunately, the kitchen and boiler fires were still alive, and there was no lack of hot water.

crafting.method: Rough wreath placed over the silk handkerchief at the neck.
crafting.quote: was a rough chaplet of the same odorous flowers

crafting.method: Lay garlic over the door clamps and fix a crucifix
crafting.purpose: Keeps Lucy from leaving the tomb
crafting.quote: I had laid over the clamps of those doors garlic

crafting.method: Crumble the wafers fine and work them into the putty with both hands; roll thin strips
crafting.purpose: Seal a tomb door so the Un-Dead cannot enter
crafting.quote: He crumbled the wafer up fine and worked it into the mass between his hands.

ingredients: round wooden stake, 2.5-3 in thick, 3 ft long
crafting.method: Char one end in fire and sharpen to a fine point
crafting.quote: One end of it was hardened by charring in the fire, and was sharpened to a fine point.

crafting.method: Light lamp, heat iron, run solder along the lead seam
crafting.quote: a soldering iron and some plumbing solder, and then a small oil-lamp

crafting.result: Three typed manifold copies of the diary
crafting.method: Play cylinders at slow pace and type from the beginning of the seventh.
crafting.purpose: Evidence set for the whole party
crafting.quote: He accordingly set the phonograph at a slow pace, and I began to typewrite from the beginning of the seventh cylinder.

crafting.method: Unscrew lid, lay Host on soil, screw lid shut.
crafting.purpose: Deny the Count a resting place.
crafting.quote: Taking from his box a piece of the Sacred Wafer he laid it reverently on the earth, and then shutting down the lid began to screw it home

crafting.method: Locksmith fits a key to the lock while holding the door with his knees.
crafting.quote: he held the door partly open, steadying it with his knees, whilst he fitted a key to the lock.

crafting.method: Draw a ring on the ground and pass crumbled wafer over it so no gap remains
crafting.purpose: Protect Mina and Van Helsing at camp and in the rock hollow
crafting.quote: I drew a ring so big for her comfort ... and I broke it fine so that all was well guarded.

crafting.method: Build and replenish through the night
crafting.quote: I light a fire, for we have brought supply of wood with us

crafting.method: Arrange a bed for hypnosis or sleep
crafting.quote: I made a couch with furs

dialogue_samples.speaker: Landlady
dialogue_samples.line: Do you know what day it is?

dialogue_samples.speaker: Dracula (driver)
dialogue_samples.line: You cannot deceive me, my friend; I know too much, and my horses are swift.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Dracula (driver)
dialogue_samples.line: The night is chill, mein Herr, and my master the Count bade me take all care of you.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Passenger
dialogue_samples.line: Look! Isten szek!

dialogue_samples.speaker: Dracula
dialogue_samples.line: Welcome to my house. Come freely. Go safely; and leave something of the happiness you bring!

dialogue_samples.speaker: Dracula
dialogue_samples.line: I pray you, be seated and sup how you please. You will, I trust, excuse me that I do not join you

dialogue_samples.speaker: Dracula
dialogue_samples.line: Take care how you cut yourself. It is more dangerous than you think in this country.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Dracula
dialogue_samples.line: We are in Transylvania; and Transylvania is not England.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Harker
dialogue_samples.line: I fear I am myself the only living soul within the place.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Dracula
dialogue_samples.line: We Szekelys have a right to be proud

dialogue_samples.speaker: Dracula
dialogue_samples.line: Then write now, my young friend. Write to our friend and to any other

dialogue_samples.speaker: Dracula
dialogue_samples.line: should you leave these rooms you will not by any chance go to sleep in any other part of the castle

dialogue_samples.speaker: Vampire woman
dialogue_samples.line: Go on! You are first, and we shall follow

dialogue_samples.speaker: Fair vampire woman
dialogue_samples.line: You yourself never loved; you never love!

dialogue_samples.speaker: Dracula
dialogue_samples.line: I promise you that when I am done with him you shall kiss him at your will.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Dracula
dialogue_samples.line: The first should be June 12, the second June 19, and the third June 29.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Dracula
dialogue_samples.line: Your letters are sacred to me. Your pardon, my friend, that unknowingly I did break the seal.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Woman
dialogue_samples.line: Monster, give me my child!

dialogue_samples.speaker: Dracula
dialogue_samples.line: You English have a saying ... ‘Welcome the coming; speed the parting guest.’

dialogue_samples.speaker: Dracula
dialogue_samples.line: Back, back, to your own place! Your time is not yet come. Wait! Have patience! To-night is mine. To-morrow night is yours!
dialogue_samples.context: To the women outside Harker's door

dialogue_samples.speaker: Harker
dialogue_samples.line: Shut the door; I shall wait till morning!

dialogue_samples.speaker: Quincey P. Morris
dialogue_samples.line: Miss Lucy, I know I ain't good enough to regulate the fixin's of your little shoes, but I guess if you wait till you find a man that is you will go join them seven young women with the lamps when you quit.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Quincey P. Morris
dialogue_samples.line: I'm going to have a pretty lonely walk between this and Kingdom Come. Won't you give me one kiss?

dialogue_samples.speaker: Lucy Westenra
dialogue_samples.line: Yes, there is some one I love, though he has not told me yet that he even loves me.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Arthur Holmwood
dialogue_samples.line: Count me in every time. I bear messages which will make both your ears tingle.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Mr. Swales
dialogue_samples.line: Lord, make me answer cheerful when my call comes!

dialogue_samples.speaker: Renfield
dialogue_samples.line: May I have three days? I shall clear them away.
dialogue_samples.context: Asked to dispose of his flies.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Renfield
dialogue_samples.line: Oh, yes, I would like a cat! I only asked for a kitten lest you should refuse me a cat.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Coastguard
dialogue_samples.line: We'll hear more of her before this time to-morrow.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Mr. Swales
dialogue_samples.line: Look! look! There's something in that wind and in the hoast beyont that sounds, and looks, and tastes, and smells like death.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Old salt
dialogue_samples.line: She must fetch up somewhere, if it was only in hell.
dialogue_samples.context: Watching the schooner speed toward the reef.

dialogue_samples.speaker: First mate
dialogue_samples.line: It is in the hold, perhaps in one of those boxes. I'll unscrew them one by one and see.

dialogue_samples.speaker: First mate
dialogue_samples.line: The sea will save me from Him, and it is all that is left!

dialogue_samples.speaker: Captain
dialogue_samples.line: If we are wrecked, mayhap this bottle may be found, and those who find it may understand.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Mina Murray
dialogue_samples.line: Strangely enough, Lucy did not wake; but she got up twice and dressed herself.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Renfield
dialogue_samples.line: The bride-maidens rejoice the eyes that wait the coming of the bride; but when the bride draweth nigh, then the maidens shine not to the eyes that are filled.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Renfield
dialogue_samples.line: I shall be patient, Master. It is coming—coming—coming!

dialogue_samples.speaker: Lucy Westenra
dialogue_samples.line: I seem to remember that once the West Lighthouse was right under me.
