chapters.narrator: Jonathan Harker (journal kept in shorthand)
chapters.dates: 3 May - 5 May (journey begins 1 May from Munich)
chapters.summary: Jonathan Harker, a young English solicitor, travels east by train through Munich, Vienna, Buda-Pesth and Klausenburgh to Bistritz to meet his client Count Dracula. He notes local food, costumes and Transylvanian superstition after researching the country in the British Museum. At the Golden Krone Hotel in Bistritz he receives a welcome letter from the Count; the landlord and his wife grow frightened at the mention of the Count, and on the eve of St. George's Day the landlady begs him not to go and gives him a crucifix on a rosary. Peasants cross themselves, make the sign against the evil eye and press protective gifts on him as the diligence climbs through the Carpathians to the Borgo Pass. At the pass the Count's black-horsed calèche arrives early, driven by a tall, strong, red-eyed stranger. During the night drive near midnight dogs and wolves howl, blue flames flicker over the ground where the driver stops to pile stones, and a ring of wolves surrounds the carriage until the driver waves them away. The chapter ends as the calèche enters the courtyard of a vast ruined castle.

chapters.narrator: Jonathan Harker (journal, continued)
chapters.summary: Harker is admitted to Castle Dracula by an old white-moustached man in black who proves to be the Count himself, welcoming him with the ritual words 'Enter freely and of your own will'. He is given a fire-lit supper and a bedroom reached through a windowless octagonal room; the Count does not eat. By day Harker finds a gold-served breakfast, no servants, no mirrors, and a library of English books on England. The Count asks him to stay and correct his English, explains the blue flames as marking hidden treasure, and finalises the purchase of Carfax at Purfleet, which Harker describes from his notes; an atlas ringed at London, Exeter and Whitby. On 8 May Harker shaves with a small mirror, cannot see the Count's reflection, is almost attacked when he bleeds, and the Count recoils from the crucifix and throws the mirror into the courtyard. Exploring, Harker finds every door locked, and concludes the castle is a prison.

chapters.narrator: Jonathan Harker (journal, continued)
chapters.summary: Harker panics on realising he is a prisoner, then resolves to keep his fears hidden and his eyes open. He watches the Count make his bed and lay the table, and so deduces there are no servants and that the Count himself drove the calèche. The Count talks proudly of the Szekely and Dracula bloodline and its wars. On 12 May he questions Harker about business law and shipping through multiple solicitors, then makes him write letters saying he will stay a month, and warns him never to sleep outside his own rooms. Harker reads the sealed letters' addresses (Billington in Whitby, Leutner in Varna, Coutts & Co., Klopstock & Billreuth). That night he sees the Count crawl head-down down the castle wall like a lizard. On 15 May Harker forces a sagging door in the south wing, finds the old ladies' rooms, and, ignoring the warning, falls asleep there. He is visited by three vampire women; the fair one is about to bite his throat when the Count appears in fury, hurls her back and claims Harker as his own, then gives them a moving bag containing a child.

chapters.narrator: Jonathan Harker (journal, continued)
chapters.summary: Harker wakes in his own bed, unsure whether the three women were a dream, and finds the south-wing door jammed shut from inside. The Count forces him to write three post-dated letters (12, 19 and 29 June) announcing his departure, which Harker understands to mark the span of his life. A band of Szgany camps in the courtyard and Harker throws letters and a gold piece through his window bars, but they give them to the Count, who burns the one to Mina and takes Harker's papers, clothes and letter of credit. Slovaks deliver empty boxes, and the Count, wearing Harker's clothes, leaves by the wall, once returning with the bag; a mother who cries 'Monster, give me my child!' is killed by wolves summoned by the Count. Harker climbs to the Count's room, finds a hoard of gold, descends to the ruined chapel where fifty earth-boxes lie and finds the Count lying in one, apparently dead. On 29 June the Count pretends to free him, opens the door onto wolves, and Harker begs him to shut it. On 30 June the door is locked again; he finds the Count gorged with blood in the box, strikes him with a shovel and only gashes his forehead, then is trapped as the Szgany and Slovaks nail the box and leave, with Harker alone in the castle with the three women. He resolves to climb down the wall or die.

chapters.narrator: Mina Murray (letter), Lucy Westenra (letters), Dr. John Seward (phonograph diary), Quincey P. Morris (letter), Arthur Holmwood (telegram)
chapters.summary: Mina writes to Lucy from her work as assistant schoolmistress, practising shorthand and typewriting so she can help Jonathan, and teases Lucy about a rumoured tall curly-haired man. Lucy replies from 17 Chatham Street that it is Mr. Holmwood, and confesses she loves him; she also describes Dr. Seward, young head of a huge lunatic asylum. On 24 May Lucy receives three proposals in one day: Dr. Seward is refused gently, Quincey P. Morris of Texas is refused with great good humour and friendship, and Arthur Holmwood is accepted. On 25 May Seward, heartbroken, turns to work and begins a phonograph case-study of his patient R. M. Renfield, a strong, morbidly excitable man of 59. Quincey invites Arthur to a camp-fire dinner with Seward at the Korea the next night, and Arthur accepts by telegram. The chapter is a quiet, social interlude that introduces the future party of vampire hunters and the first hint of Renfield's danger.

chapters.narrator: Mina Murray (journal) and Dr. John Seward (phonograph diary)
chapters.dates: Mina: 24 July - 6 August; Seward: 5 June - 20 July
chapters.summary: Mina arrives at Whitby on 24 July, is met by Lucy, and describes the town, the Esk valley, the ruined abbey, the steep churchyard on the cliff and the harbour with its two lighthouses and bell-buoy. She befriends Mr. Swales, an ancient sceptical sailor who mocks tombstones and legends, notably the suicide's grave of George Canon on which Lucy's favourite seat rests. Interleaved, Seward's diary tracks Renfield's escalating chain of pets (flies, spiders, sparrows, a requested kitten), culminating in Renfield eating his birds raw; Seward diagnoses a zoophagous (life-eating) maniac. Mina worries as Jonathan sends only a one-line letter from Castle Dracula and then goes silent, while Lucy resumes sleepwalking and Mina locks the bedroom door each night. On 6 August a grey, ominous storm builds; Swales, gentle and shaken, speaks of death in the wind, and a coastguard watches a strange Russian ship that is steered erratically.

chapters.narrator: Newspaper correspondent of The Dailygraph (pasted in Mina's journal); the captain of the Demeter (log); Mina Murray (journal)
chapters.dates: Log 6 July - 4 August; storm 6-7 August night; cutting 8-9 August; Mina 8 and 10 August
chapters.summary: A newspaper cutting describes a sudden, ferocious storm at Whitby after a beautiful day, ending with a Russian schooner, lashed to its helm by a dead man, driving into the harbour and grounding on Tate Hill Pier, from which an immense dog leaps ashore and vanishes. The ship is the Demeter of Varna, in ballast of silver sand with fifty-style great wooden boxes of mould consigned to solicitor Mr. S. F. Billington; a mastiff is found torn to pieces near the pier. The captain's log, recovered from a corked bottle, records a voyage from Varna in which crew vanish one by one, a tall thin pale stranger is glimpsed, the mate's knife passes through it, the mate opens a box and then leaps overboard, and the captain lashes himself to the wheel with a crucifix. The verdict is open and the captain is honoured with a grand funeral. Mina's journal records Lucy sleepwalking during the storm, the funeral, Mr. Swales found dead on the seat with a broken neck and terror on his face, and a dog that rages and then cowers on the suicide's tombstone.

chapters.narrator: Mina Murray (journal), Dr. John Seward (phonograph diary), with letters from Billington & Son, Carter Paterson & Co. and Sister Agatha
chapters.summary: After a long walk to Robin Hood's Bay, Mina wakes at 3 a.m. on 11 August to find Lucy gone and runs through Whitby to the East Cliff churchyard, where she glimpses a long dark figure with red gleaming eyes bending over Lucy on their seat; she finds Lucy alone, asleep and gasping, and fastens a shawl at her throat with a safety-pin, leaving two small puncture marks. Over the next days Lucy sleepwalks, sees a bat at the window, murmurs 'His red eyes again' at sunset, and grows pale and weak while two white-edged red marks fail to heal. Mrs. Westenra confides she has weeks to live from her heart. Billington's letters show the fifty earth boxes sent by rail to Carfax, near Purfleet, and delivered to the ruined chapel. Sister Agatha's letter reveals Jonathan survives in a Buda-Pesth hospital with brain fever, and Mina leaves to join him. In Seward's diary Renfield calls out for 'the Master', escapes through his window at night, climbs the wall into Carfax, begs at the ironbound oak chapel door, and is subdued and restrained in a strait-waistcoat in the padded room.

chapters.narrator: Mina Harker (letter), Lucy Westenra (letter and diary), Dr. John Seward (diary and letters), Arthur Holmwood (letter), Van Helsing (letter); telegrams
chapters.summary: Mina reaches Buda-Pesth, finds Jonathan thin and wrecked after brain fever, and marries him at the hospital after he hands her his sealed-away notebook; she wraps it in white paper, ties it with pale blue ribbon and seals it with her wedding ring. Lucy writes cheerfully from Whitby on 30 August, then from Hillingham her sleepwalking and nightmares return, with scratching or flapping at the window, pallor and a sore throat. In London, Seward watches Renfield, who is calm from moonrise to sunrise, escapes twice to the old chapel door of the deserted house (Carfax), and goes quiet when a purposeful big bat flies west. Arthur asks Seward to examine Lucy; Seward finds her blood normal and sends for Van Helsing. Van Helsing examines Lucy, finds no functional cause and goes home to think. Renfield has paroxysms at noon and sunset, drops his fly-collecting abruptly, and says he has been deserted. On 6 September Seward telegraphs Van Helsing that Lucy has suddenly worsened.

chapters.narrator: Dr. Seward (letter and diary), Lucy Westenra (diary)
chapters.summary: Seward meets Van Helsing at Liverpool Street and they go to Hillingham, where they find Lucy near death from lack of blood. Arthur arrives unexpectedly and gives blood in a direct transfusion after Lucy is given a narcotic; Lucy revives. Van Helsing glimpses two punctures over her external jugular vein when her velvet throat-band slips, and goes to Amsterdam while Seward keeps watch; Lucy sleeps peacefully. On 9 September Seward falls asleep on the sofa, and by morning Lucy is drained again; Seward gives a second transfusion with a morphia injection. Van Helsing forbids telling Arthur and takes over the nightwatch. On 11 September a parcel of garlic flowers from Haarlem arrives: Van Helsing rubs garlic on the windows, door jamb and fireplace, latches the windows and makes a garlic wreath for Lucy's neck, forbidding her to open the window or door.

chapters.narrator: Lucy Westenra (diary and memorandum), Dr. Seward (diary), Pall Mall Gazette reporter (interview); telegram from Van Helsing
chapters.summary: Lucy sleeps peacefully with the garlic. On 13 September Mrs. Westenra, thinking the smell harmful, has removed the garlic and opened the window; Lucy is again drained, Van Helsing breaks down in despair, locks the door and transfuses her himself, then forbids anyone to move the flowers. Lucy enjoys four peaceful nights and a box of garlic arrives daily from Haarlem. The Pall Mall Gazette interviews zoo keeper Thomas Bilder: the wolf Bersicker escaped after a tall thin man with a hooked nose, pointed beard, red eyes and sharp teeth visited and stroked him; Bersicker returns by himself with cut head and broken glass. On 17 September Renfield bursts into Seward's study with a dinner-knife, cuts his wrist and licks the blood, shouting that the blood is the life. Van Helsing's telegram, misdirected to Carfax, Sussex, arrives 22 hours late. That night a wolf smashes Lucy's window, her mother tears off the garlic wreath and dies of fright, a cloud of specks blows in, the maids are drugged with laudanum in sherry, and Lucy is left alone with the dead.

chapters.narrator: Dr. Seward (diary), Mina Harker (letters), Dr. Patrick Hennessey (report)
chapters.summary: Seward and Van Helsing arrive at Hillingham to find the house locked; they saw through the iron bars of a kitchen window, find the four maids drugged and Lucy and her dead mother in bed, Lucy barely alive. They revive her in a hot bath, and Quincey Morris, arriving by chance on Arthur's telegram, supplies blood for a fourth transfusion. A paper from Lucy's breast puzzles Seward, and Van Helsing keeps it. Seward registers Mrs. Westenra's death from heart disease. Quincey tells of a vampire bat that killed his mare on the Pampas. On 19 September Lucy fades; Arthur arrives at sunset. Mina's unopened letters describe Hawkins's bequest and death; Hennessey's report tells of Renfield attacking the carriers who delivered great wooden boxes to the empty house (Carfax), crying that he will fight for his Lord and Master. On the night of 20 September Lucy's wounds vanish, her teeth look longer, she tears at the garlic while asleep and clutches it while awake. She dies; just before, in a voluptuous voice she asks Arthur to kiss her, and Van Helsing hurls him back. Her last words commend Arthur to Van Helsing. Van Helsing says: 'It is only the beginning!'

chapters.narrator: Dr. Seward (diary); Mina Harker (journal); newspaper (The Westminster Gazette)
chapters.dates: c. 20-21 September (funeral eve) - 22 September; Westminster Gazette 25 September
chapters.summary: Lucy and her mother are prepared for burial at the Westenra house. Van Helsing secretly searches Lucy's papers, places wild garlic and a golden crucifix on her corpse, and tells Seward he wants to cut off her head and remove her heart; the crucifix is stolen overnight by a maid and recovered by Van Helsing. The solicitor Mr. Marquand reveals the estate goes to Arthur Holmwood, and Arthur says a grieving goodbye and grants Van Helsing permission to keep Lucy's papers. After the double funeral Van Helsing has a fit of laughing and weeping in the carriage and Seward writes 'FINIS'. Meanwhile Mina and Jonathan attend Mr. Hawkins's funeral at Exeter, then in Piccadilly Jonathan sees a rejuvenated Count Dracula admiring a girl outside Guiliano's; he faints into sleep and forgets, and Mina receives Van Helsing's telegram about the deaths. The chapter closes with two Westminster Gazette items about children on Hampstead Heath lured by a 'bloofer lady' and found with small throat wounds.

chapters.narrator: Mina Harker (journal); letters; Jonathan Harker (journal); Dr. Seward (diary)
chapters.summary: Mina reads Jonathan's Transylvanian journal and decides to type it out. Van Helsing writes to her in confidence and visits Exeter on 25 September; she hands him her typed journal on Lucy and then Jonathan's journal. He declares that Jonathan's story is true. Jonathan returns, meets Van Helsing at the hotel on the 26th, learns the diary was real and is cured of his doubt, and agrees to help against the Count. At the station Van Helsing sees the Westminster Gazette and is shocked. Back in London he shows Seward the Hampstead story, gives a long lecture on unexplained natural wonders and open-minded belief, and ends the chapter by revealing that the children's wounds were made by Miss Lucy.

chapters.narrator: Dr. Seward (diary); Van Helsing (note)
chapters.summary: Seward angrily rejects Van Helsing's claim, but they visit the injured child at North Hospital under Dr. Vincent, dine at Jack Straw's Castle and at night enter the Westenra tomb at Kingstead. Van Helsing cuts open Lucy's lead coffin with a turnscrew and fret-saw and shows it empty. They watch the churchyard; a white figure appears and Van Helsing recovers an unharmed child. The next afternoon Lucy lies in her coffin, redder and more beautiful, with sharper teeth; Van Helsing explains she is Un-Dead and must be beheaded, mouthed with garlic and staked, but delays to fetch Arthur. He leaves a note for Seward with instructions, and spends the night sealing the tomb with garlic and a crucifix. Seward doubts again, then on 29 September Van Helsing persuades Arthur and Quincey to join him.

chapters.narrator: Dr. Seward (diary)
chapters.summary: At a quarter before midnight the four men enter the Kingstead churchyard and Van Helsing shows Arthur and Quincey the empty coffin. Outside, Van Helsing seals the tomb door with crumbled Host mixed into putty; they hide as Lucy, the 'Bloofer Lady', approaches carrying a child, her mouth bloody. She tries to lure Arthur ('Come to me'), is repelled by the golden crucifix, and cannot enter the sealed tomb until Van Helsing removes the Host and she slips in through the crack. The next night, after the funeral and the sexton's locking-up, Van Helsing prepares the tomb with a soldering iron, solder, oil lamp, operating knives, a charred stake and a hammer. He explains the curse of the Un-Dead; Arthur drives the stake through Lucy while Van Helsing reads from the missal. She turns back into her peaceful self, the stake is sawed, the head cut off, the mouth filled with garlic and the lead coffin soldered shut. The party vows to hunt the author of the sorrow; Van Helsing leaves for Amsterdam.

chapters.narrator: Dr. Seward (phonograph diary), Mina Harker (journal), Jonathan Harker (journal)
chapters.summary: Van Helsing receives Mina's telegram at the Berkeley Hotel, hands Seward the Harker diaries and departs for Whitby. Seward meets Mina at Paddington and brings her to the asylum at Purfleet. Mina learns of the phonograph diary, wins Seward's trust by showing him her typescripts, and spends the night typing out the cylinders about Lucy's death in three manifold copies. Jonathan, back from Whitby and London, has traced the fifty earth boxes from the Demeter through Whitby, King's Cross and Carter Paterson to Carfax chapel. Seward realises the Count's lair is the house next door and that Renfield has been an index of the Count's presence; Renfield is suspiciously calm. Lord Godalming and Quincey Morris arrive and Mina consoles each in turn, forging a bond of 'sister' and 'little girl'.

chapters.narrator: Dr. Seward and Mina Harker
chapters.summary: Mina meets Renfield, who tidies by eating flies and spiders, then speaks as a polished philosopher, urging her to leave and later blessing her. Van Helsing arrives and agrees that Mina must be removed from further danger. At nine o'clock the party forms a committee: Van Helsing lectures on the vampire's powers, weaknesses and the Dracula history from Arminius, and all pledge their hands over his golden crucifix. Morris fires at a bat on the windowsill, shattering the window pane. Plans: trace and sterilise the earth boxes and catch the Count between noon and sunset. Mina is excluded henceforth. As the men prepare to go to Carfax, Renfield begs frantically to be released that night, but Seward refuses.

chapters.narrator: Jonathan Harker, Dr. Seward, Mina Harker
chapters.summary: After Renfield's scene the party goes to Carfax at dawn. Godalming brings a silver dog whistle; Van Helsing equips each man with a silver crucifix, garlic wreath, revolver, knife, electric lamp and a piece of Sacred Wafer. Seward picks the lock with skeleton keys. In the chapel only twenty-nine of fifty earth boxes remain; the vault is thick with a foul odour and swarms with thousands of rats, which Godalming's three terriers drive off once carried over the threshold. The party finds nothing else and locks up. Van Helsing notes the Count's animals fear dogs. Twenty-one boxes are now accounted for as removed. Van Helsing is rebuffed by Renfield. Mina, kept in the dark, dreams of mist pouring in with red eyes and a livid face, and on 2 October takes a mild sleeping draught from Seward.

chapters.narrator: Jonathan Harker and Dr. Seward
chapters.summary: Jonathan tracks the carriers: Thomas Snelling is drunk, but his boss Joseph Smollet gives destinations from a dog-eared notebook: six boxes to 197 Chicksand Street, Mile End New Town, and six to Jamaica Lane, Bermondsey, plus a tip about Sam Bloxam. Next day Jonathan decodes a phonetically spelled address, chases Bloxam through Walworth and Poplar to a cold storage building at Cross Angel Street, and learns nine boxes were carried to an empty house in Piccadilly by an old man with a white moustache of unnatural strength. He finds the house, learns from grooms and then Mitchell, Sons & Candy that the buyer is Count de Ville, who paid cash. Seward studies Renfield's talk of souls and life and deduces that the Count has visited him. The party plans to sterilise all earth between sunrise and sunset and prepares horses. Renfield is found lying in blood after a yell.

chapters.narrator: Dr. John Seward (diary), recounting Renfield's dying testimony and Mina's account
chapters.summary: Seward finds Renfield on the floor of his cell in a pool of blood with a broken back and a depressed skull fracture. Van Helsing trephines the skull above the ear, and Renfield briefly regains clarity. He confesses that the Count tempted him with flies, moths and a swarm of rats, that he invited the Count in, and that he then fought the Count bare-handed after realising Mrs. Harker was being drained. The Count threw him down and broke him. The party arms itself with crucifixes and Sacred Wafer, breaks down the Harkers' locked door and finds the Count forcing Mina to drink blood from his torn breast while Jonathan lies in a vampiric stupor. The Wafer and crucifixes drive the Count back and he dissolves into mist under the door. Downstairs the Count has burned Seward's manuscript and phonograph cylinders and killed Renfield; Quincey saw a bat fly west from Renfield's window. Mina tells her story at dawn: the Count's threat, the bite, and the forced blood drinking that binds her to his call.

chapters.narrator: Jonathan Harker (journal)
chapters.summary: Harker records the morning after the attack. Renfield's death is to be certified as misadventure. The party resolves to keep nothing from Mina, who swears to live though she resolves to die if she endangers others. Van Helsing lays out the day's plan: the Count is bound to his material form until sunset, so the party will sterilise his earth-boxes at Carfax, then search the Piccadilly house, while Godalming and Quincey destroy the boxes at Bermondsey and Mile End. Before they leave, Van Helsing touches a piece of Sacred Wafer to Mina's forehead and it sears a red scar into her flesh. They swear a pledge, sterilise all boxes at Carfax by placing Host on the earth, then reach Piccadilly where a locksmith is hired and the door opened. Eight of nine boxes are found in the dining-room and sanctified. Title deeds, keys and toiletries are found, and Godalming and Quincey leave with the keys.

chapters.narrator: Dr. Seward (diary), then Jonathan Harker (journal)
chapters.summary: Waiting at Piccadilly, Van Helsing explains the Count's history and his experiments in moving his own boxes. A telegram from Mina warns that the Count has hurried south from Carfax. Godalming and Quincey return, having destroyed twelve boxes at Bermondsey and Mile End. They ambush the Count when he enters with a key; Harker slashes at him with his kukri, cutting his coat and spilling banknotes and gold; the Count is repelled by crucifix and Wafer and leaps through the window. He escapes via the stable, leaving a sneering threat. Van Helsing burns his remaining effects and keeps the deeds. Back at the asylum Mina asks the men to pity the Count. During the night Mina asks Van Helsing to hypnotise her before dawn, and in trance she hears water, a chain and a capstan, revealing the Count is aboard a ship. Van Helsing deduces escape and warns that, because of the mark, time favours the immortal Count.

chapters.narrator: Van Helsing (phonograph), Jonathan Harker, Mina Harker, Dr. Seward
chapters.summary: Van Helsing records a message for Harker: the Count has fled to Transylvania by ship. The party consults Lloyd's and finds the sailing ship Czarina Catherine, which left Doolittle's Wharf for Varna. Dockhands describe the pale man in black and straw hat who loaded a large box and called fog up around the ship. Van Helsing explains the Count's persistence and why pursuit is necessary. Mina sees her own forehead scar in a mirror and knows she is still unclean. Seward and Van Helsing realise Mina is changing and may be mentally linked to the Count, so she is excluded from councils. They plan to leave for Varna by 17 October at latest, adding Winchesters. Mina makes Jonathan promise not to tell her the plans, then reveals at dawn on 6 October that she must go along because the Count will summon her. Van Helsing decides to put a wild-rose branch on the box aboard the ship. Harker makes his will; sunset approaches and Mina calls him.

chapters.narrator: Dr. Seward (diary), Jonathan Harker (journal), Dr. Seward again
chapters.summary: On the eve of departure Mina asks her friends to swear to kill her (stake and beheading) if she turns vampire, and asks Jonathan to read the Burial Service over her; all swear. The party travels London - Paris - Orient Express to Varna and waits at the hotel Odessus for the Czarina Catherine, with Mina hypnotised by Van Helsing at every sunrise and sunset to report what the Count's earth-box senses (lapping water, creaking masts). Lord Godalming arranges the shipper's and agent's permission to open the box, and the plan is set: behead and stake the Count at once, others cover with arms. A telegram from Lloyd's reports the ship at the Dardanelles, then, after days of delay, entering Galatz instead of Varna. Mina, the 'train fiend', knows the only train leaves at 6:30 next morning. Van Helsing privately realises the Count has cut Mina off by trance and that Mina's own link, now free of his will, can be turned against him. Mina's criminal-psychology deduction: the Count always repeats the pattern of retreating home then returning better equipped.

chapters.narrator: Dr. Seward, Mina Harker, Jonathan Harker (diaries)
chapters.summary: On the train from Varna to Galatz Mina's trances grow harder; she reports a still ship, oars, a gun, and then 'something going out' with wolves and falling water. At Galatz the party boards the Czarina Catherine and Captain Donelson tells of the unnaturally fast fog-wrapped voyage, his Roumanian sailors' fear of the box and the handspike argument. They trace the box through Immanuel Hildesheim to the Slovak agent Petrof Skinsky, who is found dead with a torn throat in St. Peter's churchyard. Mina, studying the typescripts and maps, writes a Memorandum deducing the Count must travel upriver by an open boat on the Sereth then Bistritza toward the Borgo Pass. The party splits: Godalming and Jonathan by steam launch, Seward and Morris on horseback along the bank, Van Helsing and Mina by train and carriage to the Borgo Pass and the castle. Diaries record the chase, the launch accident at the rapids, snow threatening, and Mina's trance power fading.

chapters.narrator: Mina Harker, Van Helsing (memorandum), Jonathan Harker, Dr. Seward
chapters.summary: Van Helsing and Mina drive up to the Borgo Pass changing horses daily while Mina's trances fade into drowsiness and she begins to behave oddly (eats alone, sleeps all day, looks redder and healthier). At the Pass she knows the road from Jonathan's diary. Near the castle Van Helsing draws a holy circle with crumbled Host wafer; Mina cannot leave it, and the three Brides appear in snow and mist begging her to come to them but cannot cross. The horses die. Next day Van Helsing enters the ruined castle with a blacksmith's hammer, finds the three Brides in their tombs, fights the fascination, stakes and beheads them, and lays wafer in Dracula's empty tomb, then seals the doors. Meanwhile Harker and Godalming, and Seward and Morris, converge on a gypsy party racing a leiter-wagon with the box toward the castle at sunset. In a pitched fight Jonathan's kukri slashes the Count's throat and Morris's bowie pierces the heart; Dracula crumbles to dust. Morris, stabbed, dies blessing Mina whose scar has vanished.

chapters.narrator: Jonathan Harker
chapters.summary: Epilogue Note. Seven years on, the survivors are happily settled; Mina and Jonathan's son is called Quincey after Quincey Morris, born on the day he died. They revisit Transylvania: every trace is gone, the castle stands in desolation. The record is almost all typescript, no authentic proof; Van Helsing says 'We want no proofs'.
